title: Heart-failure acute decompensation
description: ESC 2023 focused update + WHO PEN-HEARTS. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedHeartFailureDecompensation. Tier 1 CRITICAL — cardiogenic shock / acute pulmonary oedema (SBP <90 OR hypoperfusion signs OR SpO2 <90 OR RR >=30 OR pink frothy sputum): sit upright, high-flow O2 to SpO2 94–98%, CPAP / NIV for pulmonary oedema with respiratory distress, IV furosemide bolus 40–80 mg (or 2.5x usual oral dose) repeated 2–4 h, IV nitrate if SBP >110 (AVOID in known RV infarct), noradrenaline 0.05–0.5 µg/kg/min for shock, dobutamine 2.5–10 µg/kg/min for contractility, urgent ECG / troponin / CXR / ABG / point-of-care echo, ICU referral. Tier 2 CRITICAL — concerning decompensation (orthopnoea / PND, bilateral basal crackles, weight gain >=2 kg/3 d, raised JVP): admit, IV furosemide, salt + fluid restriction, investigate precipitant, optimise GDMT (LVEF-banded: HFrEF four pillars including SGLT2i; HFpEF volume control + SGLT2i; potassium >=5.5 holds ACE/MRA). Tier 3 WARNING — early decompensation (mild oedema or sub-2 kg weight gain): outpatient loop-diuretic step-up by 50% for 3 days, daily weights, yellow / red zone plan, review in 3–7 days. Tier 4 INFO — no decompensation: reinforce self-management, vaccinate.

Critical when HCV active (anti-HCV positive with HCV RNA detectable or RNA-positive standalone) — pan-genotypic DAA sofosbuvir-velpatasvir 12 weeks (cure >95%), stage fibrosis, SVR12 at week 12 post-treatment. Critical when pregnant + HBsAg unknown — universal antenatal HBsAg testing + infant birth-dose HBV vaccine within 24 h. Warning when high-risk + never tested (PLHIV, key populations, transfusion pre-screening era, healthcare-worker sharps, household contact, dialysis). Info routine one-time offer for adults in endemic setting.

title: Gestational diabetes — screen, diagnose, manage
description: WHO 2013 hyperglycaemia-in-pregnancy criteria + IADPSG + FIGO 2015 + Kenya MoH National Maternal Health Guidelines. Critical for overt diabetes in pregnancy (FPG >=7.0 OR random >=11.1 OR HbA1c >=6.5%): manage as type-2 diabetes — insulin, retinal + renal screen, aspirin 75–150 mg from week 12, combined obstetric + diabetes clinic, plan delivery 39–40 weeks. Critical for GDM by 75 g OGTT (fasting >=5.1 OR 1-h >=10.0 OR 2-h >=8.5 mmol/L): medical nutrition therapy + activity, SMBG 4 x/day targets fasting <5.3 and 1-h post-prandial <7.8, escalate to metformin then insulin if >=20% readings above target; aspirin from week 12; foetal-growth ultrasound 28–32 w; postnatal OGTT 6–12 w. Warning for risk factors (previous GDM, macrosomic infant, BMI >=30, FH diabetes, age >=35, PCOS, glycosuria, polyhydramnios) + 24–28 weeks reached without OGTT. Info universal-offer reminder for routine OGTT at 24–28 weeks in endemic regions (>=10% hyperglycaemia-in-pregnancy prevalence).

title: Status epilepticus / seizure management
description: WHO mhGAP 2.0 epilepsy / convulsive disorders module + ILAE 2015 operational definition + Kenya MoH Acute Care. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedSeizure. Critical when active convulsion >=5 min OR recurrent without recovery of consciousness — ABCDE, glucose (50 mL 50% dextrose or 2 mL/kg 10% dextrose if <3 mmol/L; thiamine 100 mg IV in alcohol use), Stage 1 (0–5 min) lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg) OR IM midazolam 10 mg (5 mg if 13–40 kg), repeat once at 10 min if still convulsing; Stage 2 (10–30 min) phenytoin 20 mg/kg IV at <=50 mg/min with cardiac monitoring OR sodium valproate 40 mg/kg IV OR levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV; Stage 3 (>30 min refractory) intubate + midazolam infusion or thiopentone. Critical override for active seizure in pregnancy — eclampsia management: magnesium sulphate loading 4 g IV + 10 g IM, maintenance 5 g IM 4-hourly x 24 h; labetalol / hydralazine if BP >=160/110; urgent delivery. Critical for post-ictal hypoglycaemia (capillary <3 mmol/L) — dextrose now. Warning for first-ever seizure post-ictal — investigate (glucose, U&E, Ca, Mg, malaria, HIV, ECG, urgent CT if focal signs / age >40 / HIV+ / head injury), do not start AED reflexively. Info for break-through seizure in known epilepsy — assess adherence + triggers + AED dose review.

title: IMCI: measles in children under 5
description: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet 2014 + WHO Measles Treatment Recommendations 2020 + Kenya MoH EPI. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedMeasles AND ageMonths < 60. Critical for severe complicated measles: any IMCI general danger sign, corneal clouding (sight-threatening), deep / extensive mouth ulcers, severe pneumonia, severe dehydration, encephalitis (seizures or altered mental state), stridor in calm child — admit; vitamin A age-banded (50 000 IU < 6 m / 100 000 IU 6–11 m / 200 000 IU >= 12 m, today and tomorrow); tetracycline 1% eye ointment + urgent ophthalmology for corneal clouding; ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg IM/IV for severe pneumonia / encephalitis; manage seizures with diazepam PR / midazolam buccal; ORS / IV fluids; respiratory isolation; immunise non-immune contacts within 72 h. Critical for measles with eye / mouth / non-severe pneumonia — outpatient bundle: vitamin A, amoxicillin DT 25 mg/kg BD x 5 d for non-severe pneumonia, tetracycline eye ointment, GV paint or salicylate gel for mouth ulcers, soft feeds. Warning for uncomplicated measles — vitamin A, paracetamol, isolate 4 days post-rash, contact tracing. Info for prodrome with Koplik spots or known contact in last 21 days — vitamin A + isolation + review at 48 h.

title: PMTCT — Prevention of mother-to-child HIV transmission
description: WHO 2021 consolidated HIV prevention / treatment guidelines + Kenya NASCOP PMTCT Algorithm 2022. Critical when HIV-positive pregnant or breastfeeding AND not on ART — start tenofovir + lamivudine + dolutegravir (TLD) same day, baseline VL / creatinine / CD4 / HBsAg / syphilis, intensive adherence counselling, plan infant prophylaxis (dual NVP + AZT for high-risk maternal profile, NVP-only for lower risk). Critical when on ART but VL >= 1000 copies/mL — repeat VL after enhanced-adherence package (3 sessions / 4–8 weeks), drug-resistance testing where available, switch to TLD if on NNRTI-based regimen, dual infant prophylaxis 12 weeks. Critical when maternal HIV status unknown — provider-initiated HIV testing today + same-day TLD if positive; offer PrEP if negative with ongoing risk. Critical when HIV-exposed infant not yet on prophylaxis — start age-banded NVP today (15 mg birth–6 w, 20 mg 6 w–6 m), add AZT for high-risk profile, cotrimoxazole from 6 weeks. Warning when virally suppressed — continue TLD, trimester VL + 6-week post-partum VL + 6-monthly thereafter, infant NVP 6 weeks, EID PCR at 6 w / 6 m / 12 m, final antibody 18 m or 6 weeks after breastfeeding stops, exclusive-feeding counselling. Warning for HIV-negative with serodiscordant partner / ongoing exposure — offer PrEP (TDF/FTC), 3-monthly retesting.

references.label: WHO — Consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery and monitoring (2021)
Kenya NASCOP — PMTCT Algorithm (2022)

title: Postpartum care — WHO 4-contact schedule + red flags
description: WHO 2022 recommendations on maternal and newborn care for a positive postnatal experience + Kenya MoH Postnatal Care Guidelines. WHO mandates four PNC contacts in the first 6 weeks: < 24 h, day 3 (48–72 h), day 7–14, week 6. Critical for any red flag any time in the first 6 weeks: heavy bleeding / PPH (uterine massage + oxytocin 10 IU bolus + 20 IU/L infusion + TXA 1 g IV within 3 h + balloon tamponade if atony persists), fever >= 38 (puerperal sepsis — cultures + ampicillin + gentamicin + metronidazole within 1 h), foul lochia (endometritis), postpartum severe-range hypertension >=160/110 OR severe headache / visual disturbance (postpartum pre-eclampsia / eclampsia — MgSO4 4 g IV + 10 g IM, labetalol or hydralazine), calf pain / swelling (DVT — LMWH), dyspnoea (PE / cardiac), breast abscess + systemic features (incision + drainage + antibiotics), suicidal thoughts (mental-health crisis pathway). Warning when first / day-3 / day-7–14 contact overdue. Warning for postpartum anaemia (Hb < 9 g/dL) — ferrous sulphate 200 mg TDS + folic acid 5 mg daily for >=3 months, workup malaria / hookworm / HIV. Warning for EPDS >=13 — perinatal mental-health pathway (psychological therapy first; sertraline 50–100 mg daily if moderate-severe and safe in breastfeeding). Info for routine week-6 contact — contraception, infant immunisations (DTP-HepB-Hib-1, PCV-1, OPV-1, rotavirus-1, IPV-1), cervical-cancer screen offer, EPDS.

title: Chronic kidney disease — screen, stage, manage
description: KDIGO 2024 CKD Evaluation & Management + WHO PEN HEARTS + Kenya MoH NCD Guidelines. Critical when eGFR < 30 (KDIGO G4 / G5) OR acute features (AKI, refractory hyperkalaemia K >= 6, severe metabolic acidosis HCO3 < 15) — urgent nephrology referral, avoid nephrotoxins (NSAIDs / aminoglycosides / IV contrast / herbal), renal-dose every medication (metformin contraindicated at eGFR < 30), hyperkalaemia bundle (IV calcium gluconate if ECG changes + insulin / dextrose + salbutamol nebuliser + dialysis for definitive removal). Critical for heavy proteinuria (uACR >= 300 mg/g, uPCR >= 50 mg/mmol, dipstick +++) OR rapid eGFR decline (> 5 mL/min/year) — workup HIV / HBsAg / anti-HCV / ANA / SPEP, maximally tolerated ACE inhibitor or ARB, ADD SGLT2 inhibitor (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin) when eGFR >= 20 and uACR >= 200 regardless of diabetes, BP < 130 / 80, nephrology referral for biopsy if cause unclear. Warning for KDIGO G3a / G3b (eGFR 30–59) OR A2 albuminuria (uACR 30–300) — confirm chronicity, BP < 130/80, ACE/ARB, SGLT2i for diabetic kidney disease, moderate-intensity statin, avoid nephrotoxins, vaccinate (influenza / pneumococcal / hepatitis B), annual review. Warning for high-risk patient without recent eGFR / uACR — order both today (risk markers: known hypertension, diabetes, HIV, age >= 60, family history CKD, recurrent UTI, kidney stones, long-term NSAID / herbal use).

references.label: KDIGO — 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for the Evaluation & Management of Chronic Kidney Disease

title: Severe head injury / traumatic brain injury triage
description: NICE NG232 (2023) Head injury: assessment and early management + Brain Trauma Foundation Guidelines 4th edn + CRASH-3 trial + WHO Acute Care + Kenya MoH Acute Care. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedHeadInjury. Critical for severe TBI (GCS <= 8) OR herniation features (unilateral fixed dilated pupil, motor posturing, Cushing's triad) — RSI for airway, target SpO2 >= 94 and SBP >= 110 (single episode of hypotension or hypoxia doubles mortality), 30 degree head-up, sedate, hypertonic saline 3% 250 mL OR mannitol 1 g/kg for herniation features, tranexamic acid 1 g IV + 1 g infusion 8 h if within 3 h of injury (CRASH-3), urgent CT, neurosurgical referral, reverse any anticoagulation. Critical for moderate TBI (GCS 9–12) OR any NICE high-risk feature (focal deficit, > 1 vomit, post-traumatic seizure, suspected open / depressed / basal skull fracture, age >= 65 + LOC / amnesia, anticoagulant + LOC / amnesia, dangerous mechanism + LOC / amnesia) — urgent CT brain within 1 hour, admit for neuro-obs every 30 min for 2 h then hourly for >= 24 h or until GCS 15 for 4 h, TXA if GCS <= 12 within 3 h. Warning for mild TBI (GCS 13–15) with intermediate feature (LOC / amnesia / single vomit / persistent headache / intoxication / suspected non-accidental injury in child) — 4-hour facility neuro-observation then discharge if asymptomatic with a written head-injury warning card to a responsible adult. Info for low-risk mild TBI — discharge with the written warning card and instruction to return immediately.

references.label: NICE NG232 — Head injury: assessment and early management (2023)
Brain Trauma Foundation — Guidelines for the management of severe TBI, 4th edition

title: Hyperosmolar Hyperglycaemic State (HHS) — recognition + bundle
description: JBDS-IP HHS Guideline (2022) + ADA Standards of Care 2024 + WHO PEN HEARTS. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedHhs. Diagnostic triad: hypovolaemia + plasma glucose >= 30 mmol/L + osmolality >= 320 mOsm/kg WITHOUT significant ketonaemia (< 3 mmol/L) or acidosis (pH > 7.30, HCO3 > 15 mmol/L). Critical bundle: 0.9 % NaCl 15 mL/kg over the first hour then ~1 L every 2 h, switch to 0.45 % NaCl only if osmolality does not fall despite positive balance AND corrected sodium is rising; add 5 % dextrose when glucose < 14 mmol/L; fixed-rate insulin 0.05 U/kg/h (lower than DKA) ONLY after 60 min of fluids AND glucose has stopped falling OR ketones rise; potassium 40 mmol/L when K 3.5–5.5, withhold when > 5.5 with ECG monitoring; prophylactic LMWH for very high VTE risk; investigate precipitant (infection, silent MI, stroke, missed therapy, steroid load). Severity overlay (osmolality >= 350, Na >= 160, K outside 3.5–6.0, GCS <= 12, SBP < 90 after fluids, SpO2 < 92) triggers ICU input. Mixed HHS/DKA picture (glucose >= 30 + ketones >= 3) returns a warning card recommending DKA-priority management with slow osmolality correction. Cards carry ICD-10 E14.0 / E11.0, ICD-11 5A21, SNOMED 421750000, LOINC 2345-7 + 2951-2.

references.label: JBDS-IP — The management of the hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state (HHS) in adults with diabetes (2022)

title: Tuberculosis treatment regimens (DS / RR / MDR / pre-XDR / XDR)
description: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on Tuberculosis — Module 4: Treatment (2022 with 2024 update) + Kenya NTLD-P Treatment Protocol. Sentinel-gated by tbConfirmed. Critical (drug-susceptible pulmonary / extrapulmonary TB) — 2HRZE/4HR with weight-banded 4FDC tablets per WHO band (25–37 / 38–54 / 55–70 / >=71 kg), paediatric child-friendly dispersible RHZ + E for < 25 kg; CNS / bone / disseminated TB extended to 9–12 months with adjunctive prednisolone for TB meningitis / pericarditis; alternative WHO 4-month 2HPMZ/2HPM rifapentine-moxifloxacin regimen for pulmonary DS-TB >= 12 y >= 40 kg. HIV co-infection: ART within 2 weeks (CD4 < 50 or TB meningitis) or 8 weeks otherwise, rifampicin doubles dolutegravir clearance so DTG 50 mg twice daily during rifampicin + 2 weeks. Pyridoxine 25–50 mg daily to prevent isoniazid neuropathy. Pregnancy-safe regimen. Critical (rifampicin-resistant / MDR-TB) — refer to PMDT site within 48 h for WHO 6-month all-oral BPaL(M): bedaquiline + pretomanid + linezolid + moxifloxacin (drop moxifloxacin if fluoroquinolone resistance). Critical (pre-XDR / XDR) — national reference centre individualised regimen with bedaquiline + linezolid + clofazimine + cycloserine ± delamanid for 18–20 months. Monthly LFTs, full blood count (linezolid myelosuppression), ECG QTc (bedaquiline + moxifloxacin), visual acuity + colour vision (ethambutol + linezolid). Mandatory case notification within 24 h; trace household contacts; offer TPT (3HP / 6H / 1HP) to <5y + PLHIV contacts. Cards carry ICD-10 A15/A16, ICD-11 1B10/1B14, SNOMED 56717001/85729005, ATC J04AM06 (HRZE) / J04AK05 (bedaquiline) / J04AK08 (pretomanid).

references.label: WHO Consolidated Guidelines on Tuberculosis — Module 4: Treatment (Drug-susceptible TB, 2022)
WHO Consolidated Guidelines on Tuberculosis — Module 4: Treatment (Drug-resistant TB, 2022 with 2024 update)

title: Rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP)
description: WHO position paper on rabies vaccines (April 2018) + CDC ACIP rabies prevention + Kenya MoH rabies elimination strategy. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedRabiesExposure. Critical (WHO Category III: transdermal bite, scratch breaking skin, mucous-membrane / broken-skin contamination, ANY bat exposure) — (1) wound care: wash with soap and running water for >=15 min then virucidal (povidone-iodine / 70% alcohol / quaternary ammonium); (2) rabies immunoglobulin HRIG 20 IU/kg (or equine RIG 40 IU/kg) infiltrated AS MUCH AS ANATOMICALLY POSSIBLE into and around each wound with any remaining volume IM distant from the vaccine site; (3) start vaccine same day — WHO 4-dose IM Essen schedule (days 0/3/7/14–28) using purified Vero-cell vaccine, OR dose-sparing intradermal Updated Thai Red Cross (0.1 mL ID at two sites days 0/3/7/28). Critical (Category II: nibbling on uncovered skin or minor scratch without bleeding) — wound care + full vaccine course, NO RIG. Critical (re-exposure after prior full PEP / pre-exposure vaccination) — abbreviated 2-dose booster days 0+3, NO RIG. Info (Category I: touch / feed / intact-skin lick) — no PEP unless contact uncertain. Pregnancy / breastfeeding / immunocompromised state are NOT contraindications. Tetanus prophylaxis + reassure that PEP is never too late as long as symptoms have not started. Notify public-health surveillance. Cards carry ICD-10 Z20.3 / Z29.2, ICD-11 1G40, SNOMED 14168008 (rabies) / 313160007 (vaccination) / 417303002 (RIG administration), ATC J07BG01 + J06BB05.

title: Neonatal jaundice — AAP 2022 thresholds + acute bilirubin encephalopathy
description: AAP 2022 Clinical Practice Guideline Revision: Management of Hyperbilirubinaemia in the Newborn >= 35 Weeks Gestation + WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children (2nd edn) + Kenya MoH National Newborn Care Guidelines. Critical (acute bilirubin encephalopathy: lethargy progressing to hypertonia, retrocollis/opisthotonus, shrill cry, fever, seizures) — INTENSIVE phototherapy immediately (continuous LED panels >=30 µW/cm²/nm), prepare double-volume exchange transfusion 160 mL/kg, cross-match, NPO, monitor temperature/glucose/calcium/electrolytes, investigate cause (DAT, blood group, FBC + retics + film, G6PD, sepsis, TORCH). Critical (jaundice in the first 24 h of life — NEVER physiological) — admit, TSB + direct bilirubin, DAT + maternal antibody screen, G6PD, sepsis screen, phototherapy. Critical (TSB >= AAP exchange threshold for postnatal age + risk profile — gestational age < 38 wks OR DAT+/G6PD/ABO-Rh/sepsis/dusky pallor/poor feeding) — exchange transfusion + intensive phototherapy. Critical (TSB >= AAP phototherapy threshold) — intensive phototherapy + investigate cause if rapid rise. Warning (within 2 mg/dL of threshold OR rise > 0.2 mg/dL/h) — repeat TSB 6–12 h, optimise feeding (>=8 breastfeeds in 24 h), risk-factor review. Warning (prolonged jaundice >14 d term, >21 d preterm) — measure split bilirubin (must be < 1 mg/dL or < 20% total); conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia is biliary atresia until proven otherwise — URGENT abdominal ultrasound + Kasai window < 60 d. Cards carry ICD-10 P59/P57/P55, ICD-11 KA86/KA64, SNOMED 387731001 (neonatal jaundice) / 234468005 (severe hyperbilirubinaemia), LOINC 1975-2 + 6082-2.

references.label: AAP — Clinical Practice Guideline Revision: Management of Hyperbilirubinaemia in the Newborn Infant >= 35 Weeks (Kemper et al., Pediatrics 2022)
WHO — Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children (2nd edn, 2013)

title: Sickle-cell disease — vaso-occlusive crisis + complications
description: American Society of Hematology 2020 Clinical Practice Guidelines for Sickle Cell Disease (Acute & Chronic Pain) + NHLBI 2014 Evidence-Based Management of Sickle Cell Disease + Kenya MoH Sickle Cell Disease Guidelines (2019). Sentinel-gated by sickleCellDisease. Critical (life-threatening SCD emergency: acute chest syndrome [new infiltrate or SpO2 < 92], stroke / focal neurology, priapism > 4 h, splenic sequestration with falling Hb, aplastic crisis Hb <6 with low retics, sepsis with fever >=38.5, severe anaemia Hb <5) — ABC + oxygen to SpO2 >=95, isotonic IV fluids at maintenance (AVOID over-hydration — risk of ACS), morphine 0.1 mg/kg IV every 10–20 min titrated, ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg + azithromycin for ACS, exchange transfusion for stroke / severe ACS / refractory priapism, urology for priapism, urgent neurology + CT/MRI for stroke (NO tPA). Critical (vaso-occlusive pain crisis NRS >=4) — analgesia within 30 min per ASH 2020, paracetamol + ibuprofen + opioid titrated, maintenance fluids, incentive spirometry, screen for precipitants, optimise hydroxyurea (15–20 mg/kg/day titrated to MCV 100–110, ANC > 2). Warning (chronic-care gaps): not on hydroxyurea (offer at >=9 months), missing penicillin V prophylaxis <5 y, missing PCV13/PPSV23/meningococcal/Hib/influenza, no annual transcranial Doppler 2–16 y, no retinal screen >=10 y, no folic-acid 5 mg daily. Cards carry ICD-10 D57/D57.0, ICD-11 3A51, SNOMED 237364002 (SCD) / 417847000 (vaso-occlusive crisis), LOINC 67881-8 (HbS%), ATC L01XX05 (hydroxyurea).

references.label: American Society of Hematology — 2020 Clinical Practice Guidelines for Sickle Cell Disease: Management of Acute and Chronic Pain (Brandow et al., Blood Adv 2020)
NHLBI — Evidence-Based Management of Sickle Cell Disease (Expert Panel Report 2014)

title: Dengue / chikungunya / Zika — arboviral fever triage
description: WHO Dengue Guidelines for Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention and Control (2009 + 2024 update) + WHO Handbook for Clinical Management of Dengue (2012) + PAHO Guidelines (2022) + CDC Dengue Clinical Guidance. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedArboviralFever. Critical (severe dengue, Group C): shock features (narrow pulse pressure <=20 mmHg, SBP <90), severe organ involvement (AST/ALT >=1000, GCS <=13, creatinine >200), or clinically-significant mucosal bleeding with platelets <20 — admit HDU/ICU, isotonic crystalloid 10–20 mL/kg over 1 h titrated down to 7-5-3 mL/kg/h, colloid bolus for refractory leakage with rising Hct, transfuse packed cells for occult bleeding (falling Hct despite fluids), STRICTLY NO NSAIDs / aspirin, paracetamol 15 mg/kg every 6 h (NOT every 4 h). Critical (warning signs, Group B): abdominal pain or tenderness, persistent vomiting, clinical fluid accumulation (ascites / pleural effusion), mucosal bleeding, lethargy or restlessness, hepatomegaly >2 cm, rapid platelet fall, haematocrit rise >=20% from baseline — admit IV fluids 5–7 mL/kg/h titrated, 4-hourly observations through critical phase (days 3–7). Critical override: suspected Zika in pregnancy — refer maternal-foetal medicine for serial foetal ultrasound + RT-PCR (serum + urine within 14 d). Warning (uncomplicated, Group A): outpatient supportive care + daily review during critical phase + oral fluids + paracetamol ONLY + mosquito-net protection. Chikungunya overlay (marked polyarthralgia) and Zika overlay (rash + conjunctivitis + safe-sex counselling) included.

references.label: WHO — Dengue: Guidelines for Diagnosis, Treatment, Prevention and Control (2009 with 2024 update)
WHO — Handbook for Clinical Management of Dengue (2012)
PAHO — Guidelines for the clinical diagnosis and treatment of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika (2022)
CDC — Dengue Clinical Guidance

title: Schistosomiasis — treatment + complications + MDA eligibility
description: WHO Guideline on Control and Elimination of Human Schistosomiasis (2022) + CDC Schistosomiasis Clinical Guidance + Kenya MoH National Schistosomiasis & STH Strategic Plan. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedSchistosomiasis. Critical (complicated disease: neuroschistosomiasis with myelitis / seizures / focal signs, portal hypertension with variceal bleed, massive haematuria with shock, obstructive uropathy) — admit + specialist referral + complication-specific resuscitation + prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day for neuroschistosomiasis BEFORE praziquantel + ultrasound + MRI spine/brain where indicated. Critical (Katayama fever / acute schistosomiasis 4–8 weeks post-exposure: fever + urticaria + eosinophilia + cough + hepatosplenomegaly) — prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day x 5–7 days FIRST, defer curative praziquantel 6–12 weeks. Critical (confirmed infection: positive egg / antigen / serology) — praziquantel 40 mg/kg single oral dose with food (S. mansoni / haematobium / intercalatum / guineensis), 60 mg/kg for S. japonicum / mekongi; split 20 mg/kg twice 4–6 h apart for tolerability. Pregnancy >=14 weeks safe per WHO 2006/2022. Recheck eggs / antigen at 8–12 weeks; second course if positive (efficacy ~85%). Warning (high suspicion without confirmation) — urine microscopy + stool ova + urine CCA + serology + empirical praziquantel reasonable in endemic settings. Info (MDA eligibility): yearly praziquantel 40 mg/kg for school-age (5–14 y) per WHO MDA; WHO 2022 expands to preschool + adults in high-prevalence (>=10%) settings.

references.label: WHO — Guideline on Control and Elimination of Human Schistosomiasis (2022)
CDC — Schistosomiasis Clinical Guidance

title: IMCI: ear infection in children under 5 (AOM / CSOM / mastoiditis)
description: WHO IMCI Chart Booklet (2014) + WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children (2nd edn) + AAP Clinical Practice Guideline: Diagnosis and Management of Acute Otitis Media (Lieberthal et al. 2013) + Kenya MoH IMCI. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedEarProblem + ageMonths < 60. Critical (mastoiditis: tender swelling behind the ear with outward-pushed pinna) — admit, IV ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg once daily until improved + oral step-down for total 14 days; add metronidazole if suspected intracranial extension; contrast CT or MRI of the temporal bone; urgent ENT referral for myringotomy +/- mastoidectomy if not improving 48 h. Critical (AOM: pus <14 d OR bulging tympanic membrane + ear pain): amoxicillin 80–90 mg/kg/day divided twice daily for 5–10 days (10 days if <2 y or severe); co-amoxiclav for prior amoxicillin failure; macrolide for IgE-mediated penicillin allergy; AAP watchful-waiting allowed in age >=2 unilateral without otorrhoea if family can return; paracetamol + ibuprofen for analgesia. Warning (CSOM: pus >=14 days) — dry wicking >=3 times/day + topical ciprofloxacin 0.3% drops 5 drops BD for 2 weeks (or until 3 days after dryness); AVOID aminoglycoside drops (ototoxic) and oral antibiotics; safe-water practices; ENT referral if no response in 2 weeks or cholesteatoma suspected. Info (no infection) — reassure + return triggers + PCV / influenza vaccination.

references.label: WHO — IMCI Chart Booklet (2014)
WHO — Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children (2nd edn, 2013)
AAP — Clinical Practice Guideline: Diagnosis and Management of Acute Otitis Media (Lieberthal et al., Pediatrics 2013)

title: Neonatal sepsis / Possible Serious Bacterial Infection (PSBI)
description: WHO Managing Possible Serious Bacterial Infection in Young Infants When Referral is Not Feasible (2015 simplified regimens) + WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children (2nd edn 2013) + WHO Sepsis 2020 + Kenya MoH National Newborn Care Guidelines (2014). Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedNeonatalSepsis (postnatal age 0–28 days). Critical (PSBI features: unable to feed since birth or stopped feeding, convulsions, movement only when stimulated, severe chest indrawing, grunting, RR >=60, temperature >=38 OR <35.5, bulging fontanelle, neck stiffness) — first-line within 1 hour: ampicillin 50 mg/kg IV/IM every 12 h (week 1) or every 8 h (week 2+) + gentamicin 5 mg/kg IM/IV once daily (4 mg/kg if <32 weeks) for 10–14 days; suspected meningitis adds ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg (or cefotaxime in jaundiced / premature) — LP when stable; full sepsis screen (blood culture >=1 mL, FBC, CRP, glucose, urine culture, CXR if respiratory features); refer to neonatal admission within 1 hour. When referral NOT possible, WHO 2015 simplified outpatient PSBI regimen: IM gentamicin once daily for 7 days + oral amoxicillin 50 mg/kg BD for 7 days with DAILY follow-up. Warning (risk-factor screen positive in a well infant: maternal chorioamnionitis, PROM >18 h, intrapartum fever, GBS+ without IAP, prematurity <35 wks) — admit 48 h observation + sepsis screen + culture-driven decision. Info (well infant): routine PNC + WHO danger-signs counselling + cord care + vitamin K 1 mg IM + BCG / OPV at birth + exclusive breastfeeding 8–12x/24 h.

references.label: WHO — Managing possible serious bacterial infection in young infants when referral is not feasible (2015)
WHO — Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children (2nd edn, 2013)
WHO — Improving the prevention, diagnosis and clinical management of sepsis (resolution 70.7, 2020)
Kenya MoH — National Newborn Care Guidelines (2014)

title: Heat stroke / heat-related illness
description: CDC NIOSH Heat-Related Illness clinical guidance + WHO Heat and Health technical brief + Korey-Stringer Institute Exertional Heat Stroke Consensus + NEJM 2019 Heat-Related Illnesses review. Sentinel-gated by context.suspectedHeatIllness. Critical (heat stroke: rectal core temperature >=40 °C OR >=39 °C with CNS dysfunction — confusion, ataxia, seizures, coma): rapid cooling within 30 minutes is the primary survival determinant — EXERTIONAL heat stroke COLD-WATER IMMERSION (head out of water, continuous rectal-temp monitoring, target <=39 °C in 30 min; stop at 39 °C to avoid overshoot); CLASSIC heat stroke evaporative cooling (continuous fanning of wet patient + ice packs neck/axillae/groin); ABC support; IV 0.9% NaCl 20 mL/kg bolus titrated; AVOID antipyretics (paracetamol / aspirin do NOT lower hyperthermic body temperature); benzodiazepine for seizures; rhabdomyolysis bundle (target urine output 2 mL/kg/h, urinary alkalinisation if severe, recheck CK / K+ / creatinine 6-hourly); ICU admission. Critical (severe heat exhaustion with red flags: SBP <90, persistent vomiting, Na <=130 or >=150, creatinine >200, dark urine suggesting rhabdomyolysis, CK > 5x ULN) — admit + IV fluids + close monitoring + escalation to heat-stroke pathway if temperature climbs or any CNS dysfunction. Warning (heat exhaustion: heat-exposure symptoms with core temp <40 °C and no CNS dysfunction) — move to cool, oral ORS 1–1.5 L over 1 h (or IV 0.9% NaCl 1 L over 1 h in vulnerable groups), rest >=30 min, recheck temperature / pulse / orthostatic BP every 15 min. Info (heat-exposure risk) — WHO counselling (hydration ~200 mL every 20 min, work-rest cycles, light loose clothing, avoid 11 am–4 pm exertion, NEVER leave infants / pets in parked vehicles, twice-daily check on vulnerable household members during heat waves).

references.label: CDC NIOSH — Heat-Related Illness clinical guidance for healthcare workers
WHO — Heat and Health technical brief
Korey-Stringer Institute / NATA — Exertional Heat Stroke Consensus

title: MDR/RR-TB all-oral regimen builder (BPaL/M)

title: STEMI — fibrinolysis vs PCI pathway

title: Alcohol withdrawal — CIWA-Ar protocol

title: Uncomplicated UTI — empirical therapy
description: For non-pregnant women with cystitis: nitrofurantoin 100 mg BD × 3 days (preferred where eGFR ≥ 45) OR trimethoprim 200 mg BD × 3 days (avoid if local E. coli resistance > 20 %). title: Asthma — GINA stepwise therapy
description: On context.diagnoses contains asthma + context.gina.SABAUsePerWeek, recommends GINA-aligned step: Track 1 MART (budesonide-formoterol PRN ± low/medium maintenance). title: Iron-deficiency anaemia — replacement pathway
description: Calculates iron deficit using Ganzoni formula or simplified table. Prefers oral ferrous sulphate 200 mg OD (alternate days dosing supported by HEPCIDIN evidence). IV ferric carboxymaltose if intolerance, malabsorption, CKD-anaemia, IBD, pregnancy ≥ 14 weeks, or Hb < 70 with symptoms. title: Hypothyroidism — levothyroxine initiation
description: On TSH > 10 mU/L OR TSH 4–10 with symptoms / pregnancy / fertility planning, recommends levothyroxine 1.6 µg/kg/day (start full dose if young + no IHD; start 25 µg if elderly / IHD). Repeat TSH at 6–8 weeks. Pregnancy: aim TSH < 2.5 mU/L; increase dose by 30 % on confirmed pregnancy. Reads context.tsh, context.freeT4, context.ageYears, context.pregnant, context.ihd.

title: HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP)
description: For occupational / sexual / mother-to-child exposure within 72 h: recommends TDF + 3TC (or FTC) + DTG once daily × 28 days; alternative regimens for renal impairment. title: Tumour lysis syndrome risk recognition + prophylaxis
description: Fires for oncology patients about to receive cytolytic therapy in high-risk haematological malignancy (Burkitt, ALL with WBC > 100, AML with WBC > 50, bulky high-grade lymphoma). title: Neutropenic sepsis emergency — Sepsis-6 within 1 hour
description: Fires for any patient with neutrophil count < 0.5 (or < 1.0 with falling trend) AND fever ≥ 38°C single OR ≥ 37.5°C sustained 1 h. Recommends immediate broad-spectrum antibiotic (piperacillin-tazobactam OR meropenem per local policy + vancomycin if line / shock / MRSA risk), blood + line cultures, lactate, fluids, urine output. References NICE CG151. Reads context.neutrophilCount, context.temperature, context.cancerTherapyStartDays, context.suspectedFocus — never patient identity.

title: Acute intracerebral haemorrhage — BP control + anticoagulant reversal
description: Fires for any patient with imaging-confirmed ICH. Recommends acute SBP lowering to 130–140 mmHg with IV labetalol / nicardipine (INTERACT-2 / ATACH-2 targets) and immediate reversal of any anticoagulant: warfarin → vit K + 4F-PCC; dabigatran → idarucizumab; FXa DOAC → andexanet OR 4F-PCC; heparin → protamine. Antiplatelet platelet transfusion NOT recommended unless neurosurgery imminent (PATCH). Reads context.ichDiagnosis, context.systolicMmHg, context.anticoagulant, context.gcs — never patient identity.

title: mhGAP — Self-harm / acute suicide-risk pathway
description: Fires when patient has documented suicidal ideation with plan / intent OR recent self-harm act. Reads context.suicideIdeationPresent, context.suicidePlanPresent, context.recentSelfHarmAct, context.suspectedIngestion — never patient identity.

title: NSAID at ≥ 20 weeks gestation — contraindicated

title: Codeine and tramadol in children < 12 — contraindicated

title: Nirmatrelvir-ritonavir (Paxlovid) — major interaction screen

Recommends stopping the serotonergic agent (2 weeks washout for most, 5 weeks for fluoxetine) BEFORE linezolid, or selecting alternative antibiotic. Includes monitoring guidance if combination unavoidable. Reads context.medications — never patient identity.

title: WHO HEARTS — stepwise BP-lowering protocol prompt
description: Fires for adults with confirmed hypertension whose BP remains above target on the current step. title: Opioid overdose — titrated naloxone + observation

title: Lithium toxicity — recognition + dialysis criteria

title: Beta-blocker / calcium channel blocker overdose — high-dose insulin euglycaemia

title: Methanol / ethylene glycol poisoning — fomepizole + dialysis criteria

title: Suspected viral encephalitis — empirical aciclovir + LP within 6 h
description: Fires for fever + new altered mental state / personality / focal seizure / new focal neurology. title: TOF hypercyanotic spell management

title: Suspected ductal-dependent CHD — start prostaglandin

title: Kawasaki disease — IVIG + aspirin + coronary echo

title: Severe hypothermia — ECMO rewarming criteria

title: Acute limb ischaemia — heparin + Rutherford classification

recommendation: Admit; F-75 130 ml/kg/day in 8–12 feeds; no iron in stabilisation; routine amoxicillin + vitamin A + folic acid + measles vaccine. recommendation: Activate E-MOTIVE bundle: uterine massage + oxytocin 10 IU IM/IV + TXA 1 g IV (within 3h) + IV crystalloid + genital tract exam + catheter + escalation if uncontrolled at 30 min. Add misoprostol 800 mcg SL, balloon tamponade, B-Lynch, NASG for transport. Use carbetocin where heat-stable available.
rationale: WHO 2022 PPH guideline + E-MOTIVE Lancet 2023 + WOMAN trial 2017.

title: Sepsis — Hour-1 bundle in adults
recommendation: Within 1 hour: lactate + blood cultures before antibiotics + broad-spectrum antibiotic + 30 ml/kg crystalloid if hypotensive/lactate > 4 + noradrenaline (MAP ≥ 65) if persistent hypotension. Source control within 6–12h. Test for malaria in endemic areas (RDT) before attributing to bacterial sepsis.
rationale: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 + WHO sepsis resolution.

title: Cholera — aggressive rehydration + outbreak notification (Kenya IDSR)
indicators: acute watery diarrhoea with severe dehydration
recommendation: Plan C IV Ringer's lactate 100 ml/kg over 3h (adults) / age-specific paediatric regimen; continue ORS as soon as able to drink; doxycycline 300 mg single dose (or azithromycin in children/pregnancy); zinc 20 mg × 10 days in children; notify IDSR within 24h; set up CTC; reactive OCV per GTFCC/MOH.
rationale: GTFCC Ending Cholera Roadmap 2030 + Kenya National Cholera Plan + IDSR.

title: GBV — LIVES support + 72h HIV PEP + 120h emergency contraception (Kenya)
indicators: disclosed or suspected sexual / intimate partner violence
recommendation: Use WHO LIVES first-line psychological support. For sexual assault within 72h start TLD HIV PEP × 28 days, within 120h give levonorgestrel 1.5 mg or Cu-IUD, STI prophylaxis (ceftriaxone + azithromycin + metronidazole), hepatitis B vaccine ± HBIG, tetanus. Complete PRC1/P3 form. Refer to SGBV centre; mandatory reporting for child cases (Children Act + Sexual Offences Act).
rationale: WHO Clinical Handbook on IPV/Sexual Violence (2014) + Kenya National GBV Guidelines.

title: Breastfeeding support — BFHI Ten Steps
recommendation: Implement Ten Steps: skin-to-skin within 1h, exclusive breastfeeding 6 months, rooming-in, responsive feeding, no formula/bottles/pacifiers unless medically indicated, discharge with community support. Latch + position counselling. Continue breastfeeding through mastitis with antibiotics. Follow Kenya BMS Act + WHO Code (no formula marketing).
rationale: WHO/UNICEF BFHI 2018 + Kenya BFCI.

title: RTI trauma — cABCDE + TXA within 3h + permissive hypotension
recommendation: cABCDE primary survey; control catastrophic haemorrhage (tourniquet, pelvic binder); permissive hypotension (SBP 80–90) until bleed controlled; TXA 1 g IV within 3 hours of injury then 1 g over 8h; massive transfusion 1:1:1; head-up 30° + SBP > 110 for head injury; activate trauma referral per Kenya EMC strategy.
rationale: ATLS + CRASH-2 + Kenya National EMC Strategy 2020–2025.

title: Pediatric HIV — DTG-based ART from 4 weeks (Kenya NASCOP)
recommendation: Start ART immediately regardless of CD4. < 4 wks: AZT + 3TC + NVP. 4 wks–< 20 kg: ABC + 3TC + paediatric DTG dispersible. ≥ 20 kg: TDF + 3TC + DTG. Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis from 6 wks of age in HIV-exposed until HIV excluded. TB preventive therapy. Routine VL at 6 + 12 months then annually; enhanced adherence if VL > 1000. Operation Triple Zero for adolescents.
rationale: Kenya NASCOP ARV Guidelines 2022 + WHO 2024 update.

title: Drowning — 5 rescue breaths first, oxygen, observe asymptomatic 4–6h
recommendation: Hypoxia is the primary problem — start CPR with FIVE rescue breaths before compressions. Oxygen titrated to SpO2 ≥ 94%. Spinal immobilisation only if mechanism + signs. No prophylactic antibiotics or steroids. Asymptomatic with normal exam at 4–6h can discharge. 'Not dead until warm and dead' — rewarm to 32°C before terminating resuscitation. Implement WHO 10 prevention interventions.
rationale: WHO Global Report on Drowning + ILCOR 2021 + UN A/RES/75/273.

title: Neonatal resuscitation — The Golden Minute (HBB)
recommendation: Dry + stimulate + clear airway within 30 sec; if not breathing by 60 sec start BMV 40–60/min with room air (term) ensuring chest rise. Add chest compressions 3:1 if HR < 60 after 30 sec effective ventilation. Adrenaline 0.01–0.03 mg/kg IV. Delayed cord clamping ≥ 1 min. Skin-to-skin. Discontinue at 20 min if no HR. Therapeutic hypothermia for HIE where available.
rationale: WHO Basic Newborn Resuscitation 2012/2024 + Helping Babies Breathe 2nd Ed + Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols.

title: Rabies PEP — wound wash + vaccine ± RIG by exposure category
recommendation: Wash wound with soap + running water × 15 min + virucidal. Category II → vaccine only. Category III / immunocompromised / bat / head-face-hand bite → vaccine + RIG (HRIG 20 IU/kg or ERIG 40 IU/kg infiltrated into wound). Cell-culture vaccine days 0, 3, 7, 14, 28 IM or WHO dose-sparing ID 4-visit regimen. Previously vaccinated: 2 doses days 0 + 3, no RIG. Notify One Health team.
rationale: WHO Rabies Position Paper 2018 + Kenya National Rabies Elimination Strategy 2014–2030.

title: Suspected anthrax — start ciprofloxacin + combination therapy if systemic
indicators: painless eschar with surrounding oedema after livestock/hide contact
recommendation: Cutaneous uncomplicated: ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BD × 7–10 days (or doxycycline). Systemic / inhalational / extensive cutaneous: IV ciprofloxacin + clindamycin + meropenem; add antitoxin (raxibacumab / obiltoxaximab) where available. Do NOT excise lesion. Notify IDSR within 24h + county veterinary. PEP for contacts: ciprofloxacin 500 mg BD × 60 days + 3-dose vaccine.
rationale: WHO Anthrax 4th ed + Kenya IDSR + CDC 2014.

title: Brucellosis — doxycycline + rifampicin × 6 weeks (WHO regimen)
recommendation: Adult: doxycycline 100 mg PO BD + rifampicin 600–900 mg daily × 6 weeks (or doxy 6w + streptomycin 1 g IM × 14–21d). Neurobrucellosis / endocarditis / spondylitis: add ceftriaxone, treat ≥ 3–6 months, surgery if abscess/valve. Children ≤ 8 yrs: rifampicin + cotrimoxazole. Pregnancy: rifampicin ± cotrimoxazole (no doxy / strep). Counsel: complete full course, avoid raw milk.
rationale: WHO Brucellosis Guidelines + Kenya One Health plan.

title: Suspected RVF — supportive care + outbreak notification
indicators: acute febrile illness + livestock abortions in area
recommendation: No specific antiviral — supportive (blood products, AKI dialysis, ICU). Notify IDSR + WHO IHR within 24h. Standard precautions sufficient (no documented human-human). Coordinate with county vet for livestock ring vaccination + animal movement restriction. Refer survivors with visual symptoms to ophthalmology.
rationale: WHO RVF + Kenya RVF Contingency Plan.

title: Leptospirosis — doxycycline (mild) / penicillin G (severe) + IDSR notify
indicators: febrile illness + conjunctival suffusion + calf myalgia + floodwater/sewer exposure
recommendation: Mild: doxycycline 100 mg BD × 7 d (amoxicillin in children / pregnancy). Severe (Weil's, pulmonary haemorrhage, AKI): IV penicillin G 1.5 MU q6h or ceftriaxone 1 g daily × 7 d; ICU support; consider methylprednisolone for pulmonary haemorrhage. Watch for Jarisch-Herxheimer. Doxycycline 200 mg weekly chemoprophylaxis for short-term high-risk exposure. Notify IDSR.
rationale: WHO Leptospirosis Guidance + PAHO manual.

title: OP poisoning — atropinise to clear chest, add pralidoxime, watch for intermediate syndrome
recommendation: ABCDE; early intubation if GCS drop or severe secretions; decontaminate skin; activated charcoal if < 1h + airway protected. ATROPINE doubling-dose IV (start 2–5 mg) every 5 min until atropinised (clear chest, HR>80, dry axillae); then infusion 10–20%/h of cumulative. PRALIDOXIME 30 mg/kg IV bolus then 8 mg/kg/h × 7 d. Diazepam for seizures. Avoid suxamethonium. Watch INTERMEDIATE SYNDROME days 1–4 (proximal weakness, respiratory paralysis). Mental health assessment if intentional. Paraquat: NO antidote, AVOID supplemental O2.
rationale: WHO Pesticide Intoxication Guidelines 2008 + Eddleston Lancet 2008.

title: Adolescent contact — HEEADSSS + confidentiality + WHO AA-HA! standards
recommendation: Confidential HEEADSSS interview; screen for depression (PHQ-A) + substance use (CRAFFT) + sexual health + safety. SRH: full method-mix contraception (LARC), EC, STI syndromic, HIV test (opt-out 15+ with maturity), PrEP if eligible. HPV vaccine 10 yrs (catch-up 14). Mental health per mhGAP adolescent module. Defilement reporting per Sexual Offences Act if < 18 with partner > 18. School re-entry support after pregnancy. DREAMS bundle for AGYW.
rationale: WHO AA-HA! 2nd ed + Kenya ASRH Policy + DREAMS.

title: Major burn — Parkland fluids + early airway + transfer if criteria
recommendation: Stop burning + cool with running water × 20 min; high-flow O2; INTUBATE EARLY if inhalational suspected. Parkland: 4 ml/kg × %TBSA RL over 24h (half in first 8h from burn); titrate to UOP 0.5 ml/kg/h adult, 1 ml/kg/h paeds. IV opioid analgesia. Silver sulfadiazine or honey dressings; tetanus prophylaxis; NG feeds within 6h. Refer per ABA criteria (face/hands/feet/perineum/inhalational/>10% paeds/>15% adult/electrical/chemical). Screen for NAI in children + IPV in women.
rationale: WHO Burn Guidelines 2018 + ISBI 2018 + Kenya KNH Burn Guidelines.

title: Tungiasis — dimeticone topical + footwear + community treatment
recommendation: Topical dimeticone two-oil mixture, repeat at 7 days; avoid kerosene/petrol home remedies. Wound care + tetanus prophylaxis; antibiotic if secondary cellulitis. PREVENTION: closed-toe shoes, concrete floors, animal reservoir treatment, CHV-led community case-finding. Heavy infestation: refer + treat household / community concurrently per Kenya jigger policy.
rationale: WHO NTD Roadmap + Kenya National Jigger Policy 2014 + Heukelbach Lancet ID 2006.

title: Podoconiosis — daily hygiene + footwear + community programme
indicators: bilateral ascending leg lymphoedema in highland barefoot agricultural worker
recommendation: WHO morbidity-management package: daily foot wash + dry + emollient + elevation + exercise + compression + closed footwear. Treat acute adenolymphangitis (ADL) attacks with rest + antibiotic (penicillin/flucloxacillin). Surgical nodulectomy for severe nodular disease (specialist). Address stigma + livelihood. Primary prevention: shoes + cement floors from childhood in endemic highland areas.
rationale: WHO Podoconiosis NTD 2011 + Davey et al + WHO NTD Roadmap 2021–2030.

title: SCD — penicillin V + hydroxyurea + TCD screen + pneumococcal vaccine
recommendation: Penicillin V prophylaxis to age 5 (longer if past pneumococcal sepsis), PCV13 + PPSV23, meningococcal, annual flu, folic acid 5 mg, ITN + malaria prophylaxis. HYDROXYUREA in ALL children HbSS from 9 months (start 20 mg/kg/day, titrate to MTD). Annual TCD age 2–16. Acute pain: IV opioid within 30 min + IV fluids 1.5× maint + incentive spirometry. ACS: ceftriaxone + macrolide + simple/exchange transfusion. Stroke: urgent exchange transfusion. Fever = sepsis until proven otherwise.
rationale: WHO SCD strategy + REACH NEJM 2019 + NHLBI 2014.

title: Obstetric fistula — early catheter + refer fistula centre + comprehensive rehab
recommendation: Continuous Foley catheterisation early (within 6 weeks of delivery may close some — 15–20% spontaneous closure). Skin barrier care, treat UTI, screen + treat depression. Refer to fistula surgical centre (KNH / Jamaa / Fistula Foundation network). Post-repair: catheter 14–21 d, no PV intercourse 3 m, elective C-section future pregnancies. Address prevention: skilled birth attendance, partogram, EmONC access, delay child marriage.
rationale: WHO Obstetric Fistula 2006 + Kenya Fistula Elimination Framework + UNFPA Campaign.

title: School-based deworming + vitamin A + adolescent iron-folate (Kenya NSBDP)
indicators: school-based programme contact in endemic area
recommendation: Pre-school (12–59 mo): vitamin A 100k–200k IU 6-monthly + albendazole 200–400 mg 6-monthly. School-age (5–14): albendazole 400 mg or mebendazole 500 mg single dose annually (twice yearly if STH > 50%) + praziquantel 40 mg/kg if schisto > 10%. Adolescent girls (10–19): weekly iron-folate 60+2.8 mg + HPV vaccine + menstrual hygiene + comprehensive sexuality education. Universal: vision + hearing + oral health + WASH + ITN + IPTsc per WHO 2022 where indicated.
rationale: WHO Preventive Chemotherapy 2022 + WHO Vitamin A 2011 + Kenya NSBDP + WHO IPTsc 2022.

title: Suspected noma — emergency antibiotics + nutritional rehabilitation + refer reconstructive
indicators: necrotising orofacial gangrene in malnourished child
recommendation: URGENT — 90% mortality untreated. IV amoxicillin-clavulanate OR ampicillin + metronidazole + gentamicin × 7–14 days. Aggressive nutritional rehab per IMAM (F-75 → F-100/RUTF). Treat malaria/measles/HIV/dehydration concurrently. Mouth care chlorhexidine 4×/day, gentle debridement only after antibiotic response. Vitamin A 200k IU, folate, zinc. Refer to reconstructive surgery (Noma Hospital network) at 3–6 months. PREVENTION: address SAM, measles immunisation, oral health education.
rationale: WHO Noma NTD designation 2023 + WHO Noma brochure + MSF Sokoto protocol.

title: VL eastern Africa — PM+SSG combination or AmBisome
indicators: fever > 1 month + splenomegaly + pancytopaenia in endemic area
recommendation: Confirm rK39 + bone marrow / spleen aspirate. First-line: paromomycin 15 mg/kg/d IM + SSG 20 mg/kg/d × 17 d. AmBisome 3–5 mg/kg/d total 30 mg/kg for pregnancy / HIV / age > 45 / severe. HIV co-infection: AmBisome 40 mg/kg total + miltefosine, then monthly maintenance until CD4 > 200. Monitor SSG QT + LFT.
rationale: WHO TRS 949 + Kenya VL Strategic Plan.

title: HAT — fexinidazole (gambiense) / NECT or melarsoprol (rhodesiense)
recommendation: T.b. gambiense first-line: fexinidazole PO × 10 d (stage 1 + stage 2 with CSF WBC ≤ 100). Stage 2 severe: NECT (eflornithine + nifurtimox). T.b. rhodesiense stage 1: suramin; stage 2: melarsoprol with prednisolone cover (5–10% mortality reactive encephalopathy). Follow-up LP at 6+12+24 months. Notify WHO surveillance.
rationale: WHO HAT treatment guidelines 2019.

title: CL — local for small, systemic SSG / miltefosine for facial / multiple
recommendation: Confirm slit smear / PCR. Small lesions on body: observe or intralesional SSG / cryotherapy / thermotherapy. Facial / large / multiple / immunocompromised: systemic SSG 20 mg/kg/day × 20 d or miltefosine 2.5 mg/kg/d × 28 d (avoid pregnancy). AmphoB if refractory.
rationale: WHO TRS 949 + Aronson IDSA 2017.

title: LF — IDA triple therapy where loa loa not co-endemic
recommendation: MDA: triple-drug IDA (ivermectin 200 mcg/kg + DEC 6 mg/kg + albendazole 400 mg) where loa NOT co-endemic; DA elsewhere. Loa loa co-endemic: albendazole twice yearly + vector control. Chronic LE: daily hygiene + skin care + elevation + compression + footwear; treat ADL with antibiotic. Hydrocele surgery at district level.
rationale: WHO GPELF + Triple-Drug Therapy 2017.

title: Onchocerciasis — ivermectin annual/biannual; doxycycline if loa co-endemic
indicators: chronic pruritus + nodules / skin lichenification in endemic area
recommendation: Confirm skin snip / Ov16 / slit-lamp. Ivermectin 150 mcg/kg PO annual (biannual in active transmission per WHO 2023) × 10–15 years. Loa co-endemic + mLOA > 8000/ml: doxycycline 100–200 mg/d × 4–6 wk (Wolbachia). Eye care for vision-threatening sequelae. MDA via ESPEN.
rationale: WHO Ivermectin position paper 2023 + Oncho Elimination 2021–2030.

title: Buruli ulcer — rifampicin + clarithromycin × 8 weeks
indicators: painless undermined ulcer in child / endemic area
recommendation: PCR IS2404 confirmation. Rifampicin 10 mg/kg/d + clarithromycin 7.5 mg/kg BD × 8 weeks (WHO 2017 — replaced streptomycin). Wound care + minimal debridement only; skin grafting after antibiotic completion. Physio + splinting to prevent contractures. Manage paradoxical reaction supportively.
rationale: WHO Mycobacterium ulcerans 2012/2017.

title: Hydatid — albendazole + WHO staging (CE1-CE5) + PAIR / surgery
indicators: cystic liver / lung mass + serology / endemic exposure
recommendation: WHO cyst staging. CE1/CE3a < 5 cm: albendazole 10–15 mg/kg/d × 3–6 mo or PAIR with hypertonic saline scolicide. CE2/CE3b complex: surgery (cystectomy/pericystectomy) + albendazole 4 d pre + 1 mo post. CE4/CE5 inactive: watch + wait. Pre-op albendazole reduces recurrence. Anti-spill technique mandatory; anaphylaxis precautions.
rationale: WHO IWGE consensus + Kenya Hydatid Control (Turkana).

title: NCC viable cysts — albendazole + dexa ± praziquantel; AEDs for seizures
indicators: adult-onset seizures + ring lesions on imaging
recommendation: Del Brutto criteria + serology. Parenchymal viable: albendazole 15 mg/kg/d BD × 10–14 d + dexamethasone 6 mg/d BEFORE + during; add praziquantel 50 mg/kg/d × 10 d if ≥ 2 cysts. AED for seizures (carbamazepine / levetiracetam). Intraventricular / giant subarachnoid: neurosurgery + prolonged albendazole. Calcified only: AED, NO cysticidal. Ocular cyst: surgery only.
rationale: IDSA NCC Guidelines 2017 + Garcia NEJM 2014.

title: Schistosomiasis — praziquantel 40 mg/kg single dose + MDA + screen FGS
recommendation: Praziquantel 40 mg/kg PO single dose (60 mg/kg in 2 doses for S. japonicum). MDA via school programmes when prevalence > 10%. Katayama: praziquantel + steroid. FGS — treat + counsel HIV risk + fertility. Hepatosplenic: praziquantel + variceal banding. Neuroschisto: praziquantel + dexamethasone. Bladder cystoscopy surveillance if long-standing urinary.
rationale: WHO Schistosomiasis Preventive Chemotherapy 2022.

title: STH — albendazole + MDA + iron-folate adolescent girls
recommendation: Albendazole 400 mg single dose (or mebendazole 500 mg) covers all three. MDA pre-school 6-monthly + school annual/biannual. WRA twice yearly where prevalence > 20% (safe after 1st trimester pregnancy). Iron-folate for anaemic / adolescent girls. WASH + footwear (hookworm). Kenya NSBDP.
rationale: WHO Preventive Chemotherapy STH 2022.

title: Suspected Lassa — IV ribavirin + barrier nursing + IDSR notify
recommendation: Strict barrier nursing — dedicated isolation, full PPE. RT-PCR at BSL3 (KEMRI). IV ribavirin 30 mg/kg loading then 16 mg/kg q6h × 4 d then 8 mg/kg q8h × 6 d (most effective within first 6 d). Pregnancy — balance teratogenicity vs maternal mortality. Ring contact tracing 21 d. Notify IDSR + WHO IHR. PEP ribavirin for high-risk exposed.
rationale: WHO Lassa Clinical Management + Nigeria CDC.

title: Mpox — isolate + supportive; tecovirimat for severe / immunocompromised
recommendation: PCR lesion swab. Standard + contact + droplet precautions until all lesions crusted. Supportive — analgesia, fluids, wound care, antibiotic if cellulitis. Severe / immunocompromised / paediatric / pregnancy: tecovirimat via MEURI / outbreak protocols. HIV + STI testing all. Contact tracing 21 d. MVA-BN vaccine pre- + post-exposure for high-risk. Notify IDSR + WHO.
rationale: WHO Mpox Clinical Guidelines 2024 + Africa CDC + Kenya MOH Plan 2024.

title: Trachoma — SAFE strategy + azithromycin MDA + TT surgery
indicators: TF in child community / trichiasis adult / endemic area
recommendation: SAFE: TT surgery (bilamellar tarsal rotation by trained OCO); azithromycin 20 mg/kg single dose annually × 3–5 yrs MDA where TF ≥ 5% in 1–9 yrs (Pfizer ITI donation); facial cleanliness; environmental — latrines + water + fly control. Validation as PHP elimination via WHO GET2030 dossier process.
rationale: WHO Alliance for Global Elimination of Trachoma 2030.

title: Pre-op — ASA + RCRI + functional capacity + optimise
recommendation: Risk-stratify: ASA + RCRI + NSQIP + DASI. Optimise BP, glucose, Hb, smoking cessation 4 wk pre. Continue β-blockers, statins. Bridge DOAC 24–72h, warfarin INR < 1.5. Stop SGLT2i 3 d. Cardiac stress test ONLY if poor METs + intermediate-high risk + would change management. Echo if known/suspected severe valve / PHT / HF. Frailty screening; prehabilitation. Postpone elective if uncontrolled medical issue.
rationale: ESC/ESA 2022 + ACC/AHA 2024 + RCoA GPAS.

title: RSI — 7 Ps + ketamine/etomidate + rocuronium; optimise haemodynamics first
recommendation: LEMON airway assessment + Plan A/B/C/D. Preoxygenate 3 min ± NIV; apnoeic O2 nasal 15 L. Optimise BP/shock FIRST (fluid + push-dose phenylephrine/adrenaline). Induce: ketamine 1–2 mg/kg (preferred in shock/asthma) or etomidate 0.3 mg/kg; paralyse with rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg (preferred — sugammadex reversible) or sux 1.5 mg/kg (avoid hyperK+ / burns / NMS). VL preferred. Capnography mandatory. Failed: DAS algorithm.
rationale: DAS 2015 + Walls Manual.

title: Spinal anaesthesia — co-load + phenylephrine + 25–27G pencil-point
recommendation: Verify no contraindication (anticoagulation timing per ESRA, infection, raised ICP, severe AS, refusal). 25–27G pencil-point needle. Hyperbaric bupivacaine 0.5% 2–3 ml ± fentanyl 15 mcg ± morphine 100 mcg for C-section. CO-LOAD crystalloid 10–15 ml/kg at intrathecal injection; phenylephrine 50–100 mcg/min infusion (NOT ephedrine in obstetric). Maintain MAP > 65 (obstetric > 90). PDPH: hydration/caffeine; epidural blood patch if severe. SPINAL HAEMATOMA after neuraxial = MRI + neurosurgery within 8h.
rationale: RCoA + ESRA 2022.

title: Post-op pain — multimodal: paracetamol + NSAID + regional + opioid sparing
recommendation: Baseline paracetamol 1 g q6h + NSAID (ibuprofen 400 q8h or ketorolac 10 q6h, contraindicated CKD/GIB/asthma/CV). Regional block when possible (TAP, fascia iliaca, popliteal, interscalene). Adjuvants: dexamethasone 4–8 mg pre, ketamine 0.1–0.25 mg/kg ± infusion 0.1 mg/kg/h, IV lidocaine for laparotomy. Opioid for severe — PCA morphine 1 mg/5 min; minimise discharge opioids (< 3 d). Persistent post-surgical pain > 6 wk + NRS > 4: refer chronic pain.
rationale: ASA 2017 + PROSPECT + ERAS.

title: MH crisis — stop trigger + dantrolene 2.5 mg/kg + cool + treat hyperK+
recommendation: EMERGENCY. Stop volatile + sux. 100% O2 high flow. Switch to TIVA. DANTROLENE 2.5 mg/kg IV bolus, repeat q5 min up to 10 mg/kg cumulative. Active cool to 38°C (cold IV fluids + ice packs + lavage). Treat hyperK+ (Ca, insulin/glucose, salbutamol, bicarb, dialysis). Amiodarone for arrhythmia (NOT CCB). UO > 2 ml/kg/h, treat rhabdo. ICU 24h+ (recrudescence 25%). Continue dantrolene 1 mg/kg q4–6h × 24h. Family counsel + MHAUS registry + MedicAlert.
rationale: AAGBI MH 2020 + MHAUS.

title: LAST — stop, secure airway, lipid emulsion 20% rescue
indicators: seizure or arrhythmia after LA injection
recommendation: STOP injection. 100% O2, intubate if needed. Seizures: benzo (midazolam) NOT propofol if unstable. LIPID 20%: bolus 1.5 ml/kg over 1 min, infusion 0.25 ml/kg/min, repeat bolus × 2, max 12 ml/kg cumulative. Cardiac arrest: ACLS with REDUCED adrenaline (< 1 mcg/kg), NO vasopressin/CCB/β-blocker/lidocaine; amiodarone for VF. Consider ECMO. Prolonged CPR may eventually respond. Register with LAST registry. Prevent: dose limits, aspiration q3–5 ml, US guidance, adrenaline marker, monitor 30 min post.
rationale: AAGBI LAST 2020 + ASRA 2020.

title: PONV — Apfel risk + multimodal prophylaxis
recommendation: Apfel score 0–4. Mod 2 agents, high ≥ 3 agents from different classes + TIVA. Combine: 5-HT3 (ondansetron 4 mg end of surgery), dexamethasone 4–8 mg at induction, droperidol 0.625 mg (ECG), aprepitant 40 mg if high risk, scopolamine patch (motion sickness). TIVA propofol > volatile; avoid N2O > 1h; minimise opioids; hydrate 10–15 ml/kg. Rescue: different class from prophylaxis (don't repeat ondansetron in 6h). Avoid metoclopramide in young women (EPS).
rationale: SAMBA 4th consensus 2020.

title: PBM — IV iron pre-op + TXA + restrictive transfusion (Hb 70/80)
indicators: surgical patient with anaemia / major bleed risk
recommendation: Pre-op anaemia: ferritin + B12/folate 4 wk pre; IV iron (ferric carboxymaltose 1 g) for IDA; EPO if Hb < 130 men/120 women + no contraindication; defer elective if Hb < 100. Intra-op: TXA 1 g IV at induction + repeat at 3h (CRASH-2/WOMAN/HALT-IT), cell salvage where appropriate. Restrictive transfusion: RBC < 70 (or < 80 if CV/symptomatic), single-unit + reassess. Platelets per threshold (< 10, < 20, < 50, < 100). FFP only with active bleed + INR > 1.5 or fibrinogen < 1.5. Massive haemorrhage: 1:1:1 RBC:FFP:platelets + TXA + Ca + viscoelastic.
rationale: NICE NG24 + PBM modules.

title: Chronic non-cancer pain — biopsychosocial + opioid stewardship
recommendation: Biopsychosocial — non-pharm (exercise, CBT, sleep, weight) first; pharm by mechanism: paracetamol+NSAID for nociceptive, TCA/SNRI/gabapentinoid for neuropathic, SNRI+pregabalin for nociplastic. Opioid LAST RESORT, time-limited trial, MME < 50, naloxone co-prescribed > 50 MME, avoid concurrent BZD. Taper 10%/month for chronic. OUD: refer for MAT (methadone/buprenorphine). Mental health screen (PHQ-9/GAD-7). Function-based goals.
rationale: CDC 2022 + NICE NG193.

title: Opioid overdose — BVM + naloxone titrated to RR + observe
recommendation: AIRWAY + BVM 10 L O2 (hypoxia kills, not arrest). Naloxone 0.4 mg IV q2–3 min titrate to RR > 12 (NOT consciousness); 4 mg IN by lay rescuer; up to 10 mg for fentanyl. Observe 4–6h heroin, 24h+ for methadone/SR/fentanyl patch. Treat aspiration, ARDS, rhabdo, AKI. Initiate buprenorphine in ED + linkage to MAT. Take-home naloxone + bystander training. Suicide + mental health assessment. Safer-use education.
rationale: WHO Opioid Overdose Management 2014 + SAMHSA Toolkit.

title: PSA — pre-checklist + dedicated observer + capnography + reversal ready
recommendation: Pre: AMPLE + fasting + ASA + airway (LEMON) + consent + crash trolley + naloxone/flumazenil drawn up + dedicated observer. Monitoring: SpO2 + capnography + ECG + NIBP. Drug choice: ketamine 1 mg/kg IV (preserves airway, ideal paeds/asthma/shock — co-give ondansetron); propofol 0.5–1 mg/kg titrated; ketofol mix; midazolam 1–2 mg + fentanyl 0.5–1 mcg/kg; dexmedetomidine for resp-spare. Stop if airway/circulation compromise. Recovery: Aldrete ≥ 9, no driving × 24h.
rationale: ACEP 2021 + RCEM 2021 + AAGBI Safe Sedation 2021.

title: PPD — EPDS at 6 weeks + CBT/IPT + sertraline if mod-severe
recommendation: EPDS screen at 6 wk + 3/6/12 mo. Item 10 positive = immediate suicide assessment. Mild–mod: CBT / IPT + psychoeducation + social support + sleep + exercise. Mod–severe: sertraline 50–100 mg/d (lowest infant exposure breastfeeding) + CBT. Continue 6–12 mo. AVOID fluoxetine first-line breastfeeding (long half-life). Psychotic / suicidal / infanticide ideation = EMERGENCY admit + antipsychotic. Postpartum psychosis: olanzapine + mood stabiliser + admit MBU. Brexanolone / zuranolone for severe where available. Assess partner. WHO Thinking Healthy for CHV in LMIC.
rationale: NICE CG192 + WHO mhGAP + Thinking Healthy Lancet 2008.

title: Maternal sepsis — Sepsis-Six + source control + omqSOFA
recommendation: Within 1 h: O2 to SpO2 ≥ 94%, blood cultures BEFORE antibiotics, broad-spectrum (pip-tazo 4.5 g q8h or ceftriaxone 2 g + metronidazole 500 mg q8h; add clindamycin if GAS/TSS), crystalloid 30 ml/kg, lactate, UO. Source control 6–12h (evacuate retained products, drain abscess, debride wound, expedite delivery if intrauterine source). Noradrenaline if persistent hypotension (MAP ≥ 65). ICU for severe. VTE prophylaxis LMWH. omqSOFA score (GCS<15, RR>25, SBP<90 = sepsis). Notify MDR if death.
rationale: WHO Maternal Sepsis 2017 + RCOG GTG 64a/b + Surviving Sepsis 2021.

title: Eclampsia / severe PE — MgSO4 + BP control + delivery + 24h post
recommendation: MgSO4 loading 4 g IV over 5–10 min + 1 g/h maintenance × 24h post-delivery / last seizure (or IM 5 g each buttock + 5 g q4h). Calcium gluconate 1 g antidote bedside. Severe HTN: labetalol 20 mg IV doubling q10 min or hydralazine 5 mg q20 min or nifedipine 10 mg PO (NOT SL); target SBP 140–155. CAUTIOUS fluids (80 ml/h). DELIVERY after stabilisation: ≥ 34 wk deliver, 24–33+6 corticosteroids + plan, < 24 counsel termination if severe. VTE prophylaxis post. Aspirin 75–150 mg from 12 wk next pregnancy + calcium 1.5–2 g/d in low-calcium populations.
rationale: WHO PE/E 2011 + MAGPIE Lancet 2002 + RCOG GTG 10A.

title: GDM — 75g OGTT 24–28 wk + diet then metformin/insulin + 6-12 wk OGTT
recommendation: 75 g OGTT 24–28 wk: WHO/IADPSG cutoffs FBG ≥ 5.1, 1h ≥ 10.0, 2h ≥ 8.5. Pre-existing if FBG ≥ 7 / random ≥ 11.1 / HbA1c ≥ 48 at booking. Diet + exercise first; targets FBG < 5.3, 1h post < 7.8. If targets not met 1–2 wk: metformin 500 mg BD up to 2 g (first-line PO, safe per MiG); add/use insulin (NPH bedtime + rapid prandial). Aspirin 75–150 mg from 12 wk (PE prevention). Growth scans 4-weekly from 28. Deliver by 38–39 wk insulin-controlled / 40+6 diet-only. C-section if EFW > 4.5 kg. Stop meds at delivery, breastfeed, OGTT 6–12 wk postpartum + annual diabetes screen.
rationale: WHO 2013 + NICE NG3 + ACOG 190.

title: Pregnancy/postpartum VTE prophylaxis — risk-stratify + LMWH
indicators: pregnancy with VTE risk factors / postpartum
recommendation: RCOG risk score at booking, antenatal admission, postpartum. Antenatal ≥ 4 RFs = LMWH from 1st trimester; 3 RFs = from 28 wk. Postpartum ≥ 2 RFs / any major = LMWH × 6 wk; C-section 10 d minimum. Enoxaparin 40 mg OD (50–90 kg); 1 mg/kg BD for treatment of confirmed VTE. AVOID warfarin (teratogenic) + DOACs (no safety data) in pregnancy. Stop LMWH 24h before planned delivery / regional, restart 6–12h post if no bleed. Massive PE: thrombolysis. Mechanical: TEDS + IPC + mobilise. D-dimer NOT reliable. Imaging: compression US for DVT, CTPA for PE.
rationale: RCOG GTG 37a/b 2015 + ACCP CHEST.

title: Shoulder dystocia — HELPERR sequential manoeuvres + deliver in 5 min
indicators: turtle sign + failure to deliver shoulders
recommendation: Call HELP (sr obs + paeds + anaesth + scribe + clock). HELPERR sequence (30 sec each): Evaluate episiotomy, Legs McRobert's (resolves 40%), Pressure suprapubic (NOT fundal — adds 20%), Enter Rubin II / Wood's screw rotations, Remove posterior arm, Roll all-fours. Last resort: cleidotomy, symphysiotomy (Kenya MOH where C-section unavailable), Zavanelli. Post: cord gases, examine baby (Erb's, fractures), refer paeds, examine mother (tears, PPH high risk after dystocia), debrief team + family. PROMPT skill drills regularly.
rationale: RCOG GTG 42 + PROMPT + ALSO.

title: ANC — WHO 8-contact + Linda Mama booking essentials
recommendation: WHO 8-contact: < 12 wk, 20, 26, 30, 34, 36, 38, 40. Booking: history + dating scan + bloods (FBC, BG/Rh, HIV, syphilis, HBsAg, rubella, sickle); folic acid 5 mg + IFA 60+0.4 mg + calcium 1.5–2 g/d (low-Ca SSA — WHO 2018); aspirin 75–150 mg from 12 wk if PE high-risk (USPSTF); IPTp-SP × 3 in moderate-high malaria transmission; Td booster; HIV ART for PMTCT; counsel danger signs + skilled birth + Linda Mama. Ongoing: BP + urinalysis + fundal height + fetal movements; anomaly scan 18–22 wk; GDM 24–28; anti-D 28+34; ECV for breech ≥ 36 wk; Tdap 28–36 wk.
rationale: WHO ANC 2016 + Kenya Linda Mama + WHO Calcium 2018 + IPTp-SP.

title: Intrapartum — WHO Labour Care Guide + DR C BRaVADO + AMTSL
recommendation: WHO Labour Care Guide 2020 — woman-centred decisions; active labour from 5 cm (not 4). Low-risk fetal monitoring: intermittent Doppler every 15 min stage 1, every 5 min stage 2. High-risk: continuous CTG with DR C BRaVADO. Concerning CTG: left lateral + IV fluid + stop oxytocin + tocolysis if hyperstim + exclude cord prolapse + expedite if persistent. GBS IAP if indicated (penicillin G). AMTSL: oxytocin 10 IU IM within 1 min + delayed cord clamping ≥ 1 min + controlled cord traction + uterine massage. Skin-to-skin + early breastfeeding. Companion of choice + respectful care.
rationale: WHO Labour Care Guide 2020 + NICE NG235 + Kenya MOH Quality of Care.

title: PPROM — corticosteroids + erythromycin + MgSO4 + deliver at 34
recommendation: Sterile speculum (NO digital exam). PPROM (< 37 wk): admit + monitor for chorio. Corticosteroids 24–34+6 wk: betamethasone 12 mg × 2 / dexa 6 mg × 4. Erythromycin 250 mg QDS × 10 d (ORACLE I); AVOID amoxiclav (NEC). MgSO4 neuroprotection < 32 wk if imminent delivery (4 g + 1 g/h × 24h). Tocolysis NOT routine. Monitor temp, FBC, CRP, CTG. Deliver at 34+0 (or per PPROMT 34–36 wk) OR if chorio / fetal distress / abruption. Term PROM (≥ 37 wk): induce + antibiotics if > 18h not delivered. Antibiotic GBS prophylaxis per protocol.
rationale: RCOG GTG 73 + ORACLE I + PPROMT + WHO Preterm.

title: Postpartum mental health — screen + treat spectrum (blues→PPD→psychosis)
recommendation: EPDS 6 wk + 3/6/12 mo. Baby blues: education + rescreen 2 wk. PPD mod–severe: sertraline + CBT. PP psychosis: EMERGENCY admit + olanzapine/risperidone ± lithium (mood stabiliser if bipolar; AVOID valproate WCBP). ECT for severe refractory. OCD intrusive: CBT + SSRI. Birth PTSD: trauma-focused CBT + EMDR. Bipolar: postpartum prophylaxis CRITICAL — restart mood stabiliser. Partner screen too (10% paternal PPD). Most psychotropics compatible breastfeeding (LactMed). Brexanolone/zuranolone for severe PPD where available.
rationale: NICE CG192 + ACOG 757 + WHO mhGAP.

title: HFrEF — 4 pillars (ARNI + β-blocker + MRA + SGLT2i)
recommendation: Initiate all 4 pillars: ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan, 36h washout if switching from ACE-i) > ACE-i/ARB; HF-specific β-blocker (bisoprolol/carvedilol/metoprolol succinate/nebivolol); MRA (spironolactone/eplerenone — monitor K+); SGLT2i (dapa 10/empa 10 — irrespective of DM). Loop diuretic for congestion. Add ivabradine if HR > 70 SR on max β-blocker; hydralazine+nitrate for African ancestry or ACE-i intolerant; IV iron if Fe deficient; vericiguat for worsening; tafamidis for ATTR amyloid. CRT if LBBB + QRS ≥ 130 + EF ≤ 35 + NYHA II–IV. ICD post-MI ≥ 40d EF ≤ 35 + NYHA II–III. Advanced: LVAD / transplant; palliation. Heart failure education + cardiac rehab.
rationale: ESC HF 2021/2023 + ACC/AHA/HFSA 2022 + PARADIGM-HF + DAPA-HF + EMPEROR-Reduced.

title: HFpEF — SGLT2i + MRA + treat comorbidities (HTN, AF, obesity, OSA)
indicators: LVEF ≥ 50% + HF symptoms + raised filling pressures
recommendation: SGLT2i (DELIVER, EMPEROR-Preserved) reduces HF hospitalisation across full EF. MRA (spironolactone) lower-EF HFpEF (TOPCAT); finerenone (FINEARTS-HF). ARNI marginal benefit lower EF range (PARAGON-HF). Loop diuretic for congestion. Aggressive HTN control < 130/80; AF rhythm control; SGLT2i+/-GLP1-RA for DM; tafamidis for ATTR-CM; semaglutide for obesity (STEP-HFpEF); CPAP for OSA. AVOID nitrate routinely. Cardiac rehab. Workup amyloid if low voltage + raised LV mass + low BP.
rationale: ESC HF 2023 + DELIVER + EMPEROR-Preserved + FINEARTS-HF 2024 + STEP-HFpEF.

title: AF — CHA2DS2-VASc anticoag + DOAC preferred + rate/rhythm
recommendation: Anticoagulate if CHA2DS2-VASc ≥ 2 (≥ 1 men, ≥ 2 women). DOAC PREFERRED — apixaban 5 mg BD (2.5 if 2/3 of: age≥80, Cr≥133, wt≤60) / rivaroxaban 20 OD / dabigatran 150 BD / edoxaban 60 OD. Warfarin only if mechanical valve, mitral stenosis, eGFR < 15. LAAC if anticoag contraindicated. Rate: β-blocker / diltiazem (avoid DTZ in HFrEF); target HR < 110 lenient / < 80 strict. Rhythm: cardioversion (anticoag 3wk pre + 4 wk post or TOE); amiodarone or flecainide; catheter ablation increasingly first-line for symptomatic paroxysmal AF + HFrEF (CASTLE-AF, EAST-AFNET 4). Acute unstable: sync cardioversion. AF+ACS triple→DOAC+P2Y12. Treat OSA, BP, ETOH, weight.
rationale: ESC AF 2024 + ACC/AHA 2023 + EAST-AFNET 4 + DOAC trials.

title: Stable angina — β-blocker first-line + secondary prevention (A-B-C-S)
recommendation: Anti-anginal: β-blocker OR non-DHP CCB first-line; GTN SL for acute + prophylaxis. Second-line: long-acting nitrate, DHP CCB, ivabradine (SR HR>70), nicorandil, ranolazine. Secondary prevention: aspirin 75–100 mg + STATIN high-intensity (atorva 80/rosuva 20–40) target LDL < 1.4 (+/- ezetimibe + PCSK9i + inclisiran); ACE-i/ARB; tight BP < 130/80; cardiac rehab. ICOSAPENT ETHYL if TG 1.5–5.6 despite statin (REDUCE-IT). DAPT 6–12 mo post-PCI (3 mo if high bleeding). Revasc for refractory / left main / 3VD-DM (heart team). Vaccinations (flu reduces CV events). Lifestyle: smoking cessation #1.
rationale: ESC CCS 2024 + ACC/AHA 2023 + ESC Dyslipidaemia 2019.

title: Resistant HTN — confirm, optimise, add spironolactone (PATHWAY-2)
recommendation: Confirm true resistant: ABPM (rule out white coat), adherence (DOT/urine screen), stop interfering meds (NSAID/OCP/decongestant). Optimise ACE/ARB + CCB + thiazide-like at max doses. Add SPIRONOLACTONE 25→50 mg (PATHWAY-2, monitor K+/Cr). If K+ > 5.5: bisoprolol or doxazosin or clonidine. Eplerenone alternative. Workup secondary: aldosterone/renin, metanephrines, salivary/24h cortisol, renal Doppler/CTA, polysomnography, TSH. Treat cause (PA → adrenalectomy / spiro; phaeo → α then β then surgery; OSA → CPAP). Refractory: aprocitentan, central agents, renal denervation, refer tertiary.
rationale: ESC/ESH 2024 + PATHWAY-2 Lancet 2015 + NICE NG136.

title: Acute stroke — alteplase 0–4.5h + thrombectomy up to 24h LVO
recommendation: Door-to-CT < 25 min; CT brain to exclude haemorrhage + CTA for LVO. Alteplase 0.9 mg/kg max 90 (10% bolus + 90% over 60 min) within 4.5h (extended to 9h or wake-up with imaging selection — EXTEND, WAKE-UP). Tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg single bolus emerging. THROMBECTOMY for LVO within 6h standard; 6–24h with penumbra mismatch (DAWN, DEFUSE 3); basilar up to 24h (BAOCHE, ATTENTION). Pre-tPA BP < 185/110 (labetalol/hydralazine/nicardipine); post-tPA < 180/105 × 24h. Stroke unit. Aspirin 300 mg within 48h (24h after tPA). Statin high-intensity. Decompressive hemicraniectomy for malignant MCA < 60 yr. Secondary: DAPT 21 d minor stroke/high-risk TIA (CHANCE/POINT), DOAC for AF, carotid revasc for symptomatic > 50% within 2 wk.
rationale: AHA/ASA 2024 + ESO 2023 + DAWN/DEFUSE 3 + BAOCHE 2022.

title: Cardiac arrest — ACLS + reverse causes + post-ROSC care
recommendation: High-quality CPR 100–120/min depth 5–6 cm, < 10 sec interruptions; early defibrillation 150–200 J biphasic VF/VT; adrenaline 1 mg q3–5 min; amiodarone 300 mg after 3rd shock. Reverse 4Hs + 4Ts. Calcium for hyperK/Mg/CCB/β-blocker; bicarb for hyperK/TCA/ASA; lipid for LA; tPA 50 mg for PE; TXA for haemorrhage; naloxone for opioid. Capnography mandatory after advanced airway. Pregnancy: LLT + perimortem C-section by 4 min if not ROSC + ≥ 20 wk. Post-ROSC: SpO2 92–98% (avoid hyperO2), normocapnia, MAP ≥ 65, glucose 7.8–10, TTM normothermia/33–36° × 24h (TTM2 — current most do normothermia + fever prevention), EEG, urgent angio if STEMI, neuroprognostication NOT before 72h multimodal.

title: PE — DOAC for most, thrombolysis for high-risk, sPESI to outpatient
recommendation: Risk-stratify sPESI/Hestia + RV dysfunction + troponin. Anticoag: DOAC (apixaban 10 BD × 7 d then 5 BD; riva 15 BD × 21 d then 20 OD; or LMWH lead-in for edoxaban/dabigatran). LMWH for cancer + pregnancy. Massive/high-risk (shock): alteplase 100 mg IV over 2h (or surgical embolectomy / CDT). Intermediate-high (RV+ troponin+): close monitor HDU, anticoag, ?CDT. Low-risk (sPESI 0/Hestia neg): outpatient DOAC + same-day discharge (HoT-PE). Duration: 3 mo provoked; extended indefinitely unprovoked (reduced-dose apixaban 2.5 BD / riva 10 OD AMPLIFY-EXT/EINSTEIN-CHOICE); ≥ 6 mo cancer. IVC filter only if anticoag contraindicated. 3-mo follow-up — CTEPH workup if symptomatic.
rationale: ESC PE 2019/2025 + ACCP 2021 + Hokusai-Cancer + AMPLIFY-EXT.

title: Hypertensive emergency — gradual BP reduction (25%/1h) per end-organ
recommendation: ICU/HDU + arterial line. Reduce MAP 10–20% in 1h then to 160/100 over 2–6h. EXCEPTIONS: dissection target SBP < 120 + HR < 60 (β-blocker FIRST); ischaemic stroke pre-tPA < 185/110; eclampsia 140–155/90–105. IV agents: labetalol (preferred — most), nicardipine, hydralazine (pregnancy), nitroprusside (rapid + cyanide watch > 24h), GTN (pulm oedema/ACS), esmolol (dissection/phaeo), phentolamine (phaeo/cocaine), MgSO4 (eclampsia). URGENCY (no EOD): oral therapy + gradual reduction over 24–48h. AVOID SL nifedipine / hydralazine boluses. Investigate secondary cause.
rationale: ESC/ESH 2024 + AHA Statement 2022 + ACC/AHA 2024.

title: Aortic dissection — β-blocker FIRST + Stanford A surgery / B medical/TEVAR
indicators: tearing chest/back pain + pulse asymmetry / new AR
recommendation: ADD-RS → urgent CT aorta. β-BLOCKER FIRST (labetalol IV / esmolol) to HR < 60 BEFORE vasodilator (avoid reflex tachy). Then vasodilator (nitroprusside / nicardipine) for SBP 100–120. Pain control. Group + crossmatch 4–6 units. STANFORD A (ascending) → IMMEDIATE cardiothoracic surgery (80% survival vs 20% medical). STANFORD B (descending) uncomplicated → medical + long-term BP < 130/80; complicated → TEVAR > open. Pregnancy: emergency repair + delivery (C-section first if ≥ 28 wk). Long-term: lifelong BP control + surveillance + genetic counsel for connective tissue (Marfan → losartan, root replace at 5 cm).
rationale: ESC Aortic 2014/2024 + ACC/AHA 2022 + INSTEAD.

title: T2DM 2024 — GLP-1 RA / SGLT2i first-line by comorbidity (not just A1c)
recommendation: Individualised HbA1c (53 most, 48 young, 58 elderly, 64 frail). Therapy by comorbidity: ASCVD/high-CV → GLP-1 RA (semaglutide/liraglutide) ± SGLT2i; HF/CKD with albuminuria → SGLT2i (dapa/empa) first; no comorbidity → metformin then add. Combine for multiple targets. Tirzepatide most potent A1c + weight. CONTRAINDICATIONS: GLP-1RA in MEN2/MTC; SGLT2i hold for surgery 3 d (euglycaemic DKA). BP < 130/80 (ACE-i/ARB if ACR > 3), statin (atorva 20 if > 40 + DM), aspirin secondary prevention. Annual: HbA1c, BP, lipids, eGFR + ACR, retina, foot, depression. Remission possible with > 10–15% weight loss; bariatric if BMI ≥ 35 + DM.
rationale: ADA 2024/2025 + EASD 2022 + LEADER/REWIND/EMPA-REG/DECLARE/FLOW.

title: Obesity — chronic disease + GLP-1 RA / tirzepatide / bariatric
recommendation: Chronic relapsing disease framing — long-term treatment. EOSS stage. Foundation: nutrition + exercise ≥ 200 min/wk + behavioural CBT + sleep. Pharmacotherapy: semaglutide 2.4 mg SC weekly (~15% wt loss STEP) or tirzepatide 15 mg SC weekly (~22% SURMOUNT-1, superior in SURMOUNT-5). Liraglutide 3 mg, phentermine/topiramate, naltrexone/bupropion alternatives. Bariatric for BMI ≥ 35 + comorbidity / ≥ 40 (sleeve / RYGB / BPD) — multidisciplinary prep, lifelong micronutrient. Paeds: liraglutide / semaglutide ≥ 12 yr (STEP TEENS). SELECT 2023 — semaglutide reduces MACE in obesity without DM. Address stigma; advocate for affordable access in SSA.
rationale: ADA/Obesity Soc 2024 + WHO 2022 + SURMOUNT/STEP/SELECT.

title: CKD 2024 — ACE-i/ARB + SGLT2i + finerenone + GLP-1 RA (4 pillars)
recommendation: BP < 130/80; salt < 5 g/d; avoid NSAIDs. 4 PILLARS: ACE-i/ARB max tolerated (monitor K + Cr); SGLT2i (dapa 10 / empa 10) for ACR > 200 + eGFR > 20 (DAPA-CKD/EMPA-KIDNEY without diabetes); FINERENONE 10–20 mg if T2DM + albuminuria (FIDELIO/FIGARO); GLP-1 RA semaglutide for T2DM+CKD (FLOW 2024). Anaemia: IV iron then ESA target Hb 100–115. CKD-MBD: phosphate binder + active vit D + cinacalcet. Acidosis: NaHCO3 if HCO3 < 22. Hyperkalaemia: diet + patiromer/SZC to maintain RAAS. REFER eGFR < 30 / ACR > 700 / rapidly progressive. Statin from age 50.
rationale: KDIGO 2024 + DAPA-CKD + EMPA-KIDNEY + FIDELIO/FIGARO + FLOW.

title: DKA — fluid + FRIII insulin + continue basal + KCl per level
recommendation: 0.9% saline 1L/1h, 1L/2h, 1L/4h, 1L/8h (slower elderly/cardiac). Switch to 0.45% + 5% dex when glucose < 14. FRIII 0.1 U/kg/h capped 50 kg max 5 U/h; CONTINUE long-acting basal from start (reduces rebound). Target: ketones fall 0.5/h, HCO3 rise 3/h, glucose fall 3/h. K+: > 5.5 none, 3.5–5.5 add 40 mmol KCl/L, < 3.5 HOLD insulin until replaced. NO routine bicarb (only pH < 7 + shock). Switch SC when ketones < 0.3, pH > 7.3, eating + overlap 1h. Euglycaemic DKA (SGLT2i): start dex early. PAEDIATRIC: slower fluid (cerebral oedema risk), no rapid bolus > 10 ml/kg unless shock, monitor GCS, mannitol if cerebral oedema. Treat trigger.
rationale: JBDS 2023 + ADA 2024 + ISPAD 2022 + PECARN.

title: Thyroid storm — multidrug (β-blocker + PTU + iodine + steroid + cholestyramine)
recommendation: ICU. Fluids + active cooling (NOT aspirin). Multidrug IN SEQUENCE: 1) Propranolol 60–120 mg PO q4–6h (or IV slow); 2) PTU 600 mg load then 200–300 mg q4–6h (preferred over methimazole — blocks T4→T3 peripherally); 3) Iodine (Lugol's / SSKI / NaI IV) ≥ 1 HOUR AFTER thionamide (avoids organification); 4) Hydrocortisone 100 mg IV q8h; 5) Cholestyramine 4 g QDS. Treat precipitant. Plasmapheresis for refractory. Definitive after acute: RAI ablation / thyroidectomy / long-term thionamide. PREGNANCY: PTU 1st trim, methimazole 2nd/3rd. AVOID iodine contrast in Graves'.
rationale: ATA 2016/2023 + Burch-Wartofsky + JES 2024.
