rationale: WHO 2022/2024 + Kenya NTP MDR-TB + TB-PRACTECAL + NIX-TB + ZeNix.

title: Syphilis — benzathine penicillin by stage; pregnancy desensitise NOT alternative
indicators: positive treponemal + non-treponemal serology / clinical lesion
recommendation: Treponemal (TPPA) + non-treponemal (RPR — quantitative for monitoring). LP if neuro/eye/ear symptoms OR late latent unknown duration OR HIV+ with RPR ≥ 1:32 OR treatment failure. PRIMARY/SECONDARY/EARLY LATENT (< 1 yr): benzathine penicillin 2.4 MU IM SINGLE DOSE; allergy + non-pregnant — doxycycline 100 BD × 14 d. LATE LATENT/TERTIARY: benzathine PEN 2.4 MU IM WEEKLY × 3 DOSES; allergy non-pregnant — doxycycline 100 BD × 28 d. NEUROSYPHILIS: aqueous penicillin G 18-24 MU/d IV × 10-14 d; allergy — ceftriaxone 2 g IV/d × 10-14 d; LP at 6/12/24 mo. PREGNANCY: BENZATHINE PENICILLIN ONLY — if reported allergy → DESENSITISE + admit, do NOT give alternative (fetal infection only treated by penicillin). Congenital: aqueous benzylpenicillin IV × 10 d. Jarisch-Herxheimer 24h after start (especially 1° + 2°) — paracetamol + fluids; pregnancy preterm risk. FOLLOW-UP RPR at 6/12/24 mo — 4-fold decline = response. Partner notification (90 d 1° / 6 mo 2° / 1 yr early latent). DOXY-PEP for MSM/TGW reduces syphilis 73% (DoxyPEP 2023). HIV+ — more aggressive + closer follow-up. Universal antenatal screening (Kenya Linda Mama) + Triple MTCT elimination.
rationale: WHO 2024 + CDC 2024 + Kenya STI Guidelines + BASHH + DoxyPEP NEJM 2023.

title: Gonorrhoea — ceftriaxone 500 mg IM single + azithromycin if chlamydia not excluded
recommendation: NAAT first-line (any exposed site). UNCOMPLICATED ANOGENITAL/PHARYNGEAL: ceftriaxone 500 mg IM single (CDC 2021 ↑ from 250 due to MIC trends). DUAL THERAPY with azithromycin 1 g if chlamydia not excluded; if chlamydia ruled out via NAAT — ceftriaxone monotherapy adequate (CDC 2021). Cefixime 800 mg PO alternative (less effective). True cephalosporin allergy: gentamicin 240 mg IM + azithromycin 2 g. DGI: admit + ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily × 7-14 d + joint drainage if septic arthritis. OPHTHALMIA NEONATORUM: ceftriaxone 25-50 mg/kg IV/IM single + saline irrigation + topical erythromycin; prevent universal eye prophylaxis (1% tetracycline / povidone-iodine at birth). PID: ceftriaxone 500 IM + doxycycline 100 BD × 14 d + metronidazole 500 BD × 14 d (outpatient); IV severe / TOA. Test of cure pharyngeal + rectal at 14 d (high failure). PARTNERS 60 d prior — examine + treat (EPT where legal). XDR-NG emerging — gentamicin + zoliflodacin (new) + ertapenem. Pregnancy: ceftriaxone + azithromycin; AVOID doxy/tetracycline/FQ. Doxy-PEP reduces gonorrhoea (less than chlamydia/syphilis but significant) — separate. Annual STI screen + PrEP candidates q3 mo. Notify Kenya STI surveillance.
rationale: WHO 2024 + CDC 2024 + Kenya STI Guidelines + BASHH + Global Action Plan NG AMR.

title: Chlamydia — doxycycline 100 BD × 7 d (LGV × 21 d); PID dual/triple
recommendation: NAAT first-line (any exposed site). UNCOMPLICATED: DOXYCYCLINE 100 mg BD × 7 d (CDC 2021 + WHO 2024 — preferred over azithromycin esp rectal + pharyngeal). Pregnancy: AZITHROMYCIN 1 g single (doxy contraindicated). LGV: doxycycline 100 BD × 21 d + drain bubo. PID outpatient (mild-moderate, no abscess, no pregnancy): ceftriaxone 500 IM + doxycycline 100 BD × 14 d + metronidazole 500 BD × 14 d; follow-up 48-72h; if no improvement → admit. PID inpatient (severe/pregnancy/TOA/fertility concern): IV ceftriaxone 2 g + doxycycline + metronidazole 500 q8h; switch PO when stable; complete 14 d; drain TOA > 4-6 cm. Pain + fluids. IUD usually leave (remove only if no improvement at 48-72h). Abstinence × 7 d + until partner treated. PARTNERS 60 d prior — examine + treat (EPT where legal). Test of cure: 3 wk pregnancy + 4 wk rectal/pharyngeal. RE-SCREEN at 3 months (high re-infection). Universal antenatal screening (Linda Mama). Annual screen sexually active < 25 women + high-risk. Vertical: infant conjunctivitis + pneumonia (azithromycin treat). DOXY-PEP for MSM/TGW reduces chlamydia 70% (DoxyPEP). Reactive arthritis post-chlamydia: NSAID + steroid + rheumatology.
rationale: WHO 2024 + CDC 2024 + Kenya STI Guidelines + BASHH + RCOG/IUSTI PID.

title: HPV — single-dose vaccine 9-14 (WHO 2022) + primary HPV screen 30-49 + screen+treat
indicators: women 30+ / HPV screening contact / abnormal smear / suspected cervical cancer
recommendation: PRIMARY PREVENTION: HPV vaccine 9-14 — SINGLE DOSE (WHO 2022 paradigm; Kenya MOH catch-up to 14; immunocompromised 3-dose); Gardasil 9 ideal (90% cervical cancer protection). Gender-neutral consider (boys benefit). SCREENING (WHO 2021): primary HPV DNA/mRNA (self-collection acceptable) every 5-10 yr general 30-49 (extended 25-65); HIV+ start age 25 every 3-5 yr (more aggressive); VIA + same-day cryotherapy/thermal ablation in LMIC. KENYA MOH: VIA + HPV q3 yr / annual HIV+. CIN 2-3 (HSIL): excision LLETZ/LEEP / thermal ablation if eligible; adenocarcinoma in situ → cold knife conization. INVASIVE: stage IA1 conization/simple hyst; IA2-IIA radical hyst + LND or chemoradiation; IIB-IVA chemoradiation (cisplatin + EBRT + brachytherapy gold standard); IVB/metastatic: chemo + PEMBROLIZUMAB (Keynote-826 NEJM 2023 — practice-changing). HIV+ cervical cancer is AIDS-defining + more aggressive. Pregnancy: defer treatment to PP unless invasive; if invasive — stage-specific modification. Genital warts: imiquimod / podophyllotoxin / cryotherapy. WHO 90-70-90 by 2030 + Kenya National Strategy 2022-2030.
rationale: WHO 2021/2024 + Kenya Strategy + Keynote-826 + WHO 90-70-90.

title: HSV — acyclovir first / recurrent / suppression; C-section if active at delivery
recommendation: PCR lesion swab (most sensitive) + type-specific serology for serodiscordant partners. ALWAYS: HIV + STI screen + syphilis. ACUTE FIRST EPISODE: acyclovir 400 TID × 7-10 d / valacyclovir 1 g BD / famciclovir 250 TID; severe IV acyclovir 5-10 mg/kg q8h. RECURRENT (start in prodrome): acyclovir 800 BD × 5 d OR valacyclovir 500 BD × 3 d OR famciclovir 1 g BD × 1 d. SUPPRESSION (≥ 6 recurrences/y or transmission concern): acyclovir 400 BD / valacyclovir 500-1000 daily / famciclovir 250 BD — reduces outbreaks 70-80% + transmission 50%. HIV+: higher dose suppression (valacyclovir 1 g BD); foscarnet for acyclovir resistance. PREGNANCY: acyclovir SAFE — suppression from 36 wk reduces lesions at delivery + C-section need. C-SECTION if active lesions / prodrome at labour. Neonatal HSV: IV acyclovir 60 mg/kg/d × 14 d (SEM) or × 21 d (CNS/disseminated) + suppression × 6 mo post (CASG). HSV encephalitis: empirical IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg q8h × 14-21 d for any suspected encephalitis. Eczema herpeticum: admit + IV acyclovir + skin care + ?bacterial cover. Counsel: lifelong, asymptomatic shedding, disclosure to partners, condoms reduce 50%, suppression + condoms reduce > 90% transmission, triggers (UV/stress/menses), pregnancy planning.
rationale: WHO 2024 + CDC 2024 + BASHH + RCOG + CASG.

title: Vaginal discharge — Amsel/wet mount; metronidazole / fluconazole / treat partner if Trich
recommendation: Wet mount + KOH + pH; NAAT for trichomonas (high sensitivity). HIV + STI screen. TRICHOMONAS: metronidazole 500 BD × 7 d (women — CDC 2021 preferred over 2 g single) or 2 g single (men); tinidazole alternative; AVOID alcohol; TREAT PARTNER (STI) + abstinence 7 d + re-test 3 mo. BV: metronidazole 500 BD × 7 d (or 0.75% gel intravaginal × 5 d / clindamycin); recurrent — gel 2×/wk × 4-6 mo + probiotic; not primarily STI; partner treatment generally not (lesbian women may benefit); pregnancy — metronidazole reduces preterm + PROM. CANDIDA uncomplicated: topical clotrimazole or fluconazole 150 mg single; recurrent (≥ 4/y) — fluconazole 150 mg q72h × 3 then weekly × 6 mo; non-albicans (glabrata/krusei) — boric acid 600 mg intravaginal × 14 d (fluconazole resistance); pregnancy — TOPICAL only (oral fluconazole 1st trim teratogenic); investigate cause (DM, antibiotic, immunosuppression). SYNDROMIC Kenya: vaginal discharge — ceftriaxone + doxycycline/azithromycin + metronidazole + fluconazole covers gonorrhoea + chlamydia + trich + BV + candida. Refractory: re-examine + culture + rule out atrophic / lichen / malignancy / foreign body. Pediatric vaginitis — consider abuse.
rationale: WHO 2024 + CDC 2024 + Kenya Syndromic + BASHH + FDA fluconazole pregnancy.

title: Appendicitis — Alvarado + early laparoscopic; antibiotic-first option (CODA)
indicators: RLQ pain + Alvarado / Lipase / CT positive
recommendation: Alvarado score + WBC + CRP. US first-line in children + pregnancy (no radiation); CT for adults; MRI in pregnancy if US equivocal. AAST grading. Resuscitate + IV fluids + NPO + analgesia (Pain Trial — does not mask). Antibiotics: pip-tazo 4.5 g q8h or ceftriaxone + metronidazole. SURGERY: LAPAROSCOPIC APPENDICECTOMY first-line (shorter recovery, less infection); within 24h. Complicated (perforation/abscess/phlegmon): IV antibiotics × 4-7 d + CT-guided drainage > 4-6 cm abscess; interval appendicectomy at 6-12 wk (controversial). ANTIBIOTIC-FIRST (CODA NEJM 2020): adult uncomplicated — non-inferior at 90 d for major outcomes; ~30% appendicectomy by 90 d; shared decision; NOT for perforation/abscess/appendicolith. PREGNANCY: laparoscopic safe (2nd trim ideal); MRI if US uncertain. ELDERLY: lower threshold imaging + surgery; investigate underlying CRC. Send specimen histology (carcinoid/lymphoma).
rationale: WSES 2020/2024 + NICE NG143 + CODA NEJM 2020.

title: Acute cholecystitis — TG18 grading + EARLY lap-chole < 72h
indicators: RUQ pain + Murphy sign + leucocytosis + US findings
recommendation: Tokyo TG18 severity. US first-line: wall > 4 mm + pericholecystic fluid + sonographic Murphy. Resuscitate + NPO + IV antibiotics (cefuroxime + metronidazole or pip-tazo). Grade I/II: EARLY LAP-CHOLE within 72h preferred over delayed (Cochrane). Grade III (organ dysfunction): ICU + sepsis bundle + percutaneous CHOLECYSTOSTOMY bridge → interval cholecystectomy when stable. CHOLEDOCHOLITHIASIS: ERCP + sphincterotomy PRE-cholecystectomy if ALP/bilirubin raised or CBD dilated. ACUTE CHOLANGITIS (Charcot triad / Reynolds pentad): IV antibiotics + ERCP biliary drainage WITHIN 24h. Gallstone pancreatitis: ERCP within 24-48h if cholangitis/persistent obstruction; SAME-admission cholecystectomy for mild (PONCHO). Emphysematous (diabetics): emergency cholecystectomy. Pregnancy: laparoscopic safe (2nd trim ideal). Antibiotic duration 4-7 d post source control. Acalculous cholecystitis (critically ill): drain ± delayed cholecystectomy.
rationale: Tokyo TG18 2018/2024 + WSES + NICE NG188 + Cochrane.

title: SBO — gastrograffin trial; LBO/strangulation → surgery; volvulus → endoscopic detorsion
indicators: abdominal distension + colicky pain + vomiting + absolute constipation
recommendation: Resuscitate IV fluids + NPO + NG decompression + catheter + analgesia + correct electrolytes + VTE prophylaxis. CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast — transition + cause + ischaemia features; AXR + erect CXR; FBC + lactate + ABG. ADHESIVE SBO: conservative 24-48-72h with NG + IV fluid + gastrograffin (both diagnostic + therapeutic — Cochrane); surgery if strangulation/peritonitis/closed-loop/failure. HERNIA: try manual reduction with analgesia + sedation; if irreducible/strangulated — emergency repair ± resection. LARGE BOWEL OBSTRUCTION: most malignant — Hartmann's or anastomosis + diverting stoma; SEMS as bridge or palliative; sigmoid volvulus — endoscopic detorsion + flatus tube (60-90% success) then elective sigmoidectomy; caecal volvulus — surgery. MALIGNANT bowel obstruction advanced: stent vs conservative (NG + antiemetic haloperidol/cyclizine + dexamethasone + octreotide). Paediatric intussusception: air/hydrostatic enema reduction first then surgery if fails. Ileus: treat cause + electrolytes + mobilise; Ogilvie's neostigmine 2-2.5 mg IV under cardiac monitor. Early mobilise + ERAS.
rationale: WSES Adhesive SBO 2018/2024 + WSES Colon + NICE Cancer + Cochrane.

title: Diverticulitis — Hinchey CT + selective antibiotic + early surgery for III/IV
recommendation: CT abdomen/pelvis with contrast — Hinchey 0-IV grading + complications (abscess/perforation/fistula/stricture). UNCOMPLICATED OUTPATIENT (CT Hinchey 0/Ia mild + low risk): consider NO antibiotic (DIABOLO + AVOD trials) + clear fluids + analgesia + follow-up; antibiotics if immunocompromised/severe/comorbidity. Antibiotic if given: co-amoxiclav 625 TDS × 7 d or ciprofloxacin + metronidazole. COMPLICATED: admit + IV ceftriaxone + metronidazole or pip-tazo; Hinchey I-II abscess > 4 cm — CT-guided drainage; Hinchey III (purulent peritonitis) — surgery (Hartmann's or primary anastomosis with loop ileostomy — LADIES); laparoscopic lavage selected (LADIES/DILALA/SCANDIV mixed); Hinchey IV (faeculent) — HARTMANN'S + damage control if unstable. COLONOSCOPY 6-8 wk post-acute (rule out CRC 1-2%). Elective sigmoidectomy: recurrent (4+), complicated history, immunocompromised. Fistula: elective resection when inflammation settled. Avoid NSAID/steroid/opioid (worsen recurrence). High-fibre diet 25-35 g + hydration + exercise + smoking cessation; NUTS/SEEDS NO LONGER restricted (old advice).
rationale: WSES + ASCRS 2020/2024 + DIABOLO/AVOD + LADIES.

title: Adult major trauma — cABCDE + permissive hypotension + TXA + damage control
recommendation: Trauma team activation per criteria. PRIMARY SURVEY cABCDE (with c-spine + catastrophic haemorrhage). FAST/eFAST bedside. Pre-hospital: tourniquet + pelvic binder + airway with c-spine + needle decompression PTX + TXA 1 g IV within 3h. AIRWAY: RSI ketamine + rocuronium + video laryngoscope; cric if can't intubate/oxygenate. BREATHING: O2 + treat tension/open PTX + flail chest. CIRCULATION: 2× large-bore IV (IO if failed 90s); CONTROLLED HYPOTENSION (SBP 80-90 / MAP 65 in non-head injury; SBP > 110 if head injury); early BLOOD (O-neg → crossmatch); MASSIVE TRANSFUSION 1:1:1 RBC:FFP:platelets + TXA + calcium + warmth (CRASH-2/CRASH-3); pelvic binder + angiographic embolisation; REBOA selected centres. DISABILITY: GCS + pupils + glucose + treat raised ICP (head-up 30 + hypertonic saline 3% or mannitol). EXPOSURE: hypothermia prevention. Damage control resuscitation + surgery if lactate > 5 / pH < 7.2 / T < 35 / INR > 1.5. Open fracture Gustilo-Anderson: IV cefazolin + gentamicin + irrigation + debridement within 6h. ICU + tertiary survey on ward (missed injuries 10-15%). Kenya National EMC Strategy 2020-2025; WHO Decade of Road Safety 2021-2030.
rationale: ATLS 10e + EAST + WSES + Kenya EMC + CRASH-2/3.

title: ACG — IMMEDIATE IV acetazolamide + topical + ophthalmology emergency + laser PI/lens extraction
indicators: unilateral severe eye pain + halos + cloudy cornea + mid-dilated pupil + raised IOP
recommendation: EMERGENCY ophthalmology referral. Break the attack: IV acetazolamide 500 mg + oral acetazolamide 250-500 mg + topical β-blocker (timolol) + α2-agonist (apraclonidine/brimonidine) + topical steroid + pilocarpine 1-2% (only AFTER IOP starts dropping — ineffective at IOP > 40); supine; hyperosmotic (mannitol IV) for very high IOP short-term. Analgesia + antiemetic. DEFINITIVE: peripheral laser iridotomy (PI) bilateral or LENS EXTRACTION (EAGLE trial — superior long-term to PI for primary angle closure). Long-term IOP monitoring + medication review (avoid anticholinergic/antihistamine/decongestant/TCA/SSRI/prone position). Fellow eye: prophylactic PI/lens extraction. Distinguish acute red painful eye DDx: ACG (pain + halos + steamy cornea + mid-dilated fixed pupil + hard globe) vs uveitis (small pupil + KPs) vs keratitis (FB sensation + epithelial defect) vs endophthalmitis (post-op + hypopyon) vs scleritis (deep boring + tender globe).
rationale: EGS 5e 2024 + AAO PPP + NICE NG81 + EAGLE Lancet 2016.

title: CRAO — treat as STROKE within 4-6h; GCA cover + IV steroid immediate; carotid + cardiac workup
indicators: sudden painless monocular vision loss + RAPD + cherry-red spot
recommendation: Treat as STROKE EQUIVALENT. RAPD + cherry-red spot + pale retina + arteriolar narrowing on fundus. GCA assumed > 50: HIGH-DOSE IV METHYLPRED 1 g × 3 d then pred 60-80 mg taper + temporal artery biopsy within 1 week + ESR/CRP — vision loss in opposite eye can occur within days if untreated. IV tPA within 4.5h emerging evidence (treat per stroke protocol — selected centres) — controversial but increasing adoption. Older 'measures' (carotid massage, ocular massage, acetazolamide, AC paracentesis) — limited evidence + may dislodge embolus to cerebral. Stroke workup: ECG (AF), echo, CT angiography head+neck (carotid stenosis), CT/MRI brain (concurrent cerebral infarct in 25%). Secondary prevention: aspirin + statin high-intensity + BP control + anticoagulant if AF + carotid endarterectomy if symptomatic > 70% within 2 wk + smoking cessation + DM. Refer neurology + ophthalmology. Established vision loss > 12h: visual recovery limited; focus on prevention of further events + low-vision rehab. NAION (non-arteritic ischaemic optic neuropathy) different — altitudinal field defect + disc swelling; GCA must be excluded.
rationale: AAO PPP 2024 + AHA Retinal Stroke 2021 + BSR GCA + Schultheiss tPA.

title: Chemical eye burn — IRRIGATE COPIOUSLY (≥ 30 min until pH 7) + alkali worse + ophthalmology emergency
recommendation: IRRIGATE FIRST — do NOT delay for examination or workup. Remove solid particles. Topical anaesthetic (proparacaine) — facilitates cooperation. IRRIGATE COPIOUSLY with sterile saline/Ringer's/sterile water (any clean water at scene — DON'T DELAY) — Morgan lens or IV tubing; evert lids + sweep fornix; MIN 30 MIN + check pH (until 7.0-7.4); ALKALI longer (often hours — penetrates deeper, total 5-10 L may be needed). Roper-Hall grading I-IV — limbal ischaemia is key prognostic factor. Post-irrigation: topical antibiotic (chloramphenicol) + cycloplegic (atropine 1%) + topical STEROID first week ONLY (impairs healing later — specialist guidance) + lubricants + vitamin C + DOXYCYCLINE 100 BD (MMP inhibitor + anti-collagenase) + citrate 10% drops for alkali + tetanus + analgesia. Amniotic membrane / limbal stem cell transplant for severe RH III-IV. EMERGENCY ophthalmology referral all chemical. Long-term: corneal transplant for severe scarring; keratoprosthesis (Boston KPro) end-stage. PREVENTION: PPE + eye-wash stations + workplace safety + pesticide safety (Kenya agricultural) + public education to IRRIGATE IMMEDIATELY + come to hospital. Roper-Hall I good prognosis vs IV severe ischaemia poor.
rationale: AAO PPP 2024 + ICO + Wagoner.

title: Epistaxis — first aid + cautery; posterior packing for severe + antibiotic + admit
recommendation: Sit forward + pinch CARTILAGINOUS nose 15-20 min continuous + ice + spit blood. Topical cophenylcaine / oxymetazoline + reapply pressure. ANTERIOR identified bleeding point: SILVER NITRATE cautery one side only (bilateral cautery → septal perforation). If fails: anterior nasal packing (Rapid Rhino / Merocel / Floseal) × 24-48h + ANTIBIOTIC (toxic shock syndrome risk — phenoxymethylpenicillin or cephalexin while packed). POSTERIOR (10% — severe, bilateral, posterior pharyngeal blood, older anticoagulated): FOLEY catheter 16-18 Fr through nostril, balloon in nasopharynx + anterior pack + ADMIT (hypoxia/vasovagal/arrhythmia risk) + ECG monitor + O2 + analgesia + antibiotic. Embolisation IR (sphenopalatine + facial) or surgical ligation (endoscopic sphenopalatine artery — most effective posterior). Resuscitate haemodynamic instability. Reverse anticoagulation if life-threatening (vit K + 4F-PCC for warfarin; idarucizumab dabigatran; andexanet Xa inhibitor; FFP if PCC unavailable). RECURRENT: workup HHT/coagulopathy/HTN/tumour; saline + petrolatum + Naseptin preventive; humidifier; HHT — tranexamic acid + bevacizumab (severe). PAEDIATRIC: usually digital trauma + dry air; first aid + petrolatum; avoid routine cautery. Septal haematoma (post-trauma) — DRAIN URGENTLY (cartilage necrosis + saddle nose risk).
rationale: ENT UK 2024 + AAO-HNS 2020 + NICE CKS + HHT.

title: Testicular torsion — SURGERY within 6h; manual detorsion if delay; bilateral orchiopexy
indicators: sudden testicular pain in young male + absent cremasteric reflex + high-riding
recommendation: EMERGENCY — TIME IS TESTIS (viability < 6h good, < 12h declining, 24h near zero). Clinical diagnosis — DO NOT DELAY for imaging in classic presentation. TWIST score ≥ 5 high probability. Doppler US sensitivity 89% (absent flow) — only if doesn't delay surgery. Surgical consultation IMMEDIATELY. SURGICAL EXPLORATION + DETORSION + BILATERAL ORCHIOPEXY (contralateral has same bell-clapper anatomy in 80%); orchiectomy if non-viable + contralateral orchiopexy. MANUAL DETORSION if surgery delayed: 'open book' — rotate testis OUTWARD/laterally from midline (most twist inward) — 1-3 rotations (often 720°); pain relief + Doppler confirms; STILL needs definitive orchiopexy. NPO + IV access + analgesia + antibiotic prophylaxis. Consent including possible orchiectomy + prosthesis. Neonatal torsion: usually extravaginal perinatal not salvageable but explore + contralateral orchiopexy. Intermittent torsion (recurrent self-resolving): elective bilateral orchiopexy. Adolescent male education on recognising + emergency presentation. Major medicolegal — document carefully. DDx: epididymo-orchitis (gradual + STI/UTI history + cremasteric present + pyuria), hydrocele torsion, appendix testis torsion (blue dot sign, less severe), hernia, trauma, tumour.
rationale: EAU 2024 + AUA + BAUS + TWIST.

title: SJS/TEN — STOP causative drug + burns-level care + ciclosporin 3-5 mg/kg × 7-10 d
indicators: painful mucocutaneous rash + skin detachment + drug history
recommendation: EMERGENCY — like extensive burn. STOP CAUSATIVE DRUG immediately (single most important). SCORTEN at admission + day 3. Admit burns/dermatology/ICU. Fluid 2-4 ml/kg/%BSA over 24h (less than Parkland — less third-spacing in TEN). Temperature 28-32°C. Early enteral NG (hypercaloric + protein). Wound: non-adherent (Mepilex, Aquacel Ag) — AVOID silver sulfadiazine (sulfa cross-reactivity if SJS from sulfonamide). NO aggressive debridement. EYE CARE day 1 + daily (lubricants q1h + topical steroid + cyclopentolate + amniotic membrane for severe — prevents blindness). Mouth + genital mucosal care. Reverse barrier nursing — sepsis is leading cause of death. CICLOSPORIN 3-5 mg/kg/d × 7-10 d (most evidence). IVIG controversial. Etanercept emerging. Steroids controversial (early pulse may help; chronic increases infection). Multidisciplinary post-recovery (ophth+derm+GU+GI+psych). MedicAlert + genetic counselling HLA typing for family if SE Asian / sub-Saharan.
rationale: BAD 2024 + ALDEN + SCORTEN + ciclosporin meta-analyses.

title: Atopic eczema — emollient + TCS proactive 2x/wk + dupilumab / JAK for severe
recommendation: Severity SCORAD/EASI/IGA/POEM/DLQI. EMOLLIENT cornerstone — generous BD + > 250 g/wk adult; apply within 3 min of bath. TCS step-up by potency: hydrocortisone face/flexures/infants → moderate (clobetasone) → potent (betamethasone valerate) → very potent (clobetasol short-term); BD × 7-14 d acute + PROACTIVE 2 d/wk to recently flared areas during remission (reduces flares). TCI (tacrolimus 0.1% / pimecrolimus 1% / 0.03% for 2-15) — steroid-sparing for face/flexures/maintenance. Crisaborole 2% (≥ 3 yr) / ruxolitinib 1.5% topical (≥ 12 yr) JAK. Phototherapy nbUVB for refractory. SEVERE: dupilumab (≥ 6 mo — Adore-2; SC q2 wk) / tralokinumab / lebrikizumab / nemolizumab (anti-IL-31 for itch). JAK ORAL: upadacitinib / baricitinib / abrocitinib — BBW VTE/MACE/cancer especially > 65 + smokers + CV. Eczema herpeticum — admit IV aciclovir. Staph superinfection — flucloxacillin. Atopic march prevention: emollient from birth high-risk (BEEP mixed); early peanut at 4-6 mo (LEAP) reduces peanut allergy. Allergen avoidance only if proven sensitisation. Mental health support.
rationale: EuroGuiDerm 2024 + AAD + NICE NG223 + BAD + LEAP.

title: Psoriasis — topical/UVB → biologic; PsA workup + CV risk modification
recommendation: PASI/IGA/BSA/DLQI severity. Screen FOR PsA at every visit (GALS). Comorbidity: BP/lipid/glucose/HbA1c (metabolic syndrome 2× — CV risk independent). MILD (BSA < 10%): TCS first-line + vitamin D analogue (calcipotriol) + tar + salicylic acid + tazarotene + topical PDE4 (roflumilast/tapinarof). MODERATE-SEVERE: nbUVB 3×/wk × 30-40 sessions; methotrexate / ciclosporin / acitretin (NOT WCBP). BIOLOGICS: anti-IL-23 (guselkumab/risankizumab/tildrakizumab) — best plaque + low immunogenicity; anti-IL-17 (secukinumab/ixekizumab/brodalumab/bimekizumab); anti-IL-12/23 (ustekinumab); anti-TNF (etan/ada/infl/cert). DEUCRAVACITINIB (TYK2 — Sotyktu) — newer JAK with fewer BBW. Apremilast (PDE4) moderate. ERYTHRODERMIC / GENERALISED PUSTULAR: admit + IV fluids + temperature + rapid systemic (ciclosporin/infliximab); SPESOLIMAB (anti-IL-36R — Effisayer) for GPP flares (NEJM 2021). PsA: anti-TNF/IL-17/IL-23 with PsA approval; JAK + apremilast. Choice by comorbidity (IBD avoid IL-17; pregnancy certolizumab; HBV anti-IL-23 lowest reactivation). Screen TB/HBV/HCV/HIV before biologic. CV risk modification + mental health + lifestyle (smoking #1, alcohol, weight, Mediterranean).
rationale: EuroGuiDerm 2024 + AAD/NPF + NICE CG153 + GRAPPA + Effisayer.

title: Renal colic — NSAID first-line + CT KUB + MET 5-10 mm + emergency drainage if infected
recommendation: Analgesia FIRST priority: NSAID (diclofenac 75 IM / 100 PR / ibuprofen 600 PO) — first-line (reduces ureteric spasm + better than opioid); morphine 0.1 mg/kg IV for refractory; IV paracetamol + antiemetic. Urinalysis + MSU + creatinine + Ca + urate; pregnancy test. NON-CONTRAST CT KUB first-line (low-dose); US first-line in pregnancy + paeds. Stone size: < 5 mm 80% pass; 5-10 mm 50% — MET tamsulosin 0.4 OD or nifedipine 30 OD × up to 4 wk (modest — SUSPEND); > 10 mm intervention. INFECTED OBSTRUCTED KIDNEY = UROLOGICAL EMERGENCY (fever + hydronephrosis + raised Cr): emergency drainage within 6-12h (nephrostomy or JJ stent) + IV broad-spectrum antibiotics + ICU if shock. Definitive: ESWL (< 2 cm), URS+laser (1-2 cm + distal), PCNL (> 2 cm / complex). PREVENTION (most important): hydration 2.5-3 L/d urine, reduce salt + animal protein, adequate Ca (don't restrict), citrate-rich, low oxalate if Ca-ox stones; HCTZ 25-50 mg for hypercalciuria; allopurinol for hyperuricosuria; alkalinise urine for uric acid stones (potassium citrate); analyse passed stone.
rationale: EAU 2024 + AUA + NICE NG118 + SUSPEND.

title: BPH — tamsulosin / 5ARI / combination; tadalafil for LUTS+ED; surgery for failure
recommendation: IPSS + DRE + urinalysis + U&E + PSA (shared decision) + PVR + uroflowmetry + frequency-volume chart. Rule out cancer (DRE + PSA + risk-stratify), neurological cause, infection. MILD (IPSS < 8): lifestyle (fluid timing + reduce caffeine/alcohol + treat constipation + review meds — avoid anticholinergic/sympathomimetic). MODERATE-SEVERE: α1-BLOCKER — TAMSULOSIN 0.4 mg/d (uroselective, less hypotension) or alfuzosin/doxazosin (BP benefit if comorbid HTN) — rapid relief weeks; counsel floppy iris syndrome (inform cataract surgeon). 5ARI: finasteride 5 mg or dutasteride 0.5 mg — slow (3-6 mo); reduces volume 20-30% + acute retention risk (MTOPS); halves PSA. COMBO (tamsulosin + dutasteride) for moderate-severe + large prostate (CombAT). Anticholinergic / β3 (mirabegron preferred elderly) for storage; combine with α-blocker for mixed. TADALAFIL 5 mg/d (PDE5i daily) for comorbid ED. Minimally invasive: UroLift / Rezum (office). Surgery (failed medical): TURP gold standard 30-80 g; HoLEP for larger / less bleeding; open simple prostatectomy > 80-100 g. AUR: catheterise + α-blocker + TWOC in 1-3 d.
rationale: EAU 2024 + AUA 2023/2024 + NICE NG97 + MTOPS + CombAT.

title: UTI — nitrofurantoin / fosfomycin / pivmecillinam first-line; AVOID FQ uncomplicated
recommendation: Urinalysis + MSU + culture (CFU > 10^5 / > 10^3 symptomatic with dysuria). UNCOMPLICATED CYSTITIS women non-preg: nitrofurantoin 50-100 QDS × 5-7 d (avoid eGFR < 30) / trimethoprim 200 BD × 3 d (resistance check) / fosfomycin 3 g PO × 1 / pivmecillinam 400 q8h × 3 d. AVOID FQ uncomplicated (resistance + AEs). PYELONEPHRITIS: outpatient cipro 500 BD × 7 d (FQ resistance dependent); inpatient IV ceftriaxone 2 g/d ± gent if severe / pip-tazo / meropenem ESBL/CRE; 7-14 d; CT KUB if not improving 48-72h. MEN: always complicated; urological workup; 7-14 d; if prostatitis suspected — cipro / cotrim 4-6 wk. PREGNANCY: TREAT asymptomatic bacteriuria; nitrofurantoin (avoid 3rd trim) / cephalexin / fosfomycin; AVOID trimethoprim 1st trim + FQ + tetracyclines; pyelonephritis IV ceftriaxone + admit; recurrent prophylaxis nitrofurantoin 50 nocte. CAUTI: do NOT treat asymptomatic catheterised bacteriuria (except pregnancy / pre-uro surgery); change catheter > 14 d before culture; CAUTI bundle (aseptic + closed + daily review + remove ASAP). ELDERLY: bacteriuria common — DON'T TREAT unless specific symptoms (non-specific confusion alone — investigate other causes). RECURRENT UTI: vaginal oestrogen postmenopause + hydration + post-coital voiding + cranberry/methenamine (ALTAR) + low-dose prophylaxis nitrofurantoin / trimethoprim or post-coital single dose. ESBL/CRE: ceftaz-avibactam / cefiderocol. Emphysematous pyelonephritis (DM): admit + IV antibiotics + drainage + tight glycaemic + ICU. WHO AWaRe stewardship + local antibiogram.
rationale: IDSA 2024 + EAU 2024 + NICE NG109/111/113 + ALTAR Lancet 2022.

title: AOM — analgesia + watch-and-wait for > 6 mo mild; amoxicillin 90 mg/kg/d for indicated
recommendation: Otoscopy + pneumatic + analgesia first priority. ANTIBIOTIC DECISION: < 6 mo always antibiotic; 6 mo-2 yr severe/bilateral/otorrhoea → antibiotic, mild unilateral → watchful waiting with reliable 48-72h follow-up; > 2 yr + adults mild-moderate → watchful waiting + analgesia first; severe / immunocompromised → antibiotic. CHOICE: AMOXICILLIN 80-90 mg/kg/d in 2 doses (overcomes pneumococcal resistance) × 5 d (> 2 yr) / 10 d (< 2 yr); co-amoxiclav if recent antibiotic / day-care / severe / β-lactamase suspected; cefuroxime/cefdinir/azithromycin for penicillin allergy. RECURRENT (≥ 3/6 mo or ≥ 4/12 mo): ENT referral for GROMMETS + adenoidectomy if nasal obstruction. OME (glue ear): watch 3 mo (most resolve); if bilateral + hearing loss > 25 dB > 3 mo → grommets; hearing aid alternative; antibiotic+steroid+decongestant NOT effective. MASTOIDITIS: EMERGENCY admit + IV antibiotics (ceftriaxone + vancomycin or pip-tazo) + CT temporal bone + ENT cortical mastoidectomy; intracranial complication neurosurgical. Cholesteatoma surgical. PREVENTION: breastfeeding ≥ 6 mo + avoid passive smoke + pneumococcal/Hib/flu vaccination + treat allergic rhinitis. WHO IMCI ear module + Kenya MOH paediatric protocols.
rationale: AAP 2024 + NICE NG91 + WHO IMCI + AAO-HNS.

title: Sinusitis — saline + intranasal steroid; antibiotic only if ≥ 10 d / severe / worsening
indicators: facial pain + nasal congestion + duration / severity criteria
recommendation: MOST viral. Clinical diagnosis (no routine imaging). EPOS bacterial criteria: ≥ 10 d without improvement / severe (fever > 39 + purulence × 3 d) / worsening 'double-sickening'. SYMPTOM RELIEF: saline irrigation (high-volume low-pressure) — strong evidence; intranasal steroid (mometasone/fluticasone) — reduces symptoms + may avoid antibiotic; decongestant ≤ 3-5 d (rebound rhinitis); paracetamol/NSAID; hydration + rest. BACTERIAL: amoxicillin 500 q8h × 5-10 d (90 mg/kg/d if high-resistance); co-amoxiclav if recent antibiotic / treatment failure / high resistance area; doxycycline alternative; pen allergy — levofloxacin or cefuroxime/cefdinir non-severe allergy; AVOID macrolides empirically (pneumococcal resistance). Reassess 48-72h. ORBITAL/PERIORBITAL CELLULITIS: admit + IV ceftriaxone + flucloxacillin or pip-tazo + ophth/ENT + CT orbits + surgical drainage of subperiosteal abscess. INTRACRANIAL EXTENSION: emergency admit + IV broad-spectrum + neurosurgery + ENT + ICU. INVASIVE FUNGAL (immunocompromised — diabetic / neutropenic — Mucor): EMERGENCY admit + liposomal amphotericin B + surgical debridement + correct underlying. CHRONIC RHINOSINUSITIS > 12 wk: saline + intranasal steroid + treat allergy + short oral steroid + doxy 100 × 3 wk (CRSwNP); FESS specialist; BIOLOGICS for severe CRSwNP + comorbid asthma — dupilumab (SINUS-24/52) / mepolizumab / omalizumab. AB stewardship — most acute is viral.
rationale: EPOS 2024 + IDSA + NICE NG79 + AAO-HNS + SINUS-24/52.

title: Pharyngitis — Centor/FeverPAIN; penicillin V or amoxicillin × 10 d if strep confirmed (RHD prevention)
recommendation: MOST viral. Centor / FeverPAIN: 0-1 viral (no swab/AB); 2-3 RADT or throat swab; 4 empirical antibiotic. SUPPORTIVE: analgesia + warm fluids + lozenges. GAS confirmed / high probability: PENICILLIN V 500 mg QDS × 10 DAYS (or 250 q6h children) — 10 d critical for RHD prevention SSA; amoxicillin 500 TDS × 10 d alternative (AVOID if EBV suspected — rash); benzathine penicillin 1.2 MU IM single dose for adherence challenge (SSA + RHD secondary prophylaxis monthly). Pen allergy: cephalexin or macrolide. WHY treat: RHD/RHD prevention (SSA priority) + suppurative complication + transmission. QUINSY: admit + ENT + IV co-amox/pip-tazo + needle aspiration / I&D. EBV: supportive + AVOID amoxicillin + no contact sport 4-6 wk (splenic rupture). DIPHTHERIA (rare): isolation + diphtheria antitoxin + penicillin/erythromycin × 14 d + notify public health + contact prophylaxis. RHEUMATIC FEVER: Jones criteria + bed rest + NSAID + steroid if carditis + monthly benzathine penicillin secondary prophylaxis × 10 yr or to 21 (longer if carditis); echo for RHD; KENYA RHD Programme priority. Recurrent tonsillitis Paradise criteria → tonsillectomy. Gonococcal: ceftriaxone + azithromycin. HIV test recurrent/severe. AB stewardship balanced against RHD prevention SSA.
rationale: IDSA 2024 + NICE NG84 + AHA + WHO ESF + Kenya RHD.

title: VLU — ABPI then 4-layer compression + endovenous ablation early (EVRA)
indicators: chronic gaiter-area leg ulcer + venous insufficiency
recommendation: ABPI MANDATORY before compression: > 0.8 full compression / 0.5-0.8 modified (specialist) / < 0.5 NO compression (vascular). 4-LAYER COMPRESSION (Profore) 40 mmHg ankle — gold standard; change weekly; continue until healed; class 2 hosiery (23-32 mmHg) for healed ulcer maintenance — reduces recurrence > 50%. Wound care: cleanse with tap/saline (AVOID H2O2/iodine routine); dressing by wound (alginate/foam for exudate, hydrogel for dry, silver short course infected); skin barrier for maceration; honey-impregnated useful low-resource. Debridement (sharp/autolytic/maggot). PENTOXIFYLLINE 400 TDS PO improves healing (Cochrane). EARLY ENDOVENOUS ABLATION (EVRA NEJM 2018) for incompetent superficial veins — faster healing + less recurrence. Skin grafts / NPWT / Apligraf for refractory. Address pain (paracetamol + NSAID + neuropathic adjunct + topical lidocaine). Education: COMPRESSION adherence + elevation + mobilisation + smoking cessation + weight + skin care + hosiery for recurrence prevention. Specialist if mixed/arterial/malignancy suspected/non-healing > 12 wk/recurrent/atypical (vasculitis). Multidisciplinary tissue viability + community nursing. SSA: honey + compression bandage access + train primary care; treat coexisting TB/HIV/lymphoedema/SCD ulcers/tropical ulcers.
rationale: EWMA + NICE NG217 + SIGN 120 + EVRA 2018 + Pentoxifylline Cochrane.

title: CGA — multidimensional MDT assessment + individualised targets + WHO ICOPE
indicators: older adult routine / admission / functional decline / frailty
recommendation: Multidimensional CGA: physical + cognitive (MoCA preferred) + functional (ADL/IADL/TUG) + social + environmental + values + frailty (CFS) + polypharmacy (STOPP/START + Beers) + nutrition (MNA) + EoL surprise question. MDT (geriatrician + GP + nurse + physio + OT + pharmacist + SLT + dietitian + social work + palliative care). INDIVIDUALISE TARGETS for frail (HbA1c 53-64 not 48; BP 130-140 not strict 120-130; LDL liberalised). Continue evidence-based therapy where benefits exceed risks but DEPRESCRIBE with diminishing benefit. Falls prevention (separate). Cognitive screening + dementia management. Continence + nutrition (1.0-1.2 g/kg protein + ONS) + sensory (hearing aids reduce dementia per Lancet Commission). ADVANCE CARE PLANNING early. Vaccinations: pneumo + flu + COVID + shingles + RSV. CGA in hospital reduces death + dependency (Cochrane). Models: ICOPE (WHO LMIC) + day hospital + hospital-at-home + frailty hubs. Kenya National Policy on Older Persons.
rationale: BGS CGA 2024 + WHO ICOPE 2024 + AGS Beers + STOPP/START + WHO Decade of Healthy Ageing.

title: Falls — multifactorial assessment + Otago exercise + medication review + home modification
indicators: fall in older adult / ≥ 2 falls / fall with injury
recommendation: Multifactorial assessment for ≥ 2 falls / 1 fall with injury / fear of falling. Cardiovascular (postural BP lying + standing, ECG, 24h Holter for syncope), cognition (MoCA + GDS), gait (TUG > 12s abnormal), strength, vision/audiometry, foot/footwear, continence, polypharmacy, bone (DEXA + FRAX), environmental (OT). INTERVENTIONS most effective combined (Cochrane): EXERCISE primary prevention (Otago Programme home — gold standard) + resistance + balance + tai chi > 3h/wk lifelong. HOME MODIFICATION (grab bars + ramps + remove rugs + lighting + bedside commode + pendant alarm). MEDICATION REVIEW + DEPRESCRIBING — withdraw psychoactives (benzo/Z-drug/opioid/antipsychotic/anticholinergic/TCA/sedating antihistamine/sulfonylurea/orthostatic-causing antihypertensives) per STOPP/Beers/ACB. VISION (cataract surgery first eye especially). FOOTWEAR (closed-toe + low heel + non-slip). CARDIOVASCULAR (orthostatic — stop offending + hydration + compression + fludrocortisone/midodrine; bradyarrhythmia + carotid sinus → pacemaker). BONE: vit D 800-1000 IU + Ca 1000-1200 + DEXA + bisphosphonate. Postural hypotension protocol. Fall with injury: trauma protocol + low threshold CT head anticoagulated; hip fracture < 36h surgery (NICE NG124). Fear of falling — CBT + balance training. WHO Step Safely.
rationale: NICE CG161 2024 + AGS/BGS + Cochrane + WHO Step Safely.

title: Frailty — CFS + Fried + exercise (any CFS) + nutrition + deprescribing + ACP
recommendation: CFS 1-9 staging + Fried phenotype (≥ 3 frail, 1-2 pre-frail). Investigate reversible (TSH/B12/anaemia/vit D/depression/polypharmacy/sensory). EXERCISE (most evidence — even advanced frailty): resistance + aerobic + balance 3×/wk; Otago/FaME/Tai Chi/chair-based for severely frail. NUTRITION: protein 1.0-1.2 g/kg/d (1.2-1.5 in acute illness) + adequate calories + vit D + ONS for malnourished + dietitian; address sarcopenia (combined exercise + protein). DEPRESCRIBING: STOPP/START + Beers + ACB; liberalise targets (HbA1c 64 + BP 140-150) per trajectory; withdraw statins / aspirin primary prevention in CFS 6+ if limited life expectancy. Comorbidity optimisation individualised. MOOD + COGNITION + falls + continence + sleep + sensory (hearing aids — Lancet Commission). Carer support + respite. ADVANCE CARE PLANNING + TEP/RESPECT + DNACPR + LPA. Integrated care (frailty hubs + hospital-at-home + virtual ward + ICOPE). CFS 7-9 → palliative + EoL. Vaccinations universal. Address SSA poverty + food + isolation; Kenya National Policy on Older Persons.
rationale: BGS Fit for Frailty + WHO ICOPE + Rockwood CFS + Fried + FORTA.

title: Delirium — 4AT + identify cause + non-pharmacological first; AVOID benzo (except ETOH withdrawal)
recommendation: 4AT bedside (Alertness + AMT-4 + Attention + Acute change). HYPOACTIVE delirium often missed — worse outcomes. Identify TRIGGER — drugs (new/dose change — anticholinergic/opioid/benzo/steroid), infection (UTI/pneumonia/sepsis), metabolic (Na/glucose/Ca/urea/ammonia), hypoxia, pain, retention, sleep deprivation, sensory deprivation, withdrawal (ETOH/benzo), stroke/SDH (especially after fall on anticoag), cardiac (MI/arrhythmia/HF), Wernicke's (thiamine for any ETOH/malnutrition). Workup: FBC/U&E/glucose/Ca/LFT/ammonia/TSH/B12/UA+culture/blood culture/CXR/ECG/ABG/CT head if focal or fall on anticoag. PREVENTION (most effective — HELP/multicomponent non-pharm): reorientation + sleep hygiene + early mobilise + sensory aids + hydration + pain + avoid catheters/restraints/lines. MANAGEMENT: identify+treat cause + STOP offending drugs + non-pharm (quiet single room + consistent staff + family + reorient + mobilise + sleep + hearing/glasses). PHARM only severe agitation/danger: HALOPERIDOL 0.5-1 mg PO/IM (AVOID in Lewy/Parkinson — use clozapine/quetiapine); olanzapine 2.5-5 mg / risperidone 0.25-0.5 mg; AVOID BENZODIAZEPINES (worsen delirium) EXCEPT alcohol withdrawal / seizures; dexmedetomidine for ICU. QTc + minimal dose + reassess daily. DSD (superimposed on dementia) — high mortality. Post-delirium — persistent cognitive 6-12 mo; reassess dementia; family/patient counsel (PTSD-like). ABCDEF bundle ICU. Perioperative: pre-op CGA + avoid drugs/sedation + early mobilise + HELP.
rationale: NICE CG103 2023 + BGS 2024 + AGS + HELP + 4AT.

title: Hip fracture — < 36h surgery + ortho-geriatric + fascia iliaca block + ZA + FLS
indicators: fragility hip fracture in older adult
recommendation: ED: analgesia + FASCIA ILIACA BLOCK (US-guided — strongly recommended, reduces opioid + delirium); IV fluids; restrictive transfusion (Hb < 80 — FOCUS); reverse anticoag per protocol; pressure care + LMWH VTE prophylaxis; admit ortho-geriatric ward. SURGERY < 36 HOURS (NICE NG124 Best Practice Tariff — improves outcomes). DON'T DELAY for minor abnormalities. INTRACAPSULAR Garden I-II: cannulated screws; Garden III-IV: hemiarthroplasty (cemented) or THR (if independent + cognitively fit per NICE). EXTRACAPSULAR: DHS (intertroch stable) or intramedullary nail (subtroch/unstable/reverse oblique). Anaesthesia spinal vs GA — shared decision (REGAIN 2021 no difference); avoid benzo/sedatives; multimodal analgesia + peripheral blocks. POST-OP: ortho-geriatric co-management + EARLY MOBILISE within 24h + physio daily + multimodal pain + nutrition + LMWH/DOAC × 28-35 d (extended) + delirium prevention HELP + falls assess + cognitive + bone health. BONE HEALTH (don't miss — secondary prevention): vit D 800-1000 + Ca + ZOLEDRONIC ACID 5 mg IV annually starting within first week post-op (RECOVERY trial — no delay union) or alendronate 70 mg/wk; Fracture Liaison Service. 20-30% 1-yr mortality + 50% never regain function — best outcomes with co-managed pathway. SSA: emerging burden + train + integrate NCD strategy.
rationale: NICE NG124 2024 + AAOS + RECOVERY + REGAIN + FOCUS + BPT UK.

title: Polypharmacy — STOPP/START + Beers + ACB + structured deprescribing
indicators: ≥ 5 medications / frailty / falls / cognitive decline / ADR / transitions
recommendation: Medication reconciliation EVERY visit/transition (prescription + OTC + supplements + herbal). Tools: STOPP/START v2 + AGS Beers 2023 + FORTA + Anticholinergic Burden (ACB). STRUCTURED DEPRESCRIBE: 1) reconcile 2) review indication/efficacy/safety/adherence 3) prioritise stop/reduce/switch 4) plan with patient+family 5) TAPER (psychoactive/steroid/antihypertensive — avoid rebound) 6) monitor 7) document. STOPP candidates: long-term benzo > 4 wk, Z-drugs, long-term oral steroid for COPD/OA, PPI > 8 wk full-dose without indication, aspirin primary prevention low CV risk, TCA, 1st-gen antihistamine, NSAID with CV/GI/renal risk, antipsychotic in dementia (BBW). START candidates: statin + ACEi + βB + DOAC + Ca/vitD/bisphosphonate + vaccinations. ANTICHOLINERGIC BURDEN > 3 increases dementia/falls/delirium — switch to lower-burden alternatives (mirabegron β3 for OAB; SSRI not TCA; melatonin not benzo). PRESCRIBING CASCADE — recognise + reverse (CCB→diuretic; metoclopramide→Parkinson Rx; anticholinergic→laxative). INDIVIDUALISE for frail: liberalise HbA1c/BP/LDL; statin in 90-yr-old with limited life expectancy — deprescribe; ASPREE — aspirin primary prevention withdraw elderly. End-of-life — minimise burden; symptom-focused only; SC infusion when can't swallow. Pharmacist embedded in primary care + hospital — major value. SSA: cost + traditional medicine + adherence considerations.
rationale: STOPP/START 2024 + Beers 2023 + Deprescribing.org + ASPREE + WHO Medication Without Harm.

title: Osteoporosis — DEXA + FRAX + alendronate / zoledronate / denosumab / romosozumab + FLS
indicators: T-score ≤ -2.5 / fragility fracture / FRAX > threshold / glucocorticoid > 7.5 mg > 3 mo
recommendation: DEXA hip + spine + FRAX (Kenya-specific available). Vertebral fracture assessment. Bloods (FBC/U&E/Ca/PO4/ALP/25-OH vit D/PTH/TSH/testosterone in men); secondary cause workup if young/unexpected (SPEP/cortisol/coeliac). NON-PHARM ALL: Ca 1000-1200 mg/d + vit D 800-1000 IU/d (50,000 IU monthly if deficient) + weight-bearing + resistance exercise + smoking cessation + ETOH limit + protein 1.0-1.2 g/kg/d + falls prevention + sunlight. TREATMENT INDICATIONS: T ≤ -2.5 OR fragility fracture OR FRAX > 20% major / 3% hip OR long-term steroid > 7.5 mg > 3 mo. FIRST-LINE BISPHOSPHONATES: alendronate 70 mg/wk PO (upright × 30 min) or risedronate 35 mg/wk; ZOLEDRONIC ACID 5 mg IV annually for oral intolerance/adherence/hip fracture (RECOVERY ZA within first week post-op — no delay union); duration 5 yr oral / 3 yr IV initially + reassess holiday. DENOSUMAB 60 mg SC q6 mo for CKD < 35 or bisphosphonate-intolerant — NO drug holiday (rebound vertebral fractures — don't stop without bisphosphonate transition). ROMOSOZUMAB 210 mg SC monthly × 12 mo for severe (T < -2.5 + fracture / multiple) + bisphosphonate after — CV warning recent MI/stroke. TERIPARATIDE 20 mcg SC daily × 24 mo for severe + multiple fragility + failed; followed by anti-resorptive. SECONDARY PREVENTION post-fracture: ALL fragility fracture > 50 = osteoporosis (no DEXA needed pre-treatment per FLS). ALL osteoporotic fracture → Fracture Liaison Service. Glucocorticoid-induced > 7.5 mg > 3 mo: Ca+vit D + bisphosphonate. ONJ + atypical femur fracture warning (dental review + thigh pain investigate).
rationale: NICE TA464/NG56 2024 + AACE + NOF/BHOF + FRAX + RECOVERY + ARCH.

title: ACP — surprise question + Serious Illness Conversation Guide + TEP/RESPECT + DNACPR
indicators: serious illness / surprise question yes / CFS ≥ 7 / advanced dementia / end-organ failure
recommendation: Trigger: surprise question 'would you be surprised if this patient died in 6-12 months?'. Discuss EARLY while capacity intact (at diagnosis + transitions + routine review). Iterative — revisit. SERIOUS ILLNESS CONVERSATION GUIDE (Ariadne Labs): set up + assess understanding + share prognosis (range) + explore values/fears/strengths + plan + affirm + summarise. Document: advance directive + LPA + TREATMENT ESCALATION PLAN (TEP / RESPECT / POLST — broader than DNACPR; ICU/intubation/dialysis/surgery/transfusion/antibiotic) + DNACPR (clinical futility + patient wishes — Tracey/Winspear judgments communicate unless harm). Share across team + ambulance + community + family + shared EHR. Place of care preferences. Family meetings (SPIKES). Cultural + religious + spiritual care (chaplain/imam/priest/traditional). PALLIATIVE CARE early integration (Temel NEJM 2010 lung cancer — improves QoL + survival). Capacity decision-specific + time-specific; best-interest if lacking. Carer assessment + respite + bereavement. SSA: cultural variation in disclosure (sensitive + cultural mediators); religious + traditional beliefs; limited PC + opioid — Kenya National Palliative Care Policy + KEHPRO + Hospice Africa model + advocate; train primary care + CHV + religious leaders + traditional. Staff debrief + compassion fatigue prevention.
rationale: Ariadne Labs + VitalTalk + Mental Capacity Act + Temel NEJM 2010 + Lancet Commission Palliative 2018 + WHO PC Strategy + Kenya National PC Policy.

title: Elder abuse — recognise + private interview + multidisciplinary safeguarding + capacity
indicators: suspected physical / sexual / emotional / financial abuse / neglect / self-neglect / institutional
recommendation: Private interview WITHOUT caregiver if possible. Trauma-informed + empathy + believe + non-judgemental. Document carefully (verbatim + body map + photos with consent/protocol). Physical examination head-to-toe + genital + skin + dentition. Cognitive + MENTAL CAPACITY assessment (decision-specific + time-specific). Mood screen. Bloods. Toxicology if suspect. Pregnancy + STI + HIV PEP if sexual abuse < 72h. Financial review with consent/capacity. SAFETY FIRST — admit if necessary, place of safety, respite. MANDATORY REPORTING per jurisdiction (UK safeguarding adult social care; US APS; Kenya: Children Act for minors + customary/community + County Social Services + emerging older persons policy). MDT: social work + geriatric medicine + safeguarding lead + mental health + legal aid + police if criminal + community/NGO (HelpAge, Mosaic). If CAPACITY intact + returning to abusive situation — respect autonomy, provide resources, follow up. If CAPACITY LACKING — best-interest + safeguarding may override autonomy + Court of Protection / Kadhi. CAREGIVER assessment (Zarit) — many perpetrators face their own burdens; respite + support + treat mental health/substance — separate from protection. Trauma-focused CBT + counselling for survivor. Sexual abuse pathway: SGBV one-stop centre Kenya + PEP + EC + STI prophylaxis + Hep B + counsel. PREVENTION: reduce isolation + financial safeguards + caregiver support + community programmes + address WITCHCRAFT ACCUSATIONS against older women SSA (community/religious leader engagement, customary mediation, education) + property/inheritance rights protection (widows). WHO Toronto Declaration 2002 + Kenya Constitution Article 57 + emerging older persons policy.
rationale: WHO Toronto 2002 + UK Care Act 2014 + Kenya Constitution Art 57 + HelpAge International.

title: Urinary incontinence — DIPPERS reversible + PFMT first-line + mirabegron preferred elderly
indicators: UI in older adult / OAB / stress / mixed / overflow / functional
recommendation: History — type (stress vs urge vs mixed vs overflow vs functional) + 3-day frequency-volume chart + QoL + sexual. DIPPERS reversible (Delirium/Infection-UTI/Pharmaceutical/Psychological/Endocrine/Restricted mobility/Stool impaction) — ADDRESS FIRST. Urinalysis + MSU + PVR bladder scan (> 100 ml = retention) + U&E + glucose. Refer urology if haematuria + risk factors (rule out cancer). STRESS: PFMT (Kegel) physiotherapist-supervised FIRST-LINE 60-70% effective + weight loss + fluid management + smoking cessation + topical vaginal oestrogen postmenopausal; duloxetine modest; surgery (mid-urethral sling controversial + selected). URGE/OAB: bladder training + avoid bladder irritants (caffeine/ETOH/citrus/carbonated). ANTIMUSCARINIC — oxybutynin/solifenacin/tolterodine (caution elderly cognitive — anticholinergic burden); β3-AGONIST MIRABEGRON 50 mg/d PREFERRED ELDERLY/COGNITIVE (less anticholinergic SE; SE HTN/tachy); combination for refractory; botox intravesical 100 U for refractory; sacral nerve modulation. MIXED: PFMT + bladder training + treat predominant. OVERFLOW: identify cause (BPH/neurogenic); catheterise initially; treat BPH (α-blocker + 5ARI); ISC for neurogenic. FUNCTIONAL (cognitive/mobility): accessibility + bedside commode + toileting schedule + prompted voiding for dementia + caregiver education + continence products. SKIN CARE: barrier cream + prompt change. Faecal incontinence often coexists — treat constipation + dietary + biofeedback. VESICOVAGINAL FISTULA SSA: obstetric injury — refer fistula centre (Kenya KNH/Jamaa/Fistula Foundation); early catheter may close < 6 wk; PREVENTION via skilled birth + partogram + EmONC + Linda Mama. Dementia/frailty UI: avoid antimuscarinic (worsen cognition) — mirabegron preferred; toileting schedule + caregiver support. SSA stigma — train primary care + community continence services + pessaries + simple devices + advocate pad/aid access.
rationale: NICE NG123 2024 + NICE CG97 + EAU + AUA + ICS.

title: Hypothyroidism — levothyroxine; pregnancy increase 25-30%; myxoedema coma emergency
recommendation: TSH + free T4 + anti-TPO. Cortisol/ACTH check if central (low TSH + low T4) — give hydrocortisone BEFORE thyroxine if adrenal insufficient (otherwise precipitates adrenal crisis). OVERT (TSH > 10 / symptomatic): levothyroxine 1.5-1.7 mcg/kg/d adults < 60; start 25-50 mcg/d elderly/cardiac; empty stomach 30-60 min before food/Ca/iron; target TSH 0.4-2.5; recheck 6-8 wk after change; LIFELONG. SUBCLINICAL (TSH 4-10): treat if > 10, anti-TPO+ + symptoms, pregnancy/fertility, < 65 + symptoms/CV risk; OBSERVE elderly without symptoms (TRUST NEJM 2017). PREGNANCY: increase dose 25-30% (LATE — 2 extra tablets/week immediately); target TSH 0.1-2.5; monitor every 4-6 wk first half + every trimester. CONGENITAL: newborn screening + L-T4 10-15 mcg/kg/d within 2 wk (prevents cretinism). MYXOEDEMA COMA: IV L-T4 200-500 mcg load + 50-100 mcg/d + HYDROCORTISONE 100 mg q8h (before thyroxine) + warm gradually + glucose + treat trigger + ICU (mortality 25-60%). Drug interactions reduce absorption (PPI/Ca/iron/soy — separate 4h); pregnancy/oestrogen increases requirement; amiodarone/lithium/TKI/ICI thyroiditis. Kenya: KEML access + newborn screening rollout.
rationale: ATA 2024 + ETA + NICE NG145 + TRUST + LATE.

title: Hyperthyroidism — β-blocker + thionamide; PTU 1st trim pregnancy; carbimazole 2nd/3rd; Graves TED EUGOGO
recommendation: TSH + free T4 + TRAb (Graves'-specific) + radioactive uptake scan (diffuse Graves' / patchy nodular / low thyroiditis). Symptom relief: PROPRANOLOL 20-40 mg q8h or atenolol 25-50 mg/d. Definitive (3 options shared decision): 1) THIONAMIDE — carbimazole/methimazole 10-40 mg/d titrate then maintenance 5-10 mg × 12-18 mo (Graves' 30-50% remission); PTU 1ST TRIMESTER pregnancy (less teratogenic — carbimazole aplasia cutis/choanal); switch to carbimazole 2nd/3rd trim (PTU hepatotoxicity); MONITOR FBC + LFT — STOP for sore throat/fever (agranulocytosis); 2) RAI-131 — definitive for Graves'/toxic nodular; CONTRAINDICATED pregnancy/breastfeeding/active ophthalmopathy; lifelong L-T4 4-6 mo post; 3) THYROIDECTOMY — large goitre/compressive/cancer/refractory/ophthalmopathy mod-severe; pre-op euthyroid + Lugol's 10 d. GRAVES' OPHTHALMOPATHY: smoking cessation #1; mild — lubricants + selenium 100 mg BD × 6 mo (CITED); moderate-severe — IV methylpred EUGOGO 500 mg/wk × 6 then 250/wk × 6 (4.5 g cumul); TEPROTUMUMAB anti-IGF-1R (HZNP); AVOID RAI in active TED. AF + thyrotoxicosis: rate/rhythm + anticoag CHA2DS2-VASc; reverts SR after euthyroid 4-6 mo. Amiodarone-induced: type 1 thionamide / type 2 steroid. Pregnancy Graves': TSAb at 22+36 wk (fetal hyperthyroidism). Thyroid storm (separate). Postpartum thyroiditis: β-blocker only (destructive — not thionamide).
rationale: ATA 2024 + ETA/EUGOGO 2024 + NICE NG145 + HZNP teprotumumab + CITED.

title: Thyroid nodule — US TI-RADS + FNA Bethesda; DTC lobectomy/total + RAI; advanced TKI/RET inhibitor
indicators: thyroid nodule on US / calcitonin elevated
recommendation: TSH + free T4 + anti-TPO + calcitonin (MEN2/family). US thyroid + neck nodes — TI-RADS (ACR/EU/Korean): hypoechoic + microcalcifications + irregular margins + taller-than-wide + extrathyroidal extension. FNA per TI-RADS + size; Bethesda I-VI; molecular testing (ThyroSeq/Afirma) for III-IV reduces unnecessary surgery. Hot nodule on uptake scan rarely cancer (functional adenoma). DTC (papillary + follicular): ATA risk-stratify; lobectomy for small low-risk (< 4 cm, limited ETE, no nodes); total thyroidectomy for larger/multifocal/high-risk + central neck dissection if disease; lateral neck dissection if positive. Post-op L-T4 suppression (TSH < 0.1 high / 0.1-0.5 intermediate / 0.5-2 low); RAI ablation for intermediate-high (recombinant TSH Thyrogen); thyroglobulin + neck US surveillance. Advanced RAI-refractory: LENVATINIB (SELECT NEJM 2015) or sorafenib; RET inhibitor SELPERCATINIB (LIBRETTO-001) for RET-altered; BRAF/MEK dabrafenib+trametinib for BRAF V600E; NTRK fusion larotrectinib. MTC: total thyroidectomy + central neck + lateral if positive; calcitonin/CEA; RET germline test (MEN2 — phaeo screen + Ca/HPT BEFORE surgery + family cascade + prophylactic thyroidectomy in carriers timing by mutation). ATC: BRAF V600E mutation 30% — dabrafenib+trametinib+pembrolizumab transformative; chemoradiation; palliative for poor PS.
rationale: ATA Nodule + Cancer 2024 + NICE + Bethesda 2023 + SELECT + LIBRETTO.

title: Adrenal incidentaloma — functional workup ALL + characterise + ESE/ESES 2023
recommendation: FUNCTIONAL WORKUP ALL incidentalomas: 1 mg overnight DST (autonomous cortisol > 50 nmol/L); plasma free metanephrines (phaeo); ARR if HTN/hypoK (primary aldo); DHEAS/testosterone/oestradiol if ACC suspected. IMAGING: non-contrast HU (< 10 benign lipid-rich); contrast washout (> 60% absolute = benign); MRI chemical shift for lipid-rich; PET-CT/MIBG/DOTA for malignant/phaeo. Genetic testing for hereditary phaeo (RET/SDHx/VHL/NF1) if < 50/bilateral/paraganglioma/family. BENIGN (HU < 10, < 4 cm, non-functioning): observe + repeat imaging 6-12 mo (no growth = benign); annual functional × 4 yr; discharge stable + non-functioning at 4 yr. FUNCTIONAL: mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) — adrenalectomy + comorbidity workup; overt Cushing's — adrenalectomy + post-op hydrocortisone cover; PHAEO — α-blockade (phenoxybenzamine) 7-14 d BEFORE β-blockade (avoid unopposed α → HTN crisis); laparoscopic adrenalectomy + genetic testing + family. SUSPECTED MALIGNANT (> 4 cm/HU > 20/heterogeneous/rapid growth/multiple hormone excess): surgical adrenalectomy experienced centre; ACC — open + adjuvant mitotane + EDP-M for advanced. BILATERAL: workup all causes + TB/fungal/HIV in endemic (common SSA) + mets in cancer patients.
rationale: ESE/ESES 2023 + AACE 2024 + NICE + Endocrine Society Phaeo 2024.

title: Primary aldo — ARR screen for resistant HTN + AVS lateralise + adrenalectomy/spironolactone
indicators: resistant HTN / HTN + hypoK / adrenal incidentaloma / HTN < 30 yr / family
recommendation: SCREEN ARR (aldosterone/renin): replete K+ > 4; stop MRA 4-6 wk; consider switch interfering meds (β-blocker/ACEi/ARB/diuretic) to non-interfering (verapamil SR + hydralazine + α-blocker); morning sample seated. ARR > 20-40 + PA > 15 ng/dL suggests. CONFIRM: saline infusion (failure to suppress aldosterone < 5 after 2L); captopril challenge or fludrocortisone alternative. LATERALISE: CT adrenals may show unilateral but ADRENAL VENOUS SAMPLING (AVS) is gold standard before surgery (especially > 35). UNILATERAL adenoma (Conn's): laparoscopic adrenalectomy — pre-op spironolactone 50-100 mg × 4-6 wk; cure 95% biochemical + 50% clinical BP. BILATERAL hyperplasia / non-surgical: SPIRONOLACTONE 12.5-100 mg/d (gynaecomastia 5-30%) or EPLERENONE 25-50 mg BD selective (less gynaecomastia) or esaxerenone; add amiloride if insufficient. GRA (FH-I — chimeric CYP11B1/CYP11B2): low-dose dexamethasone 0.125-0.5 mg nocte. Genetic test + family if early onset/family. CV risk modification + bone health (chronic mineralocorticoid excess). Pregnancy: avoid ACEi/ARB/spironolactone (feminisation male fetus); methyldopa/labetalol/CCB/hydralazine. SSA: major hidden cause of resistant HTN — train primary care to screen + access spironolactone (cheap KEML).
rationale: Endocrine Society Primary Aldo 2024 + AHA + ESH/ESC 2024.

title: Cushing's — DST + UFC + late-night salivary + ACTH + IPSS for pituitary; TSS first-line
recommendation: Screen (any 2 of): late-night salivary cortisol > 4 nmol/L + 24h UFC > 3× ULN × 3 + overnight 1 mg DST cortisol > 50 nmol/L (1.8 µg/dL). Differentiate iatrogenic (most common — taper) vs endogenous. ACTH: suppressed → adrenal (CT); raised → ACTH-dependent (8 mg DST suppress > 50% pituitary; CRH stim — pituitary responds, ectopic doesn't; IPSS gold standard pituitary vs ectopic petrosal/peripheral > 2 basal or > 3 with CRH); MRI pituitary; CT chest/abdo/pelvis or PET for ectopic; DOTATATE for NET. TREATMENT: 1) iatrogenic — TAPER carefully; 2) PITUITARY (Cushing's disease): transsphenoidal surgery first-line (70-90% cure microadenoma); repeat TSS or pituitary radiotherapy/medical for residual; bilateral adrenalectomy last resort (Nelson's syndrome risk); medical — pasireotide/cabergoline/mifepristone/levoketoconazole/OSILODROSTAT (LINC-3/4); 3) ECTOPIC — resect source or adrenal blockade (metyrapone/ketoconazole/osilodrostat/etomidate IV critically ill); 4) ADRENAL — adrenalectomy + post-op hydrocortisone cover (contralateral suppressed); ACC — open + mitotane + EDP-M. Post-cure: hydrocortisone replacement until HPA recovery (months-yr; some lifelong); stress dose + MedicAlert; address DM/HTN/osteoporosis/depression (often persists). SSA: address topical steroid (skin lightening) + iatrogenic.
rationale: Endocrine Society Cushing's 2024 + Pituitary Society + LINC-3/4 osilodrostat.

title: Male hypogonadism — confirm two morning T + treat cause; TRT individualised + monitor
recommendation: TWO morning T (< 264-280 ng/dL or 9.2-9.7 nmol/L) + symptoms required. LH/FSH: high primary (testicular failure — karyotype/Klinefelter); low/normal secondary (HPG — prolactin/MRI pituitary/iron studies haemochromatosis/opioid/steroid/anabolic abuse/severe illness/obesity/OSA). PSA + DRE + FBC (haematocrit) + lipid + HbA1c + DEXA. TREAT CAUSE: obesity (weight loss reverses functional); OSA (CPAP); opioid taper; pituitary mass (surgery/cabergoline for prolactinoma); haemochromatosis phlebotomy; anabolic steroid abuse cessation + counsel. FERTILITY consideration BEFORE TRT — if desired: hCG ± FSH (secondary), clomiphene/SERM (off-label preserves fertility); sperm banking; TRT SUPPRESSES SPERMATOGENESIS — reversible months. TRT INDICATIONS: symptomatic + biochemical hypogonadism + no contraindications. CONTRAINDICATIONS: untreated prostate ca, active breast ca, severe LUTS, HCT > 54%, severe HF, untreated OSA, planned fertility 6 mo, suspicious PSA/DRE without urology. Formulations: IM testosterone enanthate/cypionate 100-200 mg q1-2 wk or undecanoate 1000 mg q10-14 wk; transdermal gel 50-100 mg/d (avoid contact partners/children). Target mid-range normal (350-700 ng/dL). MONITOR T + HCT + PSA + DRE + lipid + glucose at 3, 6 mo then annual. AE: polycythaemia (reduce dose/phlebotomy), acne, gynaecomastia, fluid, OSA worsen, prostate. TRAVERSE NEJM 2023 — no increased MACE middle-aged hypogonadism + CV risk. Klinefelter: lifelong TRT + micro-TESE IVF. Older men T Trials NEJM 2016 — symptomatic improvement.
rationale: Endocrine Society 2024 + EAU + AUA + TRAVERSE + T Trials.

title: Menopause — individualised HRT + transdermal preferred for VTE risk + fezolinetant non-hormonal
recommendation: PARADIGM SHIFT — HRT effective + safe most women within 10 yr of menopause / under 60. Discuss benefits vs risks individualised. Postmenopausal bleeding INVESTIGATE (TVS + biopsy — endometrial cancer until proven). HRT: OESTROGEN transdermal preferred (estradiol patch 25-100 mcg twice weekly or gel — lower VTE; preferred > 35 yr / smokers / VTE risk / migraine with aura / hepatic); oral estradiol 1-2 mg/d; NEVER ethinyl estradiol (high VTE). PROGESTOGEN (women with uterus — endometrial protection): MICRONISED PROGESTERONE 100-200 mg nocte (most physiological — less metabolic/breast risk) or Mirena IUS 5 yr (convenient). VAGINAL OESTROGEN for GSM only (minimal systemic — even breast ca with oncology consent). POI < 40: continue HRT until natural menopausal age (51) — replacement not 'symptom'. Duration no fixed limit — reassess annually. ALTERNATIVES non-hormonal for VMS: SSRI (paroxetine/escitalopram/venlafaxine), gabapentin, clonidine, CBT, FEZOLINETANT 45 mg/d (NK3 antagonist — FDA 2023 first non-hormonal targeted). GSM: vaginal oestrogen + moisturiser + lubricant + ospemifene + DHEA prasterone. Risks: breast ca — minimal/none oestrogen-only (hysterectomy women) per WHI re-analysis; modest with combined > 5 yr; endometrial only with unopposed oestrogen — combine progestogen; VTE oral (transdermal no); stroke oral small (transdermal no); CV likely cardioprotective < 10 yr menopause / < 60 (timing hypothesis). Breast cancer — HRT contraindicated; vaginal oestrogen with oncology consent for severe GSM; non-hormonal alternatives.
rationale: NICE NG23 2024 + NAMS 2022 + IMS 2024 + WHI + PEACE + FEZ-MS.

title: Gender-affirming care — WPATH 8; informed consent; multidisciplinary; mental health priority
recommendation: PATIENT-CENTRED + AFFIRMATIVE — gender-affirming care reduces depression/suicide; gatekeeping harmful. Multidisciplinary (endo + mental health + primary + surgery). WPATH 8 + Endocrine Society 2017/2024. Informed consent model adults. SOCIAL affirmation FIRST + always (name/pronouns/presentation/legal). MENTAL HEALTH support + suicide prevention + minority stress + co-occurring (depression/anxiety/autism/eating) — don't delay affirmation. FERTILITY counselling BEFORE hormones (sperm/oocyte banking — partially reversible suppression). MASCULINISING: testosterone enanthate/cypionate IM 50-100 mg/wk or 100-200 mg q2 wk or undecanoate Nebido q10-14 wk; transdermal gel; target male physiological 300-700 ng/dL; effects voice (permanent) + facial/body hair (permanent) + menses cessation (3-6 mo — supplementary norethisterone if needed) + clitoral + muscle redistribution + polycythaemia; testosterone NOT contraceptive. FEMINISING: estradiol transdermal preferred (lower VTE — patches 100-200 mcg twice weekly or gel; especially > 35 yr/smokers/VTE risk); oral 2-8 mg/d alternative; NEVER ethinyl estradiol; ANTI-ANDROGEN — spironolactone 100-200 mg/d (monitor K+) or GnRH agonist or cyproterone; effects breast (often modest) + body fat + skin + reduced muscle/libido — voice + facial hair don't change (speech therapy + electrolysis). MONITORING: T + estradiol + LH/FSH + prolactin + HCT + LFT + lipid + K+ + BP. ADOLESCENT: specialist multidisciplinary; GnRH agonist (puberty suppression reversible); cross-hormones ~ 16; surgery typically adulthood. Cass Review 2024 — cautious evidence-based; ongoing debate; WPATH maintains affirming. Surgery: chest/genital/facial/voice/laryngoplasty + hyster/ooph/orchi per individual. Primary care routine per current anatomy (cervical/prostate/breast screening). SSA: significant criminalisation + stigma — confidentiality + safety + non-judgemental + advocate (Galck+ Kenya).
rationale: WPATH 8 + Endocrine Society 2024 + ICD-11 depathologised + Cass Review 2024.

title: PCOS — Rotterdam + lifestyle + metformin + COC + letrozole for fertility (NEJM 2014)
indicators: Rotterdam 2/3 criteria + exclusion of other causes
recommendation: Rotterdam (2 of 3 + exclude): hyperandrogenism + oligo-anovulation + polycystic ovary morphology (≥ 12 follicles 2-9 mm or > 10 ml). EXCLUDE: TSH/prolactin/17-OHP (CAH)/cortisol Cushing/androgen tumour/POI/HAIR-AN. Metabolic assessment: 75g OGTT diagnosis + 2-yearly + lipid + LFT + FibroScan + STOP-Bang + mental health + AMH (not diagnostic alone). LIFESTYLE foundation (regardless BMI): Mediterranean diet + 150-300 min exercise + 5-10% weight loss + sleep/OSA + smoking cessation + mental health. MENSTRUAL/ENDOMETRIAL: COC first-line (anti-androgen progestin drospirenone/cyproterone for hyperandrogenism); cyclical progestin if oestrogen CI; Mirena IUS (endometrial + contraception). HYPERANDROGENISM: COC + SPIRONOLACTONE 50-200 mg (contraception required — teratogenic); finasteride/dutasteride for severe; eflornithine topical facial; cosmetic. METABOLIC: METFORMIN 500-2000 mg/d (insulin resistance + menstrual + weight + GDM/T2DM prevention); GLP-1 RA / TIRZEPATIDE emerging powerful for obesity + metabolic; SGLT2i; inositol modest. FERTILITY (when desired): weight first; LETROZOLE 2.5-7.5 mg days 3-7 SUPERIOR (Pregnancy in PCOS NEJM 2014); clomiphene 50-150 mg older; metformin co-therapy; gonadotrophins/IUI/IVF; laparoscopic ovarian drilling selected; metabolic surgery for severe obesity. PREGNANCY: pre-conception optimise + monitor GDM 24-28 wk + pre-eclampsia + preterm; continue metformin; aspirin 75-150 mg from 12 wk. MENTAL HEALTH: screen + treat depression/anxiety/eating/body image. ENDOMETRIAL surveillance — TVS + biopsy if abnormal bleed/thickened. Adolescent: defer Rotterdam 2 yr post-menarche; lifestyle + COC + metformin. SSA more severe metabolic — integrate NCD strategy.
rationale: International PCOS 2023 (Monash/ESHRE/Endocrine Soc) + NICE NG215 + AE-PCOS + Pregnancy in PCOS NEJM 2014.

title: CSU — H1 antihistamine step-up to 4x then omalizumab; AVOID NSAIDs
recommendation: EAACI step-wise: 1) standard H1 non-sedating (cetirizine 10/loratadine 10/fexofenadine 180/desloratadine 5/bilastine 20/levocetirizine 5); 2) UP-DOSE to 4× standard (off-label evidence-based); 3) ADD OMALIZUMAB 300 mg SC q4 wk (XCUISITE/ASTERIA — 60-70% response, safe pregnancy); 4) refractory: ciclosporin 3-5 mg/kg, MTX, MMF; emerging — ligelizumab/dupilumab/remibrutinib. AVOID 1st-gen sedating, NSAIDs (worsen 30%), opioids. Rescue severe flare: pred 30-40 mg × 3-7 d (not chronic). UAS7/UCT for severity + response. Investigate vasculitis if lesions > 24h + bruising. HAE WITHOUT urticaria + ACE-i resistant: C1-INH level + function + C4 (low) — icatibant/lanadelumab/C1-INH replacement; stop ACE-i if drug-induced. Pregnancy: loratadine/cetirizine/levocetirizine + omalizumab emerging acceptance. Inducible — H1 + omalizumab refractory; avoid trigger.
rationale: EAACI/GA²LEN 2024 + BSACI + WAO + ASTERIA/GLACIAL.

title: Anaphylaxis — IM adrenaline thigh FIRST + observe biphasic + 2 auto-injectors at discharge
recommendation: IM ADRENALINE THIGH IMMEDIATELY (most important — delays kill): adult 0.5 mg IM (0.5 mL of 1:1000); adolescent > 30 kg 0.5 mg; child 6-12 yr 0.3 mg; 6 mo-6 yr 0.15 mg; infant < 6 mo 0.1-0.15 mg; REPEAT q5 min if no improvement. Position: supine with legs elevated (CV); upright if respiratory; LEFT LATERAL if pregnant. High-flow O2. Intubate EARLY if airway compromise (oedema progresses). 2 large-bore IV + crystalloid 20 mL/kg paeds or 1-2 L adult bolus. REFRACTORY (2+ doses + fluid): adrenaline IV infusion 0.1-1 mcg/kg/min titrated; noradrenaline; GLUCAGON 1-2 mg IV if on β-blocker; methylene blue for refractory. Adjuncts (NOT primary): hydrocortisone 200 mg IV (controversial), chlorphenamine 10 mg, salbutamol neb. Observe 4-6h min; longer for severe/refractory/β-blocker/asthmatic/late. DISCHARGE: 2 ADRENALINE AUTO-INJECTORS + train use + action plan (BSACI/WAO) + medic-alert + refer allergy specialist 4-6 wk + avoid trigger + 3-5 d antihistamine + counsel biphasic 5-20%. Pregnancy: left lateral tilt + same adrenaline dose + CTG + multi-D.
rationale: WAO 2024 + BSACI + EAACI + Resus Council UK.

title: Skin cancer — ABCDE for melanoma; excise + sentinel node + immunotherapy stage IV
indicators: pigmented lesion ABCDE / suspicious skin lesion
recommendation: Full-body skin exam + dermoscopy. Excisional biopsy 2-3 mm margin for suspected melanoma. Breslow + Clark + AJCC 8th + mitotic rate + ulceration + BRAF V600E test stage III/IV. SLNB for melanoma > 1 mm or 0.8-1 mm + adverse. CT/PET-CT staging III/IV. BCC: excision (4-5 mm low-risk / 5-10 mm high-risk / Mohs face/recurrent); topical imiquimod/5-FU superficial; vismodegib advanced. SCC: excision; Mohs face/high-risk/immunocompromised; CEMIPLIMAB advanced (EMPOWER-CSCC-1); field treatment for actinic. MELANOMA: excision margins 0.5/1/1-2/2 cm; stage III adjuvant anti-PD1 (pembrolizumab/nivolumab — KEYNOTE-054/CHECKMATE-238) or dabrafenib+trametinib (BRAFV600E — COMBI-AD); stage IV first-line: IPILIMUMAB+NIVOLUMAB (CHECKMATE-067 — 50% 5-yr survival) or anti-PD1 mono or relatlimab+nivolumab (RELATIVITY-047). BRAF V600E/K: dabrafenib+trametinib. Brain mets: ipi+nivo effective + SRS. T-VEC + TIL (LIFILEUCEL — Amtagvi FDA 2024) for advanced refractory. ACRAL MELANOMA common SSA + less BRAF — immunotherapy + KIT-targeted. ALBINISM populations (SSA) — extremely high SCC — sun protection + early intervention essential.
rationale: NCCN 2024 + AAD + ESMO + CHECKMATE-067 + KEYNOTE-054 + RELATIVITY-047.

title: Diabetic retinopathy — annual screen + anti-VEGF for PDR/DMO (Protocol S/T)
indicators: DM screening / abnormal fundus / DMO suspected
recommendation: ANNUAL SCREENING: T1DM age 12 or 5 yr post-Dx; T2DM at diagnosis; pregnancy each trimester; dilated fundus photography or OCT; AI screening emerging (deployable SSA primary care). ETDRS/ICDR staging. Foundation: tight HbA1c (individualised), BP < 130/80, statin, smoking cessation, avoid rapid HbA1c drop (paradoxical worsening). MILD-MOD NPDR: observe + optimise. SEVERE NPDR/PDR: PAN-RETINAL PHOTOCOAGULATION (PRP) or ANTI-VEGF (Protocol S NEJM 2015 — non-inferior + preferred if DMO co-exists); ranibizumab/aflibercept/bevacizumab (Avastin off-label cheaper — equivalent CATT/IVAN; widely used SSA). FARICIMAB (Vabysmo) longer duration. DMO centre-involving + vision impact: ANTI-VEGF (Protocol T — aflibercept superior at lower vision); steroid intravitreal (Ozurdex/Iluvien) 2nd-line; focal/grid laser non-centre. Vitrectomy for vitreous haemorrhage/tractional. Bevacizumab cost advocacy SSA. Kenya National Eye Health Plan + integrated DM + eye care.
rationale: AAO PPP 2024 + ICO + Protocol S + Protocol T + CATT/IVAN.

title: Cataract — phaco/MSICS with IOL; intra-cameral cefuroxime to prevent endophthalmitis
indicators: cataract impacting QoL / function / driving / reading
recommendation: Indications: VA affecting QoL/occupation, anisometropia, phacomorphic glaucoma, concurrent retinal/glaucoma surgery, congenital (urgent — amblyopia prevention < 6-12 wk). Pre-op biometry + optimise DM/HTN/anticoag. PHACOEMULSIFICATION gold standard developed; MSICS cost-effective high-volume SSA (Aravind/KCCO model — < $40/surgery — excellent outcomes). IOL: monofocal (most), toric (astigmatism), multifocal/EDOF (reduce glasses). Aseptic technique + INTRA-CAMERAL CEFUROXIME at end (reduces endophthalmitis 80% — ESCRS). Topical anaesthesia common. Post-op: topical antibiotic + steroid × 4 wk tapering; review d1/wk1/wk4; avoid heavy lifting/swimming/eye rubbing × 2 wk. Complications: endophthalmitis 0.05-0.1%, PCO (YAG laser in-office), CME, refractive surprise, retinal detachment (high myopes). Congenital cataract: urgent surgery first 6-12 wk + contact lens + IOL later + patching for amblyopia. Diabetic cataract: stabilise DR/DMO first + anti-VEGF if needed. SSA: LEADING blindness cause; scale-up MSICS programmes (KCCO, Sightsavers, Operation Eyesight) + train ophthalmic clinical officers + outreach + WHO VISION 2020 + Kenya National Eye Health Plan.
rationale: AAO PPP 2024 + ICO + NICE NG77 + ESCRS Endophthalmitis Study + IAPB World Vision.

title: POAG — SLT or latanoprost first-line (LiGHT); MIGS/trab if refractory; African ancestry earlier/aggressive
indicators: optic nerve damage + visual field defect ± raised IOP
recommendation: Screening: African ancestry + FH > 35 yr annual; general > 40 yr every 2-3 yr. Diagnosis: tonometry + gonioscopy + optic nerve + VF + OCT RNFL + pachymetry. Target IOP individualised (25-30% reduction mild, 30-40% mod, >40% + < 14 severe; < 12-14 NTG). FIRST-LINE: SLT (LiGHT NEJM 2019 — non-inferior + cost-effective + low SE + repeatable — first-line many guidelines especially SSA) OR PROSTAGLANDIN ANALOGUE evening (latanoprost 0.005% generic — most common; SE iris darkening, lash growth, periorbital changes). Add β-blocker (timolol — cautions asthma/HF/bradyarrhythmia), α2-agonist (brimonidine — avoid < 2 yr severe sedation), CAI (dorzolamide — sulpha caution), Rho-kinase (netarsudil) for additional IOP. FIXED COMBINATIONS for adherence. REFRACTORY: trabeculectomy + tube shunt (Baerveldt/Ahmed/Molteno) + MIGS (iStent/Hydrus/XEN combined with cataract); cyclophotocoagulation refractory. African ancestry — earlier onset + faster progression + more aggressive. Adherence < 50% chronic drops — major barrier; SLT addresses + simplify regimen + generic affordable KEML. Train primary care + ophth clinical officers SSA. Tele-ophthalmology community screening.
rationale: AAO PPP 2024 + EGS 5e + NICE NG81 + LiGHT NEJM 2019 + OHTS.

title: AMD — AREDS2 supplement dry; anti-VEGF wet (CATT/IVAN — bevacizumab equivalent + cheaper SSA)
indicators: central vision loss + drusen / metamorphopsia / OCT findings
recommendation: Diagnosis: VA + Amsler + slit-lamp + fundoscopy + OCT (gold standard) + OCT-A + fluorescein/ICG angiography. DRY AMD: AREDS2 supplements (vitamin C 500 + E 400 IU + lutein 10 + zeaxanthin 2 + zinc 80 + copper 2 — no β-carotene if smoker) reduce intermediate-advanced dry AMD progression 25%; SMOKING CESSATION (single most modifiable); Mediterranean diet; UV protection. GEOGRAPHIC ATROPHY (advanced dry): PEGCETACOPLAN (Syfovre) + AVACINCAPTAD PEGOL (Izervay) FDA 2023 — slow progression. WET AMD: INTRAVITREAL ANTI-VEGF first-line — ranibizumab/aflibercept/BEVACIZUMAB (Avastin off-label EQUIVALENT — CATT NEJM 2011 + IVAN BMJ 2012 — much cheaper, widely used SSA + low-cost settings); FARICIMAB (Vabysmo FDA 2022) longer durability (TENAYA/LUCERNE); brolucizumab caution (inflammation); high-dose aflibercept (PHOTON/PULSAR) longer interval. Loading 3 monthly then maintenance treat-and-extend with OCT. Port Delivery System (Susvimo). POLYPOIDAL CHOROIDAL VASCULOPATHY (common SSA/Asian): anti-VEGF + ICG-guided PDT. SUDDEN CENTRAL VISION LOSS/distortion = WET AMD until proven — URGENT ophth (early anti-VEGF works best). Low-vision rehab + depression screening + fellow eye risk (50% 5 yr) + Amsler self-monitor. Bevacizumab access advocacy SSA.
rationale: AAO PPP 2024 + ICO + AREDS/AREDS2 + CATT/IVAN + TENAYA/LUCERNE + OAKS/DERBY.

title: Retinal detachment — urgent surgery (macula-on within 24h preserves vision)
recommendation: SAME-DAY ophth referral. VA + dilated fundoscopy + indirect ophth + B-scan if dense vitreous haemorrhage + OCT macula (macula-on vs off — KEY prognostic). MACULA-ON detachment — URGENT surgery within 24h preserves > 90% near-normal vision. MACULA-OFF detachment > 7 d — vision recovery limited (50% 6/12 best). Strict bed rest + positioning + avoid Valsalva + antiemetic. SURGICAL: laser/cryopexy for break alone (prophylactic — acute PVD with tear); pneumatic retinopexy single superior break; scleral buckle (young/phakic); PARS PLANA VITRECTOMY most versatile + modern + with gas/oil tamponade; combined PPV + buckle for complex. Post-op: positioning 7-14 d for gas/oil; NO air travel/altitude with intraocular gas (expansion); topical antibiotic + steroid. Re-detachment 5-15% — redo or silicone oil. TRACTIONAL (DM-PDR/ROP/SCD): vitrectomy + anti-VEGF + treat underlying. EXUDATIVE: treat cause (VKH steroid/choroidal mass/malignant HTN/eclampsia). SSA limited vitreoretinal access — train + scale-up + community awareness of warning symptoms (flashes/floaters/curtain) + immediate referral. Kenya: KNH + Lions SightFirst + regional centres. SCD retinopathy + diabetic surveillance.
rationale: AAO PPP 2024 + ASRS Practice Guidelines.

title: Hearing loss — newborn screen 1-3-6 rule; hearing aids reduce dementia (Lancet 2024)
indicators: newborn screen positive / sudden loss / age-related / ototoxic exposure
recommendation: NEWBORN screening (OAE/AABR universal) — 1-3-6 RULE: screen by 1 mo, diagnose by 3 mo, INTERVENE by 6 mo (best language + cognitive outcomes). Congenital — confirm + early hearing aids + cochlear implant if severe-profound bilateral + early sign language; treat congenital CMV (ganciclovir/valganciclovir 6 mo — improves hearing) + TORCH screen.
