SUDDEN SNHL (within 72h) EMERGENCY — refer ENT within 1-2 wk for steroid window — PREDNISOLONE 1 mg/kg/d × 7-14 d taper + intratympanic dexamethasone alternative/salvage + MRI IAM to rule out retrocochlear; 1/3 recover, 1/3 partial, 1/3 permanent. AGE-RELATED: HEARING AIDS bilateral fitting — single most effective; OTC hearing aids FDA 2022 for mild-mod cheaper; HEARING AIDS REDUCE DEMENTIA 8% (Lancet Commission 2024 modifiable RF) + ACHIEVE trial JAMA 2023 — 48% cognitive decline reduction; address tinnitus. CONDUCTIVE: cerumen (drops + irrigation if no perforation), OME (grommets if persistent + hearing loss > 25 dB > 3 mo), tympanic perforation (tympanoplasty chronic), otosclerosis (stapedectomy/hearing aid). OTOTOXICITY: minimise aminoglycoside dose/duration; serial audiogram baseline + on cisplatin/aminoglycoside/vancomycin > 5-7 d; counsel early symptoms; genetic test m.1555A>G (common Kenya/SSA + Asia aminoglycoside hypersensitivity). COCHLEAR IMPLANT for severe-profound bilateral SNHL not benefiting from hearing aids — MDT evaluation + rehab. Ramsay-Hunt: acyclovir + steroid × 7-14 d. SSA: WHO World Hearing Report 2021 + advocate newborn screening rollout + affordable hearing aid access (WHO PPP) + Kenya National Eye+Hearing Health Plan.
rationale: WHO World Hearing 2021/2024 + AAO-HNS + NICE NG98 + Lancet Commission Dementia 2024 + ACHIEVE.

title: Uveitis — workup systemic + infectious; topical steroid + cycloplegic; adalimumab for non-infectious posterior
indicators: red painful eye + photophobia + AC cells/flare
recommendation: Slit-lamp + IOP + dilated fundoscopy + OCT macula + FFA/ICG for posterior. WORKUP per features: HLA-B27 + spondyloarthropathy; ACE + CXR + CT for sarcoidosis; ANA/ANCA/RF; TB IGRA + CXR (essential SSA); SYPHILIS RPR/TPPA ALWAYS (great mimic); HIV testing; toxoplasma serology + PCR vitreous; HSV/VZV/CMV PCR vitreous selected; Bartonella; Lyme; aqueous/vitreous sampling selected severe/atypical for PCR + cytology + culture. ANTERIOR UVEITIS: topical prednisolone acetate 1% frequent (q1-2h initially taper over weeks) + cyclopentolate 1% TID (prevent synechiae + ciliary spasm) + topical NSAID adjunct + IOP monitor (steroid-induced glaucoma). POSTERIOR/INTERMEDIATE/PANUVEITIS: systemic prednisolone 1 mg/kg/d taper over months + periocular/intravitreal steroid (Ozurdex/Iluvien); steroid-sparing IMMUNOMODULATORS (MTX/AZA/MMF first-line; ciclosporin/tacrolimus); ADALIMUMAB (VISUAL-I/II — first biologic approved non-infectious posterior); infliximab/tocilizumab/rituximab refractory. INFECTIOUS — treat infection FIRST (steroid cautious + after anti-infective): TB uveitis ATT 6-9 mo + steroid; SYPHILIS aqueous penicillin G IV × 10-14 d + LP; TOXO retinochoroiditis pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + folinic acid × 4-6 wk + pred for vision-threat or cotrim; HSV/VZV anterior valacyclovir 1 g TDS × 7-14 d; CMV retinitis (HIV) ganciclovir IV + intravitreal + valganciclovir; endophthalmitis intravitreal antibiotics + vitrectomy. BEHCET'S/VKH/sympathetic — aggressive immunosuppression. MASQUERADE (chronic/atypical/steroid-refractory) — vitrectomy + cytology + flow + MRI brain (CNS lymphoma). SSA: TB+syphilis+HIV+toxo common — workup essential + train + access biologic.
rationale: AAO PPP 2024 + SUN 2024 + VISUAL I/II + IUSG.

title: SLE — HCQ for everyone; lupus nephritis triple therapy (MMF/CYC + steroid + belimumab/voclosporin)
indicators: multisystem ANA+ disease meeting EULAR criteria
recommendation: HCQ 5 mg/kg/d (max 400 mg) for ALL — disease activity + flare + CV + mortality; annual eye exam. Target LLDAS → remission on pred ≤ 5 mg. Mild flare: optimise HCQ + topical steroid + low pred + MTX 15-25/wk + belimumab. Mod-severe non-organ: pred 0.5 mg/kg + AZA/MMF + belimumab/anifrolumab. LUPUS NEPHRITIS III/IV/V: induction MMF 2-3 g or CYC Euro-lupus 500 mg q2wk × 6 + steroid (low-dose per PEXIVAS-style) + BELIMUMAB (BLISS-LN) or VOCLOSPORIN (AURORA); maintenance MMF/AZA × 3-5 yr + ACE-i/ARB BP < 130/80. Refractory: rituximab/anifrolumab; CD19 CAR-T emerging. NPSLE: high-dose steroid + CYC + rituximab. Pregnancy: HCQ throughout + ASA from wk 12; anti-Ro+ — fetal echo wk 16-26; APS+ — therapeutic LMWH; stop MMF/MTX/CYC pre-conception. Catastrophic APS: anticoag + steroid + IVIG + PLEX + rituximab + eculizumab. MAS: high-dose steroid + ciclosporin/anakinra. Vaccines (no live), TB+HBV+HIV screen + PJP prophylaxis on combined IS. SSA: more common + severe + LN; biosimilar belimumab + rituximab advocacy.
rationale: EULAR 2024 Lancet Rheumatol + ACR 2024 + BLISS-LN + AURORA-1/2 + PEXIVAS.

title: RA — MTX backbone early; biologic/JAKi if not at target by 3 mo
indicators: symmetric polyarthritis + RF/CCP+ + raised APR + EULAR/ACR criteria
recommendation: EARLY treat-to-target: MTX 15-25 mg/wk PO/SC + folic 5/wk (first-line) ± bridge pred 7.5-10 × 3 mo TAPER. Alternative csDMARD: SSZ 2-3 g, HCQ, leflunomide; triple therapy RACAT viable + cheap (MTX+SSZ+HCQ). If not at target (DAS28-CRP ≤ 3.2 or CDAI ≤ 10) at 3-6 mo: ADD biologic — TNFi first-line (etanercept/adalimumab/infliximab/golimumab/certolizumab; biosimilars cost) after TB/HBV/HIV screen + PJP if combined; alternatives — tocilizumab, abatacept, rituximab (refractory + RF/CCP+). JAKi (tofa/bari/upadacitinib) — BLACK BOX MACE/VTE/cancer if > 65 or smoker per ORAL Surveillance — cautious selection. Switch class after 3 mo no response. Dose-taper in sustained remission. Foundations: stop smoking + vaccines (no live; pneumo + flu + COVID + recombinant zoster) + CV RF + bone (DEXA + Ca/D + bisphos on pred). RA-ILD: continue MTX + abatacept/rituximab + nintedanib/pirfenidone progressive (INBUILD). Pregnancy: stop MTX/leflunomide/JAKi pre-conception; HCQ/SSZ/AZA/CsA + certolizumab safe; plan low-activity. SSA: csDMARD + MTX widely available; biosimilar TNFi advocacy.
rationale: EULAR 2023 + ACR 2021 + NICE NG100 + ORAL Surveillance + INBUILD.

title: AAV — rituximab or CYC induction + PEXIVAS low-dose pred + avacopan steroid-sparing
indicators: RPGN / pulmonary haemorrhage / ANCA+ / pauci-immune crescentic GN on biopsy
recommendation: SEVERE/organ-threatening: RITUXIMAB 375 mg/m² × 4 wk OR 1 g × 2 (RAVE/RITUXVAS — preferred for relapse/fertility) OR CYC pulse 15 mg/kg q2-3 wk (CYCLOPS) × 6-10 + PRED 1 mg/kg with PEXIVAS LOW-DOSE TAPER (NEJM 2020 — same efficacy + less infection) + AVACOPAN C5a antagonist ADVOCATE NEJM 2021 (steroid-sparing alternative). PLEX selective: anti-GBM overlap / severe pulmonary haemorrhage / very severe renal — PEXIVAS no overall benefit. Limited: MTX + pred or rituximab. MAINTENANCE 6-24 mo → 4 yr: RITUXIMAB 500 mg q6 mo × 4-5 yr (MAINRITSAN superior AZA) or AZA 2 mg/kg + wean pred ≤ 5. Relapse: rituximab + steroid. EGPA: induction same; add MEPOLIZUMAB anti-IL5 (MIRRA NEJM 2017) for relapsing/refractory/asthma component. ANCILLARIES: TB + HBV + HIV screen; PJP cotrim 480 TDS on pred > 20 + IS; vaccines (no live); CV RF + bone health; fertility (sperm/ovum cryo); bladder cancer surveillance long-term (CYC cumulative); cotrim long-term in localised GPA (Stegeman) reduces relapse. ANCA+anti-GBM: triple — PLEX + CYC/rituximab + steroid. SSA: CYC backbone affordable; rituximab biosimilar advocacy; train nephrology/rheum + biopsy capacity.
rationale: EULAR 2024 + ACR 2021 + KDIGO 2024 + PEXIVAS + ADVOCATE + MAINRITSAN + MIRRA.

title: Axial SpA — physio + continuous NSAID; TNFi or IL-17i if ASDAS ≥ 2.1 after 2 NSAID trials
indicators: inflammatory back pain + sacroiliitis MRI/X-ray + raised CRP
recommendation: ASAS-EULAR 2022: physio + exercise + stop smoking. Phase I: continuous NSAID (naproxen 500 BD or celecoxib 200 BD) × 2-4 wk × 2 trials — continuous suppresses radiographic progression. Phase II if ASDAS ≥ 2.1 or BASDAI ≥ 4: TNFi (eta/adali/infli/goli/certo; biosimilars; TB/HBV/HIV screen) OR IL-17i (secu/ixe/bimekizumab) — avoid IL-17 in IBD overlap (worsens). Phase III: switch class after 3-4 mo no response. Phase IV: JAKi (upadacitinib SELECT-AXIS) — Black Box MACE/VTE/cancer per ORAL Surveillance — refractory. PERIPHERAL arthritis: SSZ 2-3 g (no axial role). UVEITIS recurrent: adalimumab > secukinumab. IBD overlap: monoclonal TNFi (adali/infli) — NOT etanercept (poor IBD) NOT IL-17. PSORIASIS overlap: IL-17 or TNFi (avoid IL-17 in IBD). CARDIAC (AR + conduction): echo + ECG surveillance. OSTEOPOROSIS: DEXA + bisphosphonate (high fracture in ankylosed spine). SPINE FRACTURE even minor trauma: FULL spine imaging (MRI > CT) + surgical referral. Vaccines (no live). Pregnancy: certolizumab safest TNFi (low transfer); SSZ/HCQ OK; stop MTX/leflunomide/JAKi pre-conception. SSA: NSAID + physio affordable; biosimilar TNFi access advocacy.
rationale: ASAS-EULAR 2022 + ACR 2019 + SELECT-AXIS.

title: Gout — treat-to-target urate < 360 lifelong ULT; HLA-B*58:01 test in Han Chinese
indicators: acute monoarthritis + crystals / tophi / classic clinical
recommendation: ACUTE within 24h: NSAID (naproxen 500 BD or indo or diclo) × 5-7 d (caution CKD/PUD/anticoag) OR COLCHICINE 1 mg stat then 0.5 mg 1h then 0.5 mg BD-TDS × 3-5 d (renal-adjust + statin/macrolide/grapefruit interaction) OR PRED 30-40 mg × 5 d (DM-friendly; HF cautious) OR IA steroid single joint. IL-1i (canakinumab/anakinra) refractory + multi-comorbid. CONTINUE existing ULT. EXCLUDE septic — aspirate + Gram/culture. ULT lifelong if > 1 flare/yr, tophi, X-ray erosions, CKD ≥ 2, urolithiasis: ALLOPURINOL first-line — start 100 mg (50 if CKD) titrate q2-4 wk up to 300-900 mg to TARGET urate < 360 μmol/L (< 6 mg/dL) or < 300 if tophi; HLA-B*58:01 TEST before allopurinol in Han Chinese/Korean/Thai (allopurinol-DRESS); febuxostat 80-120 mg 2nd-line (FAST Lancet 2020 reassuring after CARES); probenecid/benzbromarone uricosuric (avoid in stones/CKD); pegloticase severe refractory. PROPHYLAXIS at ULT initiation: colchicine 0.5 OD-BD × 3-6 mo (paradoxical flares as tophi mobilise). CONTINUE LIFELONG. LIFESTYLE: limit alcohol (esp beer), purines, fructose; weight loss; treat metabolic syndrome; switch thiazide/loop to losartan/CCB (losartan mild uricosuric). CV + CKD RF. PSEUDOGOUT (CPPD) — positively birefringent rhomboid — NSAID/colchicine/steroid. SSA: allopurinol cheap + widely available; education on lifelong ULT essential (adherence < 50%).
rationale: ACR 2020 + EULAR 2016/2024 + BSR 2017 + FAST + CARES.

title: PMR/GCA — immediate steroid on suspicion; tocilizumab steroid-sparing in GCA (GiACTA)
indicators: > 50 yr + shoulder/hip girdle pain + raised APR (PMR) OR new HA + jaw claudication + visual sx + temporal artery (GCA)
recommendation: PMR: pred 12.5-25 mg/d × 2-4 wk → reduce 2.5 mg/2-4 wk to 10 mg × 4-6 wk → 1 mg/4-8 wk → off by 1-2 yr; relapse common — return to last effective dose + slower taper. Steroid-sparing MTX 7.5-15/wk; tocilizumab refractory. GCA: START HIGH-DOSE STEROID IMMEDIATELY on clinical suspicion (don't wait for biopsy) — vision-threatened METHYLPRED 500-1000 IV × 3 d → pred 60 mg/d × 4 wk; no visual involvement pred 40-60 × 4 wk; continue 12-24 mo taper based on response + APR. ASA 75-100 + PPI. TOCILIZUMAB 162 mg SC weekly (or 8 mg/kg IV q4 wk) — GiACTA NEJM 2017 — steroid-sparing new-onset + relapsing, reduces flares + cumulative steroid; relapse on taper → ADD tocilizumab. MTX modest steroid-sparing alternative. AVOID rapid steroid taper (relapse). STEROID ADJUNCTS: DEXA + Ca + D + bisphosphonate (FRAX > 10% major or > 70); PJP cotrim if pred > 20 + IS; PPI; BP+glucose+lipid monitor; vaccines (no live). AORTIC SURVEILLANCE annual chest imaging (LV-GCA + aneurysm). Biopsy-negative + halo on US + steroid response = treat as GCA. Pre-tocilizumab: TB+HBV+HCV screen + LFT + lipids baseline. SSA: pred + ASA + bisphos available; tocilizumab access advocacy.
rationale: BSR 2020 + ACR/VF 2021 + EULAR 2024 + GiACTA.

title: SCD — universal HU + penicillin + TCD; gene therapy curative (Casgevy/Lyfgenia 2023); REACH SSA HU
indicators: confirmed Hb SS / SC / Sβ-thal — newborn or older
recommendation: FOUNDATIONS: PEN V prophylaxis to age 5 (125 BD < 3 yr, 250 BD 3-5 yr) — reduces pneumococcal sepsis 84% (PROPS); VACCINES — pneumococcal (PCV13+PPV23 boosters) + Hib + meningococcal ACWY+B + flu + COVID + HBV + malaria where endemic; FOLATE 5 mg/d lifelong; hydration + avoid extremes + altitude; malaria prophylaxis SSA. HYDROXYUREA from AGE 9 mo (BABY-HUG + REACH SSA NEJM 2019) 20-35 mg/kg/d titrated — reduces VOC + ACS + transfusion + mortality + reduces malaria (REACH) — UNIVERSAL OFFER. L-glutamine 5-15 g BD; voxelotor (status under review 2024 — withdrawn worldwide — verify); crizanlizumab anti-P-sel (STAND mixed). Chronic transfusion + chelation (deferasirox/deferoxamine) for stroke/abnormal TCD/recurrent ACS. ANNUAL TCD age 2-16 — > 200 cm/s start chronic transfusion (STOP trial); annual echo (PHT), urine (proteinuria), retina, DEXA, dental. ACUTE VOC: morphine PCA (NOT pethidine — neurotoxic) + paracetamol + NSAID (renal-cautious) + non-pharm + screen infection + antibiotic if any fever; avoid IV fluid overload (→ ACS). ACUTE CHEST: ceftriaxone+macrolide + simple transfusion early + EXCHANGE if severe + bronchodilator + O2 + spirometer. STROKE: exchange transfusion within 6-12h target HbS < 30% + chronic transfusion or HU (TWiTCH non-inferior). Priapism > 4h: aspirate + adrenaline + urology. CURATIVE: allo-HSCT matched sibling best; GENE THERAPY exa-cel CASGEVY (CRISPR-BCL11A) + lovo-cel Lyfgenia (lentivirus) FDA 2023 — eligible severe — cost + access advocacy. Pregnancy: MDT + folate + LMWH prophylaxis + transfusion threshold + pre-eclampsia/IUGR prevention. SSA: HU+pen+vaccines+malaria prophylaxis + newborn screening scale-up; gene therapy access advocacy.
rationale: BSH 2018/21 + ASH 2020 + WHO SCD Africa + REACH + BABY-HUG + STOP + CASGEVY/Lyfgenia FDA 2023.

title: ITP — observe if plt > 30 no bleed; dex pulse first-line; TPO-RA before splenectomy chronic
indicators: isolated thrombocytopenia + petechiae/mucosal bleed + diagnosis of exclusion
recommendation: Exclude HIV/HCV/HBV/SLE/APS/HP/drugs; FBC+film+coag normal; BM selective. OBSERVE if plt > 30 + no bleed (most spontaneous remission). FIRST-LINE (bleed or plt < 30 + bleeding risk): DEXAMETHASONE 40 mg/d × 4 d (preferred ASH 2019 — fast + equivalent + less prolonged steroid) OR PRED 1 mg/kg × 1-2 wk taper 6-8 wk; OR IVIG 1 g/kg × 1-2 doses if rapid response needed (bleed/pregnancy/pre-op); anti-D in Rh+ non-splenectomised. SECOND-LINE chronic (most adults need): TPO-RA preferred over splenectomy first (ASH 2019) — eltrombopag 50 mg (East Asian start 25; food/cation/dairy interaction), romiplostim SC weekly, avatrombopag oral — response 80%; thrombosis + hepatic + marrow fibrosis (rare). RITUXIMAB 375 mg/m² × 4 wk — durable 20-30% — HBV screen. Fostamatinib refractory. THIRD-LINE: splenectomy (durable 60%) — VACCINATE pre-op (pneumo+Hib+menACWY+B) + pen V lifelong + counsel sepsis; MMF/CYC/dapsone/danazol. EMERGENCY bleed/pre-op/critical: platelets + IVIG 1 g/kg + IV methylpred 1 g + TXA + source control. PAED: most self-limit — observe if mild + no bleed (BSH/ASH watchful waiting); treat IVIG/pred/anti-D if bleed. PREG: observe mild — sever pred + IVIG; avoid TPO-RA/rituximab; deliver plt > 50 vaginal > 80 LSCS/epi; check neonate. HP eradicate if +. AVOID ASA/NSAID/antiplatelet/IM. Soft toothbrush + electric razor; no contact sport low plt. Vaccines (no live during IS). SSA: pred + dex + IVIG widely; TPO-RA + rituximab access advocacy; splenectomy with vaccines + prophylaxis.
rationale: ASH 2019 + International ITP WG 2019 + BSH.

title: AIHA — pred first-line warm; rituximab + sutimlimab cold (CADENZA/CARDINAL)
indicators: haemolytic anaemia + DAT+ (IgG warm or C3d cold)
recommendation: WARM AIHA (DAT IgG+ ± C3d, spherocytes): pred 1 mg/kg × 3-4 wk taper over 6 mo (don't rush — relapse); response 70-80% but sustained off pred 20% only. RITUXIMAB 375 mg/m² × 4 wk increasingly 1st/2nd-line non-steroid (70% response). Refractory: MMF, CYC, AZA, CsA, splenectomy (now less common). Severe acute: IVIG 1 g/kg + methylpred pulse + PLEX + transfuse (least-incompatible — don't withhold). Folate 5/d. PROPHYLAXIS chronic steroid: bone (Ca/D + bisphos) + PJP if combined IS + vaccines (no live) + cardio + glucose. COLD AGGLUTININ: avoid cold + warm fluids/blood; steroids less effective; RITUXIMAB ± bendamustine (CADENZA); SUTIMLIMAB anti-C1s IV q2 wk (CARDINAL/CADENZA — FDA 2022 first approved cold AIHA); treat underlying lymphoproliferative. PCH (Donath-Landsteiner): viral/syphilis + supportive. DRUG-INDUCED: STOP drug + supportive. EVANS (AIHA+ITP): steroid + rituximab + chronic relapsing. Workup secondary: ANA/Ig/lymphadenopathy/CT/flow/BM/lympho; HIV/HCV/HBV/Mycoplasma/EBV. PREG: pred + IVIG + folate; rituximab cautious; monitor anaemia + transfuse if severe + neonate. TRANSFUSION: cross-match difficult — involve transfusion medicine + least-incompatible if life-threat. SSA: pred + folate + steroid available; rituximab + sutimlimab advocacy.
rationale: BSH 2017 + International AIHA Consensus 2020 + CARDINAL/CADENZA.

title: Thalassaemia — transfusion + chelation + luspatercept + gene therapy; G6PD — avoid oxidants + test before primaquine
indicators: microcytic anaemia + Hb electrophoresis abnormality / haemolysis post-oxidant exposure
recommendation: β-THAL MAJOR: transfusion q3-4 wk maintain pre-transfusion Hb 95-105; CHELATION (ferritin > 1000 or > 10-20 tx) — deferasirox 20-40 mg/kg OD (first-line modern) OR deferiprone 75-100 mg TDS (cardiac iron good; agranulocytosis FBC monitor) OR deferoxamine SC 8-12h × 5-7 nights; combination for severe cardiac iron; T2* cardiac+liver MRI annual + ferritin q3 mo; folate 5/d + Ca/D; splenectomy selective (vaccines + lifelong pen V); endocrine + cardiac + hepatic + osteoporosis surveillance + treat. LUSPATERCEPT q3 wk (BELIEVE NEJM 2020) reduces transfusion burden non-curative. ALLO-HSCT matched sibling curative young. GENE THERAPY: betibeglogene (Zynteglo lentiviral FDA 2022) + exa-cel CASGEVY (CRISPR BCL11A FDA 2024) — curative severe transfusion-dependent (cost + access). β-INTERMEDIA: intermittent + chelation + HU trial + luspatercept. α-thal HbH: folate + intermittent tx; Bart's hydrops: IUT + intensive + curative HSCT. ANTENATAL screen + COUNSELLING + PGD/CVS for at-risk couples. G6PD: lifelong avoid OXIDANTS — fava beans, primaquine (TEST before in malaria-endemic — Kenya MoH; tafenoquine REQUIRES > 70% activity), dapsone, sulfa, naphthalene, nitrofurantoin, methylene blue (CONTRAINDICATED + worsens), certain quinolones, rasburicase, henna; medical alert card + family screen. Acute haemolysis: STOP trigger + HYDRATE (prevent AKI from haemoglobinuria) + transfuse if Hb < 60/symptomatic; no methylene blue. Favism severe: admit + transfuse + hydrate. Neonatal jaundice: phototherapy + exchange if severe — kernicterus prevention. P. vivax radical cure: primaquine 0.25-0.75 mg/kg × 14 d (G6PD-def: weekly 0.75 × 8 wk supervised; tafenoquine single-dose REQUIRES G6PD test); ACT for blood-stage. POC G6PD test scale-up (CareStart, SD Biosensor) before tafenoquine + dapsone. SSA: newborn screen + premarital + antenatal carrier; HU + transfusion + chelation programmes; deferasirox biosimilar advocacy.
rationale: TIF 2023 + BSH + BELIEVE + WHO G6PD/tafenoquine + CASGEVY/Zynteglo.

title: Schistosomiasis — PZQ 40 mg/kg single dose (60 mg/kg S. japonicum); FGS workup + HIV link
indicators: terminal haematuria / chronic abdominal sx / freshwater exposure / FGS
recommendation: PRAZIQUANTEL 40 mg/kg PO single dose (60 mg/kg divided for S. japonicum/mekongi). Repeat 4-6 wk if heavy infection or persistent symptoms (immature schistosomula not killed first dose). SAFE in pregnancy + lactation (WHO 2006 reversed). Paediatric > 2 yr standard dose; under-6 paediatric arpraziquantel emerging. Adverse: abdo pain + dizziness + urticaria — transient. Acute Katayama: add pred 30-60 mg/d for immune reaction + repeat PZQ at 4-6 wk. MDA in endemic — annual/biennial school-age (target 75% WHO 2030). FGS: PZQ doesn't reverse lesions — repeat treatment + counsel + HIV prevention/PrEP (3-4× acquisition risk) + fertility support + condom + cervical screen. Workup: terminal urine microscopy + stool Kato-Katz + serology in traveller + urine CCA POC + US abdomen (hepatic fibrosis + hydronephrosis + bladder); FBC eosinophilia + IgE. Complications: variceal bleed (band ligation + β-blocker), hydronephrosis (urology), bladder cancer surveillance, pulm HT (PAH specialist), neuroschistosomiasis (steroid + PZQ + decompression). Vector + WASH + behaviour change. SSA: Kenya — Lake Victoria + Tana basin + coast; integrate school MDA + community awareness + FGS recognition.
rationale: WHO 2022 Schistosomiasis Guideline + 2030 Roadmap + Kenya National Programme.

title: VL kala-azar — Indian LAmB 10 mg/kg single; East African SSG + paromomycin 17 d; LAmB HIV/pregnancy
indicators: chronic fever + splenomegaly + pancytopenia endemic area
recommendation: Diagnosis: splenic/BM aspirate + rK39 RDT (≥ 95% sens) + DAT + PCR. HIV TEST ALWAYS. INDIAN SUBCONTINENT: LAmB 10 mg/kg SINGLE DOSE preferred (WHO 2010 elimination) — ≥ 95% cure. EAST AFRICA (Kenya/Sudan/Ethiopia/Uganda/Somalia/S Sudan): SSG 20 mg/kg/d IM/IV + paromomycin 15 mg/kg/d IM × 17 d (WHO/MSF combination first-line); SSG alone × 30 d historic; LAmB 30 mg/kg total in 6 doses (5 mg/kg × 6 over 10 d) — preferred HIV + pregnancy + costly; miltefosine 100 mg/d × 28 d emerging. MEDITERRANEAN/BRAZIL: LAmB 3 mg/kg × days 1-5 + 10 (total 21 mg/kg). HIV co-infected: LAmB 30-40 mg/kg + secondary prophylaxis (LAmB monthly or pentamidine) until CD4 > 200-350 × 6 mo on ART + START ART. PREGNANCY: LAmB preferred (avoid miltefosine teratogenic + SSG cardiac). PKDL: India miltefosine × 12 wk or LAmB; Sudanese LAmB × 20 or SSG + paromomycin. Monitor: clinical + spleen + paraitology selective; > 6-12 mo follow relapse. Pre-treatment ECG (SSG QT) + LFT + amylase + FBC + HIV. Vector + reservoir control + case finding (anthroponotic East Africa). SSA: Kenya — Baringo/Marigat/Pokot/Eastern + S Sudan refugees; MSF + DNDi + WHO programmes; LAmB access advocacy; train HCWs + integrate HIV.
rationale: WHO 2022 Leishmaniasis Guideline + MSF VL Field Guide + DNDi LEAP + Kenya 2021.

title: CL — local for simple Old World; systemic for L. braziliensis (mucocutaneous risk) + complex
indicators: chronic ulcer / nodule after sandfly exposure endemic area
recommendation: DIAGNOSIS: slit-skin smear/scraping Giemsa + biopsy + culture + PCR (species essential). DECIDE local vs systemic — SPECIES (L. braziliensis ALWAYS systemic — mucocutaneous risk; L. aethiopica systemic), number > 4 or > 4 cm or face/joints — systemic; immunocompromised — systemic. LOCAL (single small away from face/joints + Old World non-braziliensis): cryotherapy weekly × 3-6; thermotherapy 50°C × 30s (ThermoMed); intralesional pentavalent antimony × 3-5; paromomycin 15% + methylbenzethonium/urea topical × 20 d; imiquimod adjunct; observation (scars). SYSTEMIC (face/joints/multiple/large/braziliensis/IC): pentavalent antimony (SSG/meglumine) 20 mg/kg/d × 20 d Old World / × 28 d New World (ECG + LFT + amylase + FBC monitor); miltefosine 2.5 mg/kg × 28 d (oral; teratogenic; effective L. major/mexicana/donovani — less braziliensis); LAmB 3 mg/kg × 6 (IC/pregnancy/refractory/L. aethiopica/tropica); pentamidine L. guyanensis. MUCOCUTANEOUS: pentavalent antimony × 28-30 OR LAmB OR amphotericin B deoxycholate + ENT/reconstruction. Diffuse CL: pentavalent + IFN-γ; long-term. Pregnancy: LAmB; defer mild non-braziliensis post-partum. Prevention: DEET + permethrin + bed nets + avoid dusk-dawn. SSA: Kenya — L. tropica/aethiopica/major in Baringo/Pokot/Turkana — biopsy + PCR scale-up + LAmB access for severe.
rationale: WHO 2022 Leishmaniasis Guideline + PAHO + LeishGEN.

title: Dengue — warning signs day 4-7 capillary leak; AVOID NSAID/ASA; platelet tx only major bleed
indicators: acute fever + thrombocytopenia + endemic area / outbreak
recommendation: Phase recognition critical: febrile day 1-3 → CRITICAL day 4-7 (defervescence + capillary leak) → recovery day 8+. WARNING SIGNS day 4-7 (ADMIT): abdo pain + persistent vomiting + clinical fluid accumulation + mucosal bleed + lethargy/restless + hepatomegaly > 2 cm + rising Hct + falling plt. TRIAGE: Group A no warning — outpatient + ORS + paracetamol + bed rest + AVOID NSAID/ASA (bleeding) + return precautions day 4-7. Group B warning sign or comorbid/age/pregnant — ADMIT IV fluid + monitor. Group C severe (shock/severe haemorrhage/organ) — ICU. FLUIDS: CRYSTALLOID titrated to maintenance + replacement; shock initial 10-20 mL/kg over 1h → reassess (more if persistent); colloid (5% albumin) if persistent shock + rising Hct; STOP IV fluid in recovery (reabsorption) — avoid pulmonary oedema. PLATELET TRANSFUSION ONLY for active major bleed OR plt < 10 + sx (NOT prophylactic — IFEX-DENGUE Lancet 2017 no benefit). FFP/cryo/blood for actual bleed + coag. Paracetamol fever only; AVOID NSAID/ASA/IM. NO steroid (no benefit shock). EXCLUDE malaria (CO-INFECTION COMMON) + chikungunya + typhoid + leptospirosis + COVID. Diagnosis: NS1 day 1-5 + IgM/IgG paired + PCR + Hct serial + FBC + LFT + UEC + clotting. PREG: severe maternal + neonatal — admit + monitor; vertical near-term. Vaccines: Qdenga TAK-003 (WHO SAGE 2024 recommended endemic 6-16 regardless serostatus); Dengvaxia restricted seropositive 9-45 yr. Aedes vector control + DEET (daytime biting). SSA: Kenya — Mombasa/coast 2024 outbreak — train warning signs + fluid + co-infection differential.
rationale: WHO 2024 Dengue Guideline + WHO SAGE 2024 + TIDES TAK-003 + Kenya MoH 2024.

title: LF — IDA triple (DEC+IVM+ABZ) MDA except Loa-endemic; MMDP for lymphoedema + hydrocele surgery
indicators: microfilaraemia / chronic lymphoedema / hydrocele / ADL endemic area
recommendation: MDA: IDA TRIPLE THERAPY single dose — IVERMECTIN 200 μg/kg + DEC 6 mg/kg + ALBENDAZOLE 400 mg annually 5+ yr (WHO 2017 — accelerated clearance) — WHERE LOA LOA NOT CO-ENDEMIC. LOA LOA CO-ENDEMIC (Central Africa — Cameroon/Gabon/CAR/DRC/Congo/S Nigeria/Eq Guinea/S Sudan) — IDA + DEC CONTRAINDICATED (encephalopathy) — IVM + ALB only OR doxycycline (anti-Wolbachia 200 mg/d × 4-6 wk). Onchocerciasis co-endemic — IVM + ALB (no DEC — Mazzotti). 65% coverage 5+ yr → interrupt transmission. INDIVIDUAL: DEC 6 mg/kg × 12 d kills microfilariae + adult; doxycycline 200 mg/d × 4-6 wk anti-Wolbachia sterilising; IVM + ALB microfilaricidal. MORBIDITY MANAGEMENT (MMDP — equally important): LYMPHOEDEMA hygiene daily wash + soap + dry + cellulitis treatment + skin care + emollients + elevation + gentle exercise + compression + train self-care + treat ADL (antibiotic + paracetamol + elevation). HYDROCELE surgical excision (hydrocelectomy) + train surgeons + integrated. Chyluria: dietary fat restriction + MCT + sclerosing/surgical. Tropical pulmonary eosinophilia: DEC × 21 d. Diagnosis: night blood smear (W. bancrofti nocturnal) + FTS day-time POC antigen + Brugia BmR1 + US (filaria dance + hydrocele); LOA LOA TEST BEFORE MDA (encephalopathy > 30,000 mf/mL). Vector control integrated. WHO 2030 elimination — many countries verified. SSA: Kenya — coastal/Lamu/Tana River — MDA + MMDP integrated.
rationale: WHO 2030 GPELF + IDA 2017 + MMDP + Kenya National LF.

title: Onchocerciasis — annual IVM CDTI; LoaScope test in co-endemic; doxycycline + moxidectin newer
indicators: pruritus / leopard skin / nodule / visual loss endemic Africa
recommendation: MDA: IVERMECTIN 150 μg/kg single dose annual or BIANNUAL community-directed treatment (CDTI) × 12-15 yr (adult worm 14 yr). MOXIDECTIN single dose (FDA 2018) superior mf clearance + duration vs IVM — adult > 12 yr — emerging adjunct. LOA LOA CO-ENDEMIC (Cameroon/Gabon/CAR/DRC/S Nigeria/S Sudan/Congo/Eq Guinea) — TEST FIRST (LoaScope individual screening; > 30,000 mf/mL DO NOT GIVE IVM — encephalopathy + death; alternative — DOXYCYCLINE programme 100-200 mg/d × 4-6 wk anti-Wolbachia kills adult sterilising). AVOID DEC for onchocerciasis (severe Mazzotti). Individual: IVM 150 μg/kg q3-6 mo (multiple + better sx); doxy 4-6 wk for sterilisation; surgical nodulectomy selected (head/face risk eye); topical permethrin/antihistamine for itch. Eye: ophth + iritis + secondary infection. NODDING SYNDROME (children S Sudan + Uganda): AED + supportive + nutrition + psychosocial. Diagnosis: skin snip 24h saline → microfilariae; Ov16 ELISA/RDT; PCR; slit lamp; LOA LOA microfilarial count BEFORE IVM. SIMULIUM black fly riverine larviciding (historic OCP 1974-2002 — eliminated 11 West African — landmark). LATAM elimination Ecuador/Colombia/Mexico/Guatemala verified. SSA: Kenya not endemic — cross-border + research; ESPEN coordinates.
rationale: WHO + APOC + Mectizan Donation Program + Awadzi Moxidectin Lancet 2018 + A-WOL.

title: HAT — fexinidazole oral first-line T.b. gambiense (revolutionary 2019); acoziborole single dose pipeline
indicators: fever + lymphadenopathy / sleep disturbance / neuro / endemic area
recommendation: T.b. GAMBIENSE (95% — West/Central Africa): FEXINIDAZOLE ORAL — 1800 mg OD × 4 d then 1200 mg OD × 6 d (> 35 kg adults; adolescents > 6 yr + > 20 kg weight-adjusted) WITH FOOD — first all-oral HAT treatment (DNDi-Sanofi WHO 2019) — AVOIDS LP for staging in most + simplifies rural management — REVOLUTIONARY. Severe stage 2 (CSF WBC > 100): NECT (nifurtimox + eflornithine combination — eflornithine 400 mg/kg IV q6h × 7 d + nifurtimox PO × 10 d) OR fexinidazole. Pentamidine historic stage 1. Melarsoprol historic (5% encephalopathy death) — no longer first-line. NEW: ACOZIBOROLE single oral dose × 1 — NEJM 2022 — under regulatory review — pipeline game-changer. T.b. RHODESIENSE (East/South Africa): SURAMIN IV stage 1; MELARSOPROL stage 2 (toxic but limited alternative); fexinidazole + acoziborole trials. DIAGNOSIS: T.b. gambiense — CATT screening + lymph node aspirate/blood/chancre wet prep + Giemsa + mAECT + capillary tube. T.b. rhodesiense — blood smear (high parasitaemia). STAGING — LP CSF WBC + trypanosomes — fexinidazole reduces LP need. FOLLOW: clinical + LP 6-12-18-24 mo cure; fexinidazole simplifies. PUBLIC HEALTH: active case detection mobile + tsetse vector control (traps + targets + Trypa-NO insecticide cloth) + One Health (cattle reservoir rhodesiense) + WHO elim transmission 2030. WHO elim public health problem gambiense 2020 ACHIEVED. PREG: limited fexinidazole data; eflornithine + pentamidine selected. SSA: Kenya — cross-border Uganda/Tanzania (rhodesiense); surveillance + tsetse + One Health.
rationale: WHO 2019/2024 HAT + DNDi fexinidazole Mesu Lancet 2018 + Acoziborole NEJM 2022 + 2030 NTD Roadmap.

title: Chagas — benznidazole × 60 d; treat acute + congenital + chronic < 50 yr + reactivation; cardiac follow-up
indicators: positive serology Latin American origin / acute fever + Romaña / congenital screening / CCM
recommendation: ANTITRYPANOSOMAL INDICATED: ALL acute, ALL congenital, ALL chronic ≤ 18 yr (high cure), adults < 50 yr without advanced cardiomyopathy (BENEFIT NEJM 2015 — no benefit in advanced CCM but pre-fibrosis stages recommended), reactivation, WCBA outside pregnancy. DRUGS: BENZNIDAZOLE 5-7 mg/kg/d (up to 10 in children) × 60 d first-line; NIFURTIMOX 8-10 mg/kg/d × 60 d (or 60 wk children) alternative. Adverse — common — rash benz (severe possible), GI, peripheral neuropathy nifurtimox — monitor + counsel. BENDITA emerging shorter regimens. PREG: DO NOT TREAT (teratogenic) — treat post-delivery; treat NEONATE within first year if congenital (high cure). CARDIAC chronic CCM: HF per HFrEF GDMT (β-blocker + ACE-i/ARB/ARNI + MRA + SGLT2i); pacemaker for AV block (common); ICD for VT/VF; anticoagulate LV thrombus or AF; cardiac transplant + post-transplant reactivation surveillance. DIGESTIVE: oesophageal dilatation / Heller + fundo; colon resection. HIV + IS endemic: REACTIVATION surveillance + suppressive if needed. FAMILY SCREENING: congenital + sibling + mother + blood donor (chronic asymptomatic carrier). DIAGNOSIS: acute direct microscopy + PCR; chronic TWO POSITIVE serology different antigens (ELISA + IFI + agglutination); cardiac ECG (RBBB + LAFB + AVB + complex VE) + echo (DCM + apical aneurysm + LV thrombus) + Holter + MRI; GI barium/endoscopy. Blood + organ donor universal screening endemic + diaspora — Latin American patients screen. Vector + housing + congenital screening + travel education. SSA: not endemic — diaspora awareness + blood safety.
rationale: WHO 2019 Chagas + PAHO + BENEFIT NEJM 2015 + DNDi BENDITA.

title: Leprosy — WHO MDT 6/12 mo; reactions = steroid emergency; single-dose rifampicin PEP for contacts
recommendation: DIAGNOSIS clinical — 3 cardinal: hypopigmented anaesthetic patch + thickened nerve + AFB on slit-skin smear/biopsy. Smear 6 sites + Fite + Ridley-Jopling. Nerve assessment + monofilament + voluntary muscle test. WHO MDT FREE: PAUCIBACILLARY (1-5 lesions, AFB-): rifampicin 600 mg (450 < 35 kg) ONCE MONTHLY supervised + dapsone 100 mg (50 < 35 kg) daily + CLOFAZIMINE added (WHO 2018 unified) × 6 MONTHS. MULTIBACILLARY (> 5 lesions, AFB+, LL/BL/BB): rifampicin 600 monthly supervised + dapsone 100 daily + clofazimine 300 mg monthly supervised + 50 mg daily × 12 MONTHS (was 24). Paeds weight-adjusted same. PREG: same MDT — SAFE. G6PD: test before dapsone — haemolysis risk — alternative (clofazimine + rifampicin + minocycline) if deficient. ROM (rif+ofx+mino) single dose — emerging paucibacillary single-lesion. REACTIONS EMERGENCY: TYPE 1 (reversal — increased inflam + neuritis — IRREVERSIBLE in days if not treated): pred 30-60 mg/d × 3-6 mo taper (longer for neuritis) + continue MDT + splint + physio. TYPE 2 (ENL multibacillary — tender nodules + fever + arthritis + iritis + neuritis): pred 30-40 taper + THALIDOMIDE 100-400 mg/d (teratogenic — strict contraception + protocol — restricted) + clofazimine high-dose + pentoxifylline/MTX + continue MDT. PEP: SINGLE-DOSE RIFAMPICIN 600/450/300/150 mg by weight for ALL contacts > 2 yr (WHO 2018 LPEP + COLEP RCT 2008 — reduces leprosy 57% NNT 26-32). REHAB: eye (lagophthalmos surgery + lubrication), hand/foot self-care (inspect/soak/oil/protective footwear), reconstructive surgery, mental health + stigma + livelihood + Persons Affected by Leprosy + zero discrimination; plantar ulcer rest + dressing + footwear. SSA: Kenya endemic low burden — integrate skin services + train + zero discrimination + community awareness.
rationale: WHO 2018+2020 Leprosy + Zero Leprosy 2030 + LPEP + COLEP BMJ 2008.

title: Trachoma — SAFE strategy; surgery TT + annual azithromycin MDA + face washing + environment
indicators: TF/TI follicular conjunctivitis / TT trichiasis / endemic area
recommendation: WHO GET2030 SAFE: S — SURGERY for TRICHIASIS (TT) — bilamellar tarsal rotation (BTR) — community-based + clinical officers — free + outreach + monitor recurrence 10-20%; A — AZITHROMYCIN annual MDA 20 mg/kg PO (max 1 g) single dose where TF in children ≥ 5% — coverage > 80% × 3-5 yr to interrupt transmission — donated ITI Pfizer Zithromax (1 billion+ doses); tetracycline 1% eye ointment BD × 6 wk alternative; treat household contacts. F — FACIAL CLEANLINESS daily face-washing for children + soap + water access + community behaviour change; E — ENVIRONMENTAL improvement — water + sanitation (WASH) + latrines + waste + housing + animals — reduces fly breeding + transmission. CLINICAL GRADING WHO Simplified — TF/TI/TS/TT/CO slit-lamp/loupe. ELIMINATION THRESHOLDS: TF < 5% children 1-9; TT < 0.2% adults ≥ 15 yr unknown to health system + surveillance. Many countries eliminated as public health problem (Oman/Morocco/Mexico/Iran/Cambodia/China/Saudi/Iraq/Ghana/Gambia/Myanmar/Togo/Malawi/Vietnam/Nepal +); Ethiopia largest + intensive + progress; Kenya endemic pockets Turkana/Pokot/Marsabit/Samburu/Baringo/Narok — programme active + nearing thresholds many districts. PARTNERS: WHO + ITI + Sightsavers + Lions Clubs + MoH + NEH Plan 2030.
rationale: WHO Trachoma + GET2030 + ITI + Kenya NEH 2030.

title: MRSA bacteraemia — vanco AUC 400-600 or dapto ≥ 8 mg/kg; TOE; source control + daily blood cultures
recommendation: Source control FIRST — remove vascular catheter + drain abscess + surgical debridement. VANCOMYCIN load 25-30 mg/kg then 15-20 mg/kg q8-12h — target AUC24/MIC 400-600 (Bayesian or 2-level kinetics; trough 15-20 mg/L less accurate alternative) — IDSA 2020 TDM. DAPTOMYCIN 8-10 mg/kg/d (≥ 8 for IE, ≥ 10 persistent) if vanc MIC ≥ 2, hVISA/VISA, vanco AKI/allergy, persistent bacteraemia — NOT pneumonia (surfactant). CEFTAROLINE 600 q8h adjunct for persistent / salvage. LINEZOLID alternative — bacteriostatic — NOT IE/bacteraemia first-line; reserve refractory SSTI/bone + bacteraemia. Rifampicin combo for PROSTHETIC/hardware (not routine native). Workup: ≥ 2 BC pre-Abx + REPEAT q48h until clear; TTE all + TOE if persistent/prosthetic/inadequate TTE/IE; source — catheter, SSTI, vertebral MRI, joint, psoas, lung. DURATION: uncomplicated cleared 72h + no metastatic 14 d IV from 1st neg BC; complicated/metastatic/IE 4-6 wk; vertebral osteo 6-8 wk. Persistent > 7 d = complicated → escalate + reseed search. SURGICAL IE: HF, perivalvular abscess, persistent BC, vegetation > 10 mm embolic, fungal, prosthetic. OPAT stable. CK baseline + weekly dapto (rhabdo). Decolonise (mupirocin + chlorhex) recurrent/outbreak. SSA: vanco available; daptomycin + ceftaroline access advocacy.
rationale: IDSA 2011 MRSA + IDSA 2020 Vanco TDM + ESC 2023 IE.

title: ESBL — nitrofurantoin/fosfomycin uncomplicated UTI; CARBAPENEM bacteraemia/severe (MERINO)
indicators: ESBL E. coli / Klebsiella on culture
recommendation: MILD UTI (cystitis): NITROFURANTOIN 100 QDS × 5 d preferred (preserves carbapenem); fosfomycin 3 g single (multi-dose male/complicated); pivmecillinam 400 TDS × 3-7 d; cotrim/cipro if susceptible. PYELONEPHRITIS / SEVERE / BACTERAEMIA: CARBAPENEM first-line — ERTAPENEM 1 g OD (no Pseudomonas/Acinetobacter cover but good for ESBL) or meropenem 1-2 g q8h; step-down oral if susceptible (cotrim/cipro/pivmecillinam; amox-clav cautious bacteraemia). MERINO RCT JAMA 2018 — PIP-TAZ INFERIOR to meropenem for ESBL bacteraemia (increased mortality) — do NOT use pip-taz definitive ESBL bacteraemia. INTRA-ABDOMINAL: carbapenem + source control (drainage). Ceftolozane-tazo + ceftaz-avi generally reserved CRE/Pseudomonas — selective ESBL. Aminoglycoside (amikacin/gentamicin) combination salvage. PREVENTION: hand hygiene + contact precautions + stewardship (AWaRe Watch carbapenem) + reduce inappropriate cephalosporin/FQ. PROPHYLAXIS recurrent UTI: nitrofurantoin/fosfomycin nightly + address contributing. Risk factors: travel S Asia/Mediterranean, prior abx, hospitalisation, catheter. SSA: ESBL widely prevalent — ertapenem + nitrofurantoin + fosfomycin essential KEML + stewardship + IPC + lab.
rationale: IDSA AMR 2024 + MERINO JAMA 2018 + ESCMID.

title: CRE — treat by enzyme: ceftaz-avi (KPC/OXA-48), ceftaz-avi+aztreonam or cefiderocol (NDM/VIM/IMP)
recommendation: ID CONSULT MANDATORY. Identify enzyme (PCR — KPC/NDM/OXA-48/VIM/IMP critical). KPC: CEFTAZIDIME-AVIBACTAM 2.5 g q8h OR MEROPENEM-VABORBACTAM 4 g q8h OR IMIPENEM-RELEBACTAM. OXA-48: CEFTAZ-AVI preferred. NDM/VIM/IMP metallo-β-lactamases: CEFTAZ-AVI + AZTREONAM combination (aztreonam stable to MBL + avibactam protects from ESBL/AmpC) OR CEFIDEROCOL 2 g q8h (siderophore — only approved single agent for MBL CRE — APEKS-NP/CREDIBLE-CR). Alternatives/salvage: polymyxin B/colistin (nephro + neurotox), tigecycline (NOT bacteraemia — low serum), aminoglycoside (plazomicin/genta/amikacin if susc), eravacycline, fosfomycin IV (urinary). DURATION 7-14 d (longer endovascular/complicated 4-6 wk). SOURCE CONTROL — drain + remove catheter + abdominal control essential. DECOLONISATION not recommended (no benefit + resistance). IPC: contact precautions + cohort + dedicated equipment + active surveillance high-risk units + hand hygiene + environmental + stewardship. NOTIFIABLE many jurisdictions — report WHO GLASS. Risk factors: travel endemic, prior CRE/colonisation, transfer from endemic hospital, prolonged stay. SSA: emerging — lab capacity (Kenya KEMRI), access ceftaz-avi/cefiderocol limited — advocacy + ID/micro training.
rationale: IDSA AMR 2024 + ESCMID + CREDIBLE-CR Lancet ID 2021.

title: Loa loa — LoaScope < 30,000 mf/mL before ivermectin; DEC × 21 d individual; doxycycline alt MDA
indicators: Calabar swelling / eye worm / endemic Central African forest exposure
recommendation: TEST LOA MICROFILARIAL LOAD before any MDA (LoaScope POC smartphone Cameroon NEJM 2017): < 20,000 mf/mL IVM safe; 20-30,000 caution; > 30,000 mf/mL DO NOT GIVE IVM/DEC (ENCEPHALOPATHY + death). INDIVIDUAL: DEC 6 mg/kg/d × 21 d (escalate from low dose + antihistamine + steroid cover for symptomatic relief during microfilarial death) — first-line symptomatic + low load. ALBENDAZOLE 200 mg BD × 21 d alternative — slow + safer for high load; macrofilaricidal. IVERMECTIN 150 μg/kg single — reduces mf but NOT cure adult — only if load safe. Surgical removal of subconjunctival eye worm under topical anaesthesia + slit-lamp + forceps. PRE-MDA in oncho/LF co-endemic Central Africa (Cameroon/Gabon/CAR/DRC/Congo/S Nigeria/Eq Guinea/S Sudan): test + alternative pathway — DOXYCYCLINE 200 mg/d × 4-6 wk anti-Wolbachia (works for oncho/LF without IVM/DEC encephalopathy risk); or pre-treat albendazole to lower Loa before IVM (TEST-AND-NOT-TREAT or TEST-AND-DOSE). ENCEPHALOPATHY: ICU + high-dose IV steroid + supportive + IVIG/PLEX experimental. PREVENTION: repellent + clothing + avoid day forest. SSA: huge obstacle to oncho/LF elim in Central Africa — LoaScope deployment + alternative regimens.
rationale: WHO Boussinesq 2022 + LoaScope Kamgno NEJM 2017.

title: Cystic echinococcosis — WHO-IWGE stage-based; albendazole + PAIR or surgery; anaphylaxis ready
indicators: hydatid cyst US/CT + serology in endemic area
recommendation: WHO-IWGE STAGE-BASED (US): CE1/CE3a active small < 5 cm — albendazole alone or PAIR + albendazole; CE1/CE3a large > 5 cm — PAIR + albendazole or surgery; CE2/CE3b multivesicular — SURGERY (PAIR ineffective); CE4/CE5 inactive — WATCH AND WAIT + serial US. ALBENDAZOLE 10-15 mg/kg/d divided BD (max 800 mg/d adult — 400 BD) × 3-6 mo continuous OR cyclical 4 wk on / 2 wk off × 3-6 cycles; reassess imaging; LFT + FBC monthly (transaminitis + neutropenia); pre + intra-op 4 d before to 1 mo after reduces recurrence. ADD praziquantel for daughter cysts / pre-op / post-spillage prophylaxis. PAIR (Puncture-Aspiration-Injection-Reaspiration) for selected CE1/CE3a — TRAINED CENTRE + emergency anaesthesia + ANAPHYLAXIS READY (adrenaline + ICU) — aspirate → scolicide (95% ethanol or hypertonic saline) × 15-30 min → reaspirate + albendazole cover before + 1 mo after. SURGERY: cystectomy/pericystectomy/partial hepatectomy/lobectomy — bilateral lung — minimise spillage with hypertonic gauze + meticulous technique. BILIARY RUPTURE/OBSTRUCTION: ERCP + sphincterotomy + drainage + surgery. ANAPHYLAXIS during procedure: adrenaline IM + ICU. PULMONARY: surgery preferred (lung less responsive albendazole). ALVEOLAR (E. multilocularis): radical surgery R0 like cancer + lifelong albendazole; transplant selected. ONE HEALTH PREVENT: dog deworming PZQ monthly endemic + slaughter hygiene + hand + food hygiene + community education. SSA: Kenya (Turkana) endemic — surgical centres + education + One Health.
rationale: WHO-IWGE 2010+2017 + Brunetti Acta Tropica 2010.

title: Brucellosis — doxy + rif × 6 wk (or + strep/genta); 3-6 mo focal (endocarditis/spondylitis/neuro)
recommendation: UNCOMPLICATED adult: DOXYCYCLINE 100 mg BD × 6 wk + RIFAMPICIN 600-900 mg OD × 6 wk (WHO oral combination) OR doxy × 6 wk + STREPTOMYCIN 1 g IM OD × 14-21 d (or gentamicin 5 mg/kg OD × 7-14 d) — aminoglycoside combination often LESS relapse than oral combo. AVOID monotherapy. Children < 8 yr: cotrim + rifampicin × 6 wk ± gentamicin 1st wk; doxy acceptable short course > 7 d if benefits outweigh (WHO update). Pregnancy: cotrim (after 1st trimester) + rifampicin × 6 wk; rifampicin alone × 6 wk (less effective + more relapse). FOCAL (SPONDYLITIS/NEURO/ENDOCARDITIS): TRIPLE THERAPY × 3-6 MONTHS minimum — doxy + rifampicin + aminoglycoside first 2-4 wk → continue doxy + rifampicin ≥ 12 wk spondylitis ≥ 4-6 mo neuro. ENDOCARDITIS: triple/quad ≥ 3 mo + EARLY valve surgery (better outcome). Neuro: add cotrim (CSF pen) ± ceftriaxone × 4-6 mo + steroid for vasculitis. Workup: blood culture (special media 3-6 wk + PCR); Rose Bengal screen + SAT + ELISA + 2-mercaptoethanol; FBC pancytopenia + LFT + ESR; MRI spine, echo, US testes; LP neuro. RELAPSE 5-15% — repeat extended + reseed source. PEP lab exposure: doxy + rifampicin × 3 wk + serology surveillance. PREVENT: pasteurise + boil milk + occupational PPE + animal vaccination (Rev-1/S19). SSA: Kenya pastoralist + occupational + dairy — One Health + vet + pasteurisation + education.
rationale: WHO Brucellosis + Ioannidou Lancet Infect Dis 2019.

title: Q fever — doxy × 14-21 d acute; doxy + HCQ ≥ 18-24 mo chronic IE; cotrim in pregnancy
indicators: culture-negative IE / atypical pneumonia + hepatitis + livestock/abattoir / pregnant occupational
recommendation: ACUTE Q fever: DOXYCYCLINE 100 mg BD × 14 d (severe × 21 d). PREGNANCY: COTRIMOXAZOLE 160/800 BD throughout pregnancy (until delivery) — reduces congenital + chronic risk. Children < 8 yr: cotrim or short doxy. CHRONIC Q fever (endocarditis/vascular/persistent focus): DOXYCYCLINE 100 mg BD + HYDROXYCHLOROQUINE 200 mg TDS for ≥ 18-24 MONTHS native valve, ≥ 24 MONTHS prosthetic; HCQ ophthalmology baseline + 6 mo annually (retinopathy); phase I IgG titre serial monitoring (≥ 4-fold drop sustained = consider stopping after 18-24 mo); surgical valve replacement for severe/refractory/structural. POST-Q FEVER FATIGUE: supportive + graded exercise + CBT + symptoms; no specific antibiotic. Diagnosis: IFA serology — acute phase II IgG ≥ 1:200 + IgM ≥ 1:50 (or 4× rise paired); chronic phase I IgG ≥ 1:1024 (or 800 — endocarditis/vascular). PCR blood + tissue early acute pre-seroconversion. Culture BSL-3. Echo (TOE+TTE culture-negative IE) + PET-CT (IE/vascular). VACCINE Q-VAX (Australia occupational; pre-vax skin + serology screen). PREVENT: PPE P2 respirator + animal vaccination + birthing fluid avoidance + pasteurise + environmental. OUTBREAK: ID + public health + occupational + livestock + serology screen at-risk + treat; pregnant post-outbreak — screen + treat + paeds follow congenital. NOTIFIABLE. SSA: Kenya pastoralist + abattoir + livestock — One Health surveillance.
rationale: CDC MMWR 2013 + European Q Fever 2017 + ESC 2023 IE.

title: Lyme — doxy 10-14 d EM/early; IV ceftriaxone severe carditis/neuro; no prolonged Abx for PTLDS
indicators: erythema migrans / bilateral facial palsy / Lyme carditis / arthritis in endemic
recommendation: EARLY LOCALISED erythema migrans — CLINICAL diagnosis, TREAT EMPIRICALLY (serology poor early) — DOXYCYCLINE 100 mg BD × 10 d or amoxicillin 500 TDS or cefuroxime axetil 500 BD × 14 d. Pregnancy: AMOX or cefuroxime × 14 d (no doxy). Children ≥ 8 yr: doxy short course < 21 d NOW ACCEPTED IDSA 2020 or amoxicillin. Early DISSEMINATED mild: doxy × 14 d. LYME ARTHRITIS: doxy × 28 d; incomplete — repeat 28 d or IV ceftriaxone 2 g × 14-28 d; refractory post-Abx Lyme arthritis — NSAID + DMARD (NOT more antibiotic). LYME CARDITIS: hospitalise if 2nd/3rd-degree AV block, sx, syncope, PR > 300 ms; IV ceftriaxone 2 g OD × 14-21 d → transition oral doxy when stable + PR < 300; mild 1st-degree outpatient oral doxy × 14-21 d; temporary pacing if high block — permanent rarely needed. NEUROBORRELIOSIS (meningitis/radiculitis/encephalitis): IV ceftriaxone 2 g OD × 14-28 d (severe/enceph 28 d); doxy 200 mg BD or 100 BD × 14-28 d alternative (CSF penetration acceptable per trials). Facial palsy isolated: oral doxy × 14-21 d (palsy resolves over wks regardless). Acrodermatitis chronic Europe: doxy × 28 d. PTLDS: NO prolonged/repeated antibiotic benefit (Klempner NEJM 2001 + others) — supportive + graded exercise + symptom + MDT. POST-TICK PROPHYLAXIS: single doxy 200 mg if adult or > 8 yr + attached ≥ 36 h + within 72 h removal + endemic; otherwise watch for EM. Two-tier serology for disseminated/late (ELISA → Western blot IgM+IgG); LP for neuroborr; ECG for carditis; PCR skin/synovial/CSF limited. Prevent: DEET/permethrin + clothing + tick check + prompt removal fine forceps; VLA15 Pfizer-Valneva vaccine emerging. SSA: not endemic — return-from-travel; refer ID.
rationale: IDSA/AAN/ACR 2020 + NICE NG95 2018 + Klempner NEJM 2001.

title: Long COVID — MDT symptom-based; PACING for PEM (no graded exercise); workup phenotype-specific
recommendation: Multidisciplinary phenotype-based: holistic assessment + GP + MDT long-COVID clinic if available + tailored rehab plan. PACING for post-exertional malaise (PEM) — DO NOT force graded exercise if PEM present (worsens — ME/CFS lesson); energy management + activity diary; symptom-targeted graded return if NO PEM. RESPIRATORY (dyspnoea/cough): pulmonary rehab + inspiratory muscle training; inhaled corticosteroid/bronchodilator if airway/asthma; ANTICOAGULATE if PE confirmed; HRCT + PFT (DLCO) if persistent — ILD pathway if progressive. CARDIOVASCULAR: chest pain — exclude myocarditis (cardiac MRI), pericarditis, PE, ischaemia; MYOCARDITIS — cardiology + exercise restriction 3-6 mo + serial imaging; POTS — increased salt + fluid + compression + graded exercise recumbent → upright + low-dose β-blocker (propranolol/ivabradine) + midodrine + fludrocortisone; pericarditis NSAID + colchicine. NEURO/COGNITIVE: brain fog — cognitive rehab + sleep + treat OSA + mood + exercise as tolerated; headache standard migraine; anosmia — olfactory training + steroid trial; small fibre neuropathy — gabapentinoid + IVIG investigational; stroke — secondary prevention. MENTAL HEALTH: CBT + mindfulness + peer support + specialist if severe; suicide risk. FATIGUE/PEM: pacing + energy management + sleep + treat anaemia/endocrine/thyroid; AVOID forced GET. MIS-C children — IVIG + steroid + ICU. Workup: tailored — D-dimer + CTPA early period; HRCT + PFT; echo + ECG ± cardiac MRI; tilt for POTS; thyroid + cortisol + Hb + B12/folate/D + autoimmune; neuropsych if cognitive; EXCLUDE alternatives (hypothyroid/anaemia/depression/OSA/postural). VACCINATION: COVID booster + influenza + pneumococcal; vaccination may modestly improve symptoms. Antivirals post-acute — no proven benefit (PAXLOVID trials mostly negative). PAED: less common — supportive + school accommodation. OCCUPATIONAL accommodations + phased return. ENROL in trials (RECOVER + PHOSP-COVID). SSA: under-recognised + integrate with chronic disease + mental health + rehab.
rationale: NICE NG188 + WHO 2023 + PHOSP-COVID + RECOVER.

title: Pre-travel — start 4-8 wk before; YF + typhoid + Hep A + malaria proph + risk-tailored
recommendation: Start 4-8 wk before travel. Routine catch-up: MMR/Tdap/polio/varicella/HPV/flu/COVID. YELLOW FEVER single dose lifetime + IHR cert (10 d after) — SSA + Amazon entry; contraindicated < 9 mo, pregnant (unless high risk), severely IC, thymic, caution ≥ 60 yr (YEL-AVD). TYPHOID Vi injectable or oral live Ty21a × 3 (live CI in IC); booster 3-5 yr. HEP A 2 doses 6-12 mo; combined HepA/B if needed. HEP B at-risk; accelerated 0-7-21 d + 12 mo. MENINGOCOCCAL ACWY mandatory HAJJ/UMRAH + meningitis belt + outbreak. RABIES PrEP 3-dose IM or 2-dose WHO 2018 if rural+animal+remote. JE rural Asia > 1 mo. TBE central/east Europe forest. CHOLERA Dukoral outbreak/aid. POLIO IHR cert from endemic. MALARIA chemoprophylaxis by region+resistance+patient: atovaquone-proguanil (Malarone — well-tolerated 1-2 d to 7 d), doxycycline 100 OD (1-2 d to 4 wk; photosens + GI + no preg/<8), mefloquine 250 wkly (2-3 wk to 4 wk; neuropsych CI; OK preg), primaquine/tafenoquine terminal eradication P. vivax (G6PD TEST), chloroquine only chlor-sensitive (rare). BITE PREVENTION: DEET 30-50/picaridin/IR3535 + permethrin clothing + bed nets. TRAVELLER DIARRHOEA: hygiene + ORS + loperamide + AZITHROMYCIN 500 × 3 d (preferred Asia high quinolone R) or cipro Africa/Americas; rifaximin proph selected. ALTITUDE: 'climb high sleep low' + acetazolamide 125 BD 24h before + 2 d; HAPE/HACE descend + dex + nifedipine. VTE long-haul: hydration + movement + compression; ASA/LMWH high-risk. OTHER: sun + water + ROAD TRAUMA (#1 mortality) + animal + sex (condoms + STI + PrEP) + mental + insurance + jet lag + motion + contraception. SPECIAL: pregnant defer Zika/high-risk; paeds adjusted; chronic + alert card. POST-TRAVEL fever 3 mo = malaria until proven (thick film + RDT); schisto serology 3 mo post freshwater; pattern workup. SSA: Kenya referral travel clinics + cross-border + Hajj.
rationale: WHO ITH 2024 + CDC Yellow Book + NaTHNaC + Kenya MoH.

title: RRT modality — shared decision; transplant > home HD/PD > in-centre HD; conservative care option
indicators: ESKD eGFR < 15 or symptomatic — RRT decision
recommendation: Pre-dialysis education + SHARED DECISION (eGFR ~ 20). MODALITIES: HD (in-centre vs home), PD (CAPD/APD), TRANSPLANT (deceased/living — best outcomes if feasible; refer eGFR ≈ 20; LIVING DONOR preferred; ABO-i + paired exchange; pre-emptive ideal), CONSERVATIVE/SUPPORTIVE (active management without dialysis — frail/multimorbid/preference — comparable survival some elderly with less burden). PATIENT values + lifestyle + comorbid + access + social. HD: AVF (gold) > AVG > tunnelled CVC (last) — Fistula First; AVF needs 8-12 wk maturation + avoid PICC/forearm cannulation early CKD; 4h × 3/wk standard; home/nocturnal/daily better selected; Kt/V ≥ 1.2 + regional citrate anticoag. PD: catheter + 2 wk healing; CAPD 4 manual exchanges OR APD overnight; suitable home/employment/preserve residual function/less CV swings; PERITONITIS empirical IP cefazolin+ceftaz/genta — retain catheter unless refractory. ANCILLARY: ESA + iron — Hb 100-115; HIF-PHi (roxadustat) oral alt; phosphate binder + active vitD + cinacalcet SHPT; BP individualised < 140/90; CV RF + statin (4D + SHARP); VACCINES HBV ESSENTIAL pre-HD + pneumo + flu + COVID + zoster recombinant (NO live on transplant); protein 1.0-1.2 + dietitian + Na/K/PO4 mgmt; psychosocial — dialysis depression high + screen + peer support. EMERGENCY dialysis: refractory hyperK/acidosis/fluid overload/uraemic enceph/pericarditis/severe intox. SSA: Kenya KRH transplant growing; HD expanding (KNH + private); PD scale-up potential (lower infrastructure); cost barrier — NHIF advocacy.
rationale: KDIGO 2024 + KDOQI 2019 + ISN.

title: CRRT — 20-25 mL/kg/h effluent; REGIONAL CITRATE preferred; right IJ access; pharmacist for drug dosing
indicators: AKI Stage 3 ICU + haemodynamic instability + RRT indication
recommendation: INDICATIONS (AEIOU + clinical judgement) — STARRT-AKI NEJM 2020: NO benefit of earlier initiation — wait for established indication. MODALITY: CRRT (CVVH/CVVHD/CVVHDF) for haemodynamic instability + MOF; SLED 6-12 h alt cost-effective; IHD if stable. DOSE: effluent 20-25 mL/kg/h delivered (ATN + RENAL NEJM 2008-9 — no benefit higher 35; prescribe higher to deliver target with interruptions). ANTICOAGULATION: REGIONAL CITRATE (RCA) PREFERRED KDIGO 2024 — longer filter life + less bleeding (CI severe liver failure/shock — citrate accumulation: ionised hypoCa + total/ionised Ca ratio > 2.5 alarm; monitor); systemic/regional heparin alternative (HIT precautions); argatroban/fondaparinux HIT alternative; no anticoag for bleeding (high filter loss). FLUID: net UF by haemodynamics + cumulative; avoid rapid shifts; integrate vasopressor + sedation. CATHETER: ultrasound right IJ preferred > left IJ > femoral; AVOID SUBCLAVIAN (stenosis later AVF); CXR position before use; tunnel if > 2-3 wk. DRUG DOSING: most antibiotics + sedatives need adjustment for CRRT clearance — PHARMACIST + drug clearance per modality/flow; vanco + aminoglycoside + β-lactam TDM. COMPLICATIONS: hypothermia (warm), electrolyte (HYPOPHOSPHATAEMIA common — add to dialysate), catheter infection/dysfunction, bleeding, air/clotting alarms. WEAN: spontaneous UO > 500 mL/d off diuretic = good sign; discontinue + monitor 24-48 h; restart if needed. SSA: CRRT expanding tertiary (KNH/Aga Khan/MTRH); SLED + PD alternatives; train ICU + nephro + nursing.
rationale: KDIGO 2012 AKI + 2024 + STARRT-AKI + RENAL/ATN.

title: Massive haemorrhage — 1:1:1 + TXA within 3h trauma/PPH (CRASH-2/WOMAN); NO TXA in GI bleed (HALT-IT)
indicators: > 10 RBC/24h or > 4 RBC/1h or hemorrhagic shock
recommendation: ACTIVATE MTP — clear team + lab + porter; DAMAGE CONTROL bleeding source FIRST (surgery/IR/endoscopy/tourniquet/pack). RATIOS 1:1:1 RBC:FFP:platelets (PROPPR JAMA 2015); pack 1 = 4-6 RBC + 4-6 FFP + 1 plt pool; pack 2 = + cryo 2 pools. TXA: TRAUMA 1 g IV 10 min then 1 g 8 h WITHIN 3 H (CRASH-2 Lancet 2010 + CRASH-3 head 2019); PPH 1 g IV repeat 30 min if bleeding within 3 h (WOMAN Lancet 2017); GI BLEED — HALT-IT Lancet 2020 NO benefit + harm signal — DO NOT USE. FIBRINOGEN target > 1.5-2 g/L PPH > 2 — cryoprecipitate (4 pools ≈ 8 g) or fibrinogen concentrate. CALCIUM: monitor ionised + replace IV CaCl 1 g per 4 RBC (citrate binds; hypoCa worsens coag + cardiac). PREVENT TRAUMA TRIAD: warm (Bair Hugger + warmed fluid/blood + warm room); correct acidosis (perfusion + cause); PERMISSIVE HYPOTENSION in trauma without head injury (SBP 90/palp radial) until source control. REVERSAL: warfarin — vit K 10 IV + 4F-PCC 25-50 IU/kg by INR; dabigatran — idarucizumab 5 g IV; Xa-i (apix/rivarox) — andexanet alfa (cost) or 4F-PCC 50 IU/kg; heparin — protamine 1 mg/100 U last 2-3 h; antiplatelet — platelets if life-threatening. ROTEM/TEG-guided component if available. FACTOR VIIa NOT routine — salvage refractory. DIC — treat cause + replace components. OBSTETRIC: uterotonic ladder (oxytocin → ergometrine → carboprost → misoprostol) + B-Lynch/balloon/hysterectomy + IR embolisation. POC: Hb HemoCue + lactate + base deficit + ABG + ionised Ca; cross-match + emergency O-. AUDIT + simulation + debrief. SSA: Kenya KNBTS + facility MTP + safe blood + train + TXA access for PPH advocacy.
rationale: European Trauma 2023 + PROPPR JAMA 2015 + CRASH-2/3 + WOMAN + HALT-IT.

title: Difficult airway DAS — VL first; SGA 2nd; FONA scalpel-bougie-tube CICO; AFOI anticipated
indicators: airway compromise / planned difficult / failed intubation / RSI
recommendation: Airway assessment (Mallampati + thyromental + neck + mouth + LEMON; obese/burn/trauma/anaphylaxis/distorted anatomy); US identify cricothyroid membrane high-risk. PRE-OXYGENATE 3-5 min 100% O2 + denitrogenate; APNOEIC OXYGENATION nasal high-flow 60 L/min in difficult patients reduces desat. PLAN A INTUBATION (max 3 attempts) — optimal position (sniffing or RAMP if obese) + VIDEOLARYNGOSCOPY first-line (C-MAC/Glidescope/McGrath) + bougie + 7-8 ETT + cuff + CAPNOGRAPHY MANDATORY; cricoid pressure release if obscuring; rocuronium 1-1.2 mg/kg or sux 1-1.5 mg/kg for RSI (rocuronium preferred + sugammadex 16 mg/kg reverses within 3 min if failed). PLAN B SUPRAGLOTTIC AIRWAY (max 3) — 2nd gen i-gel/LMA Proseal; consider intubate through Fastrach; decide: wake (elective), proceed surgery via SGA (urgent), or Plan C. PLAN C FACE MASK 2-person 2-handed + oral/nasal adjunct + relaxant if not given; wake if possible. PLAN D CICO — FRONT-OF-NECK ACCESS (eFONA) EMERGENCY: declare CICO loudly; SCALPEL-BOUGIE-TUBE (DAS 2015 adult) — horizontal stab cricothyroid → bougie → 6.0 ETT → capnography + bilateral air entry; cannula crico + jet ventilation alternative (paeds < 8 yr first-line; barotrauma risk); convert formal tracheostomy when stable. AWAKE FIBREOPTIC anticipated difficult — distorted (burns/Ludwig/AC/neck mass/severe OSA/unstable c-spine/anaphylaxis oedema) — topical anaesthesia + minimal sedation (alert + cooperative); awake VL emerging. PAEDIATRIC (DAS Paeds 2024) — large head/tongue/anterior larynx + high O2 consumption + rapid desat — appropriately sized equipment + skilled help + cannula crico+jet < 8 yr. EXTUBATION high-risk DAS 2012 — LMA exchange + airway exchange catheter + surgical airway ready. DOCUMENT + ALERT (chart + bracelet + difficult airway letter to patient + GP + future). NAP4 lessons + simulation + critical incident.
rationale: DAS 2015 Adult + 2018 + DAS Paeds 2024 + NAP4 + ASA.

title: Stillbirth — confirm 2 clinicians + respectful care + mementos + cause workup + bereavement + subsequent care
indicators: confirmed intrauterine fetal death / neonatal death / late miscarriage
recommendation: CONFIRM by 2 clinicians US (auscultation alone insufficient). ACUTE care: PRIVATE quiet room + continuity + named midwife/clinician + RESPECTFUL communication (use baby's NAME + parental wishes + acknowledge as baby) + informed choices (labour vs LSCS + position + family) + generous pain relief + epidural if requested. INDUCTION usually preferred (DIC + psychological) — mifepristone + misoprostol regimen + oxytocin. MEMENTOS (offer + revisit — not forced): holding baby + cuddle cot extend time + photographs (NILMDTS volunteer) + footprints/handprints/lock of hair/blanket/clothes/name bracelet + naming + birth certificate where legal + faith/cultural rituals. FAMILY support — partner + siblings (age-appropriate) + grandparents + cultural-sensitive. WORKUP: maternal FBC+coag+UEC+LFT+glucose+HbA1c+TSH+viral (CMV/parvo/syphilis/toxo/rubella)+Kleihauer+APL+thrombophilia selective+autoimmune+cultures if infective; FETAL postmortem (parental consent — uptake higher empathetic) + PLACENTAL HISTOLOGY essential even no PM + karyotype/microarray + photographs + footprints + measurements + cord/cardiac for chr/culture. DISCHARGE: lactation suppression (cabergoline 1 mg single or supportive) + postnatal recovery + contraception (offered not pressured) + MENTAL HEALTH SCREEN (Edinburgh + PTSD + complicated grief) + bereavement pack + support orgs (Sands, Tommy's, local) + memorial + funeral arrangements + benefits + return-to-work + legal registration + avoid ward with newborns + private discharge if requested. FOLLOW-UP: consultant-led debrief 6-8 wk — review results + cause + risk subsequent + emotional; GP 1-2 wk + community midwife/HV; peer support + counselling (CBT PTSD); subsequent pregnancy — early consultant + early scan + extra support + RAINBOW pregnancy clinic. STAFF: bereavement training + own support (debrief + supervision + time off). AUDIT + perinatal mortality review (MBRRACE-PMRT + WHO Standards). PREVENT: ANC quality + 8-contact + risk assessment + GROW + reduced movements action + smoking cessation + BMI + glycaemia + APL + ASA in PE risk + lateral sleep > 28 wk + ENAP. SSA: Kenya 21/1000 — respectful care + PMR + ENAP + community education + obstetric quality.
rationale: RCOG Green-top 55 + ACOG + WHO Every Newborn + Sands.

title: Paeds obesity — IHBLT 26+ contact hours; GLP-1 from 12 yr; bariatric > 13 yr severe; no stigma
indicators: BMI > 95th percentile + comorbid screen / family concern
recommendation: BMI percentile/z-score (WHO < 5 + 5-19; CDC; IOTF) + waist + BP + Tanner + comorbid screen (HbA1c/OGTT for T2DM, lipids, ALT/AST for NAFLD, TSH if growth, vit D); SLEEP + STOP-BANG/PSG if severe; MENTAL HEALTH + bullying + ED screen; family environment + SDoH; GENETICS if extreme + < 5 yr + syndromic. INTENSIVE HEALTH BEHAVIOUR LIFESTYLE TREATMENT (IHBLT — AAP 2023): family-based + ≥ 26 contact hours over 3-12 mo + MI + goal-setting + self-monitor + school/community + address SDoH (food insecurity/housing/safety/screen/parental work) — AVOID weight stigma + diet talk + focus health behaviours. NUTRITION: whole + veg + fruit + lean + reduce ultra-processed; reduce SSB + juice + portions; family meals + structured times; dietitian. ACTIVITY: 60 min/d MVPA (WHO) + reduce screen + enjoyable + family + community + barriers. SLEEP age-appropriate + screen-free bedroom + routine. MENTAL HEALTH treat depression/anxiety/body image/bullying/ED + CBT. PHARMACOTHERAPY ≥ 12 yr (AAP 2023): LIRAGLUTIDE 3 mg SC OD (Saxenda FDA 2020); SEMAGLUTIDE 2.4 SC wkly (Wegovy FDA 2022 — STEP-TEENS 16% loss); phentermine-topiramate (Qsymia FDA 2022); orlistat 120 with meals; SETMELANOTIDE selected genetic (POMC/LEPR/Bardet-Biedl). METABOLIC-BARIATRIC SURGERY ≥ 13 yr severe (BMI ≥ 35 + comorbid or ≥ 40): VSG common adolescent or RYGB at adolescent MBS centre + comprehensive psychosocial + family — Teen-LABS NEJM 2016 durable + comorbidity remission; lifelong supplements + follow-up. T2DM: lifestyle + METFORMIN first-line (often inadequate alone); insulin if HbA1c > 8.5; GLP-1 liraglutide ≥ 10 yr (ELLIPSE T2DM) + dapagliflozin ≥ 10 yr. OSA: ENT + adenotonsillectomy + CPAP. NAFLD: lifestyle + selected vit E (no resmetirom in paeds). POPULATION: WHO ECHO + SSB tax + labelling + advertising + school nutrition + active transport. STIGMA-FREE care + family-centred + long-term + no shame. SSA: double-burden under-/overnutrition coexist + nuanced messaging; Kenya urbanisation + SSB tax debate.
rationale: AAP 2023 + WHO 2024 + NICE NG189 + STEP-TEENS + Teen-LABS.

title: FTT — MDT + root cause + WHO SAM/MAM CMAM with RUTF + WASH + 1000 days + no overshadow
indicators: growth faltering / weight crossing percentiles / inadequate gain / SAM/MAM
recommendation: MDT: paeds + dietitian + SLT (feeding) + nurse + SW + CHW + GP. SERIAL ANTHROPOMETRY: weight + length/height + HC + WAZ/HAZ/WHZ + MUAC (WHO < 5; growth velocity). RED FLAGS: SAM = MUAC < 11.5 OR WHZ < -3 OR bilateral oedema (WHO/UNICEF emergency); MAM = MUAC 11.5-12.5; STUNTING HAZ < -2; WASTING WHZ < -2; anaemia + micronutrient. WORKUP TARGETED (not blanket): FBC + iron + UEC + LFT + TFT + coeliac TTG + urinalysis + faecal occult/fat/parasites + lead + HIV test essential SSA + TB Mantoux/GeneXpert if exposure; genetics/cardiac/GI/neuro/metabolic per clinical; bone age if linear. ROOT-CAUSE-BASED: treat medical cause (HIV/TB/GI/heart/etc); feeding behaviour + technique (latch + paced bottle + position + oromotor); caregiver education + mental health + food security + parenting. NUTRITIONAL RESCUE: breastfeed optimisation (lactation counsellor; relactation possible); complementary feeding 6 mo+ diverse + energy-dense + iron + zinc + frequency (WHO IYCF); calorie supplements (high-cal + thickeners + oils + nut paste + fortification); SAM WHO 2013+2023 simplified — outpatient if no complications + appetite test (eat RUTF) — CMAM/IMAM with RUTF (Plumpy'Nut + local); inpatient if complicated (oedema 3+/anorexia/infection/hypothermia/hypoglyc/severe dehydration) WHO 10 STEPS — F-75 then F-100 + antibiotic (amox or amp+genta) + vit A + folate + Zn + transition to RUTF + rehab. REFEEDING SYNDROME: gradual + monitor PO4/Mg/K/glucose + thiamine before glucose. MICRONUTRIENT: vit A high-dose q6 mo < 5 yr deficient settings; iron + folate; zinc; iodised salt + multimic; DEWORM albendazole 400 q6 mo > 1 yr endemic. INFECTION: TB/HIV/malaria/diarrhoea (Zn + ORS)/pneumonia (IMCI antibiotic). EARLY STIMULATION (UNICEF/WHO Care for Child Development) + play + responsive feeding + cognitive. FOLLOW-UP serial weight + growth + dev + nutrition + family + community transition. SAFEGUARDING — suspected neglect/abuse → pathway + MDT + SW; inpatient observation may clarify. POPULATION WHO 1000 days + BFHI + Code substitutes + school feeding + maternal nutrition + food security + WASH + agriculture + SDG 2. SSA: Kenya MOH + IMAM + RUTF + CHV + integrate HIV/TB + UNICEF + WFP.
rationale: WHO 2013/2023 SAM + IYCF + NICE NG75 + Kenya IMAM.

title: Disability — UNCRPD + reasonable adjustments + avoid diagnostic overshadowing + annual LD/ID health check
recommendation: ACCESSIBILITY: physical (ramps + accessible toilets + height-adjust couches + scales for wheelchair + hoists + parking); communication (Easy Read + pictorial + SIGN LANGUAGE interpreter + longer appts + plain language + hearing loop + AAC + Braille/large print); sensory-friendly autism (quiet room + sensory adjust); telehealth + outreach + affordability (NHIF + fee waivers). REASONABLE ADJUSTMENTS (legal — UK Equality Act/ADA/UNCRPD): individual + ask + record + act — longer appt, first/last slot, separate waiting, named clinician, advance info, sedation for dental/proc, social story. CO-PRODUCTION 'Nothing About Us Without Us' — engage in service design + decisions; SUPPORTED DECISION-MAKING UNCRPD Art 12 — supported autonomy + best interests; carers/family support but PATIENT is centre. AVOID DIAGNOSTIC OVERSHADOWING — investigate symptoms thoroughly + don't attribute to disability without workup; pain expressed differently (behavioural change in ID + non-verbal — DisDAT/FLACC/Abbey/PAINAD scales); objective + collateral + careful. PREVENTIVE CARE — general + specific: cancer screening (cervical/breast/colorectal) often missed + adapted access; vaccinations; bone (low activity + AED + low BMI); MENTAL HEALTH SCREEN (high prev depression/anxiety/PTSD); dental + vision + hearing checks regularly missed; sexual + reproductive health (often denied — rights-based); continence + bowel + skin. ANNUAL HEALTH CHECK (LD/ID per NHS Cardiff Health Check — improves detection). MEDICATION: polypharmacy common — STOPP/START + anticholinergic burden + interactions; avoid sedating in falls/aspiration risk; STOMP/STAMP UK — Stopping Over-Medication of People with LD/Autism (psychotropic). SAFEGUARDING + ADULT PROTECTION — 3-4× abuse/neglect/hate crime — routine enquiry + safe disclosure + multi-agency. MDT: GP + specialist + PT/OT/SLT + community nurse + SW + carer + advocate; transition paeds → adult 'Ready Steady Go'. ASSISTIVE TECHNOLOGY WHO GATE + APL — wheelchair/hearing/glasses/prosthetic/AAC; community-based rehab (CBR) LMIC. INTERSECTIONAL gender/race/LGBTQ+/age/rural/refugee compounding. POPULATION: UNCRPD Kenya 2008 ratified + national action plan; WHO Disability Inclusion + Rehab 2030; Persons with Disabilities Act Kenya 2003 (in revision); disability employment + education + transport + social protection (cash transfers); inclusive emergency response; data disaggregated by disability (Washington Group Questions).
rationale: WHO Disability + Health 2022 + UNCRPD 2006 + WHO World Report 2011/2022 + NHS LD Annual Health Check + Kenya PWD Act.

title: PE — risk-stratify; massive thrombolysis; intermediate-high PERT for CDT; DOAC first-line stable
recommendation: Risk stratify (ESC 2019/2024): clinical Wells/Geneva; D-dimer (age-adjusted) if low to exclude; CTPA gold (V/Q if contrast CI / preg); bedside US — RV dilation + McConnell + TR + RA thrombus + DVT confirms PE clinical context; ECG (S1Q3T3 rare; tachy + RBBB) + troponin (RV strain → mortality) + BNP. CLASS: low (PESI I-II) outpatient; intermediate-low anticoag + monitor; INTERMEDIATE-HIGH (RV dysfunc echo + biomarker pos) anticoag + watch + PERT if deteriorating; HIGH (shock) MASSIVE — THROMBOLYSIS. ANTICOAG: DOAC first-line stable non-cancer non-preg — apixaban 10 BD × 7 d → 5 BD; rivaroxaban 15 BD × 21 d → 20 OD; dabig/edox after parenteral LMWH 5-10 d; LMWH first-line cancer (apix/edox alt non-GI per HOKUSAI/CARAVAGGIO); preg LMWH only; warfarin INR 2-3 alt (KEML-affordable). DURATION: provoked transient 3 mo; unprovoked/cancer/thrombophilia 6 mo-indefinite (HERDOO2 for women shared). MASSIVE (high-risk shock/arrest): SYSTEMIC THROMBOLYSIS alteplase 100 mg over 2 h (or 0.6 mg/kg bolus 15 min arrest) — class I; avoid active bleed/recent surg/stroke/late preg; PEA arrest + RF — bolus + CPR 60-90 min; surgical embolectomy or CATHETER-DIRECTED THROMBOLYSIS for lysis CI or failed (SEATTLE-II + EXTRACT-PE + FLARE — EkoSonic/FlowTriever — reduce RV/LV + less bleeding); VA-ECMO refractory. INTERMEDIATE-HIGH (submassive RV strain + tn): anticoag + close monitor ICU; PERT review for CDT/embolectomy — PEITHO NEJM 2014 (alteplase reduced decompensation but bleeding); routine systemic lysis NOT beneficial. PERT MDT — IC/IR/CT surg/ICU/pulm/haem rapid activation for inter-high + massive — decide CDT/mechanical thrombectomy/surgical/ECMO. PREG PE: CTPA or V/Q + MRI; LMWH therapeutic throughout + 6 wk PP + switch UFH peri-delivery; thrombolysis OK life-threatening (alteplase doesn't cross placenta). FOLLOW-UP: extend decision + CTEPH at 3-6 mo (4% — echo + V/Q if persistent dyspnoea) + cancer workup unprovoked + lifestyle + secondary prevention. IVC FILTER only anticoag CI (active bleed/imminent surg) or progressive despite anticoag; remove when CI resolved (PREPIC-2). SSA: Kenya CTPA tertiary; alteplase + DOAC affordability/access advocacy; PERT tertiary; warfarin resource-limited.
rationale: ESC 2019/2024 PE + PEITHO NEJM 2014 + FLARE + PERT Consortium.

title: Serotonin syndrome — Hunter criteria; STOP serotonergic + benzo + cyproheptadine; AVOID dantrolene
indicators: autonomic + neuromuscular clonus/hyperreflexia + mental status + serotonergic exposure within 24 h
recommendation: HUNTER criteria (preferred) — exposure + clonus (spontaneous/inducible/ocular) + agitation/diaphoresis OR tremor + hyperreflexia OR hypertonia + temp > 38 + ocular/inducible clonus. STOP ALL serotonergic IMMEDIATELY (SSRI/SNRI/MAOI/TCA/triptan/tramadol/pethidine/fentanyl/linezolid/methylene blue/St John's/MDMA/cocaine). SUPPORTIVE mainstay: IV fluid + cardiac/temp/neuro monitor + ICU mod-severe; ACTIVE COOLING for hyperthermia (ice/evaporative/cooling blanket — NO antipyretics; temp is muscle-driven). BENZODIAZEPINE first-line for agitation/autonomic/rigidity/clonus — diazepam 5-10 IV q5-10 min titrated or midazolam 1-2 or lorazepam 2-4 IV. CYPROHEPTADINE (5-HT2A antagonist) mod-severe — 12 mg PO/NG initial then 2 mg q2h to response (max 32/24h); maintenance 8 mg q6h (NG if intubated). Chlorpromazine 50-100 IM alternative (avoid hypotension). SEVERE (temp > 41 / rigid / rhabdo): intubate + sedate + PARALYSE non-depolarising (rocuronium/vecuronium — SUXAMETHONIUM CONTRAINDICATED hyperK rhabdo) — reverses rigidity → controls temp; treat rhabdo (fluid + K/CK/AKI; dialyse severe) + DIC. AVOID dantrolene (no good evidence — that's MH), bromocriptine (that's NMS), antipyretics (ineffective + hepato-renal in rhabdo), physical restraint alone. Most resolve 24-72 h. WASHOUT before restart: SSRI 2 wk, FLUOXETINE 5-6 wk, MAOI 2 wk before serotonergic. PREVENT: review meds + ED/primary care prescribing tramadol/fentanyl/triptan/linezolid/methylene blue/St John's in patient on SSRI/SNRI/MAOI.
rationale: Boyer NEJM 2005 + Hunter QJM 2003 + ACMT 2014.

title: NMS — stop neuroleptic / restart L-DOPA; benzo + DANTROLENE + bromocriptine; ICU support
indicators: hyperthermia + lead-pipe rigidity + autonomic + altered mental + neuroleptic exposure (or L-DOPA withdrawal)
recommendation: DSM-5/Levenson criteria — neuroleptic exposure + hyperthermia + rigidity + 2 of: autonomic + altered + CK > 4× ULN + tremor + leucocytosis + diaphoresis + incontinence. CK often > 10,000. STOP NEUROLEPTIC / dopamine antagonist; RESTART L-DOPA if withdrawal-precipitated. SUPPORTIVE: IV fluid + electrolyte + ACTIVE COOLING (ice/evaporative/blanket) + ICU; correct rhabdo (fluid + K/Mg/PO4/CK/UO + alkalinise if pigmenturia); treat acidosis + hypoxia + DIC + AKI (dialysis severe). BENZODIAZEPINE for agitation/autonomic — lorazepam 1-2 IV q4-6h. DANTROLENE skeletal relaxant 1-2.5 mg/kg IV q6-12h (max 10 mg/kg/24h) for severe rigid + hyperthermia; PO 100-200 mg/d as improves. BROMOCRIPTINE dopamine agonist 2.5-5 PO/NG q8h titrate to 45 mg/d; restart L-DOPA if Parkinsonian (CAUTION serotonergic combination). Amantadine 100-200 BD alt. ECT for refractory / overlap catatonia. Intubate + paralyse non-depolarising (NOT sux — rhabdo hyperK) for refractory. DURATION 5-10 d (longer depot). RESTART neuroleptic ≥ 2 wk post-recovery + switch lower potency / atypical (clozapine sometimes) + start low + slow + monitor + share decision; recurrence 30%; avoid all dopamine antagonist if possible — use alternative antiemetic (ondansetron/antihistamine). DIFFERENTIAL: serotonin syndrome (hyperreflex + lower-limb clonus + recent serotonergic + faster onset), heat stroke, thyroid storm, MH (anaesthesia + sux), lethal catatonia (overlap). PREVENT: avoid rapid neuroleptic escalation + dehydration + monitor temp/CK in high-risk init; gradual L-DOPA + don't stop abruptly.
rationale: Strawn AJP 2007 + Caroff + DSM-5.

title: Catatonia — Bush-Francis + lorazepam challenge 2 mg IV; ECT refractory; rule out NMDAR encephalitis
indicators: mutism + immobility + posturing + waxy flexibility ± autonomic
recommendation: BUSH-FRANCIS catatonia rating scale ≥ 2 of first 14 + total ≥ 6 (or DSM-5 catatonia 3+ of 12). STOP any neuroleptic (worsens + precipitates malignant catatonia). MEDICAL WORKUP essential: NMDAR + autoimmune + UEC + LFT + Ca + Mg + glucose + TSH + B12 + folate + CRP + CK + drug screen + neuroimaging (CT/MRI) + EEG + LP if encephalitis suspected. TREAT UNDERLYING (anti-NMDAR encephalitis with teratoma — immunotherapy + tumour resection). LORAZEPAM CHALLENGE 2 mg IV (or 4) DIAGNOSTIC + therapeutic — observe 5-10 min for improvement (mutism/immobility/eye contact) — 70-80% response confirms diagnosis. MAINTENANCE LORAZEPAM 6-24 mg/d divided q4-8h titrated — may need surprisingly high — safe sedation. Alternatives: zolpidem, memantine, amantadine, carbamazepine, valproate. ECT gold standard refractory/malignant/rapid response — bilateral + daily then taper — 80-90% response (more than lorazepam alone). NUTRITION (NG) + IV fluid + DVT prophylaxis (LMWH) + position/pressure + mouth care + monitor electrolytes + treat aspiration pneumonia. MALIGNANT CATATONIA (hyperthermia + autonomic): ICU + ECT urgent + lorazepam + supportive (cool/fluid/electrolyte); AVOID NEUROLEPTIC. ANTI-NMDAR ENCEPHALITIS specific: ovarian teratoma screen (young woman essential — US + MRI + tumour markers); methylpred 1 g/d × 5 + IVIG 0.4 g/kg × 5 OR PLEX first-line; rituximab + cyclophosphamide second-line; tumour resection; long-term 1-2 yr; relapse 20%; recovery months. Most resolve with treatment. Family education + early recognition. SSA: lorazepam + ECT capacity expanding tertiary; train.
rationale: Sienaert Lancet Psychiatry 2014/19 + BFI + Dalmau NEJM 2008.

title: Refeeding — risk-stratify; thiamine BEFORE glucose; 10 kcal/kg/d high-risk; monitor PO4/K/Mg daily
indicators: malnourished/starved patient about to start feeding (oral/enteral/parenteral)
recommendation: RISK STRATIFY (NICE CG32) — HIGH ≥ 1 major OR ≥ 2 minor; MAJOR: BMI < 16, weight loss > 15% in 3-6 mo, > 10 d minimal intake, pre-feeding low K/PO4/Mg; MINOR: BMI < 18.5, > 10% loss, > 5 d minimal, alcohol/drug/insulin/chemo/diuretic/antacid history. VERY HIGH ≥ 2 major or BMI < 14 or > 15 d nil. BEFORE feeding: THIAMINE 200-300 mg IV/IM (Pabrinex 1+2 IV in alcoholic/severe over 30 min) + multivitamin daily × 3-10 d — THIAMINE BEFORE GLUCOSE (Wernicke prevention). Correct fluid + electrolytes BEFORE feeding (or together) + replace K/PO4/Mg even if low-normal high-risk — target K > 4, PO4 > 0.8, Mg > 0.7. CALORIE: HIGH-RISK start 10 kcal/kg/d (max 5 if very high risk/BMI < 14/> 15 d nil); increase slowly over 4-7 d to need (25-35 kcal/kg/d); carb ≤ 50% energy initially; balanced protein + fat. Salt/fluid restrict if cardiac risk. ELECTROLYTE REPLACE: phosphate IV (Phosphate Polyfusor 500 mL = 50 mmol over 12-24h severe; oral Phosphate Sandoz 16.2 mmol BD-TDS mild-mod); K IV/PO; Mg IV severe/PO. MONITOR: daily weight + fluid balance + electrolyte (PO4/K/Mg) + glucose + UEC × 7 d → 2-3× wk × 2 wk; cardiac (ECG + telemetry high-risk + HF); refeeding bloods even after target. WERNICKE'S: thiamine 500 IV TDS × 2-3 d → 250 IM/IV daily → PO 100 TDS long-term; missed → Korsakoff. SAM children: WHO 10 steps (F-75 → F-100; antibiotic + vit A + folate + Zn; specific). ANOREXIA NERVOSA: specialist eating disorder team + MDT + medical + psych + dietitian + family; supervised; capacity + MHA if life-threatening refusing.
