PN: same risk + slower titration + central + specialist.
rationale: NICE CG32 2017 + ESPEN + WHO SAM.

title: Stones — NSAID > opioid analgesia; MET tamsulosin 5-10mm; URGENT decompression infected+obstructed
recommendation: DIAGNOSIS: CT KUB non-contrast gold; US first in pregnancy + paeds + low-dose alt; urinalysis + UEC + Ca + urate + FBC + CRP + pregnancy test; ANALYSE PASSED STONE (sieve urine); 24h urine + serum PTH + uric acid for recurrent/young/family. ACUTE COLIC: NSAID first-line (diclo 75 mg IM/IV/PO or ketorolac 30 IM/IV — superior Cochrane) + paracetamol IV adjunct; opioid if NSAID CI/inadequate (morphine; tramadol cautious); antiemetic; IV fluid only if dehydrated (forcing fluids does NOT speed passage); hot pack. SIZE/LOCATION: < 5 mm 80-90% pass — trial 2-4 wk + sieve; 5-10 mm 50% pass — MET TAMSULOSIN 400 μg/d × 4 wk distal ureteric stones (SUSPEND modest benefit; NICE 2019 still); > 10 mm or failed or upper ureter — intervention. INTERVENTION: ESWL stones < 2 cm renal/upper; URS + holmium laser ± JJ stent most stones; PCNL > 2 cm + staghorn; stent for obstruction; nephrostomy if infected. EMERGENCY INFECTED + OBSTRUCTED: sepsis bundle + broad-spectrum (ceftriaxone + gentamicin or pip-taz) + URGENT decompression — retrograde stent or PERCUTANEOUS NEPHROSTOMY within hours; NEVER delay decompression for full stone treatment; definitive after sepsis resolved. STONE-TYPE: Ca oxalate (most) — hydration + low oxalate + adequate Ca + thiazide if hyperCa-uria + K-citrate 10-30 mEq TDS; uric acid — alkalinise K-citrate/NaHCO3 pH > 6.5 + allopurinol; struvite — treat infection + complete removal; cystine — high hydration + alkalinise + tiopronin/D-penicillamine; Ca phosphate — investigate RTA + hyperPTH. PREVENT recurrent: HYDRATION > 2.5 L/d (urine > 2 L); diet — moderate Ca (NOT low — increases oxalate absorption), reduce Na < 100 mmol/d, reduce animal protein, oxalate if hyperox; thiazide chlortalidone 25 if hyperCa-uria recurrent (NOSTONE); citrate if hypocitraturia; treat 2° (hyperPTH parathyroidectomy/RTA/gout). PREGNANCY: US + paracetamol/codeine (avoid NSAID 1st+3rd) + urology if obstruction (JJ/nephrostomy until post-partum); tamsulosin off-label cautious. SSA: hot climate + dehydration + scale-up imaging + urology + ESWL/URS tertiary; primary care awareness.
rationale: EAU 2024 + AUA 2016/2019 + NICE NG118 + SUSPEND Lancet 2015.

title: Food allergy — SPT/specific IgE + OFC; 2 auto-injectors + plan; early peanut introduction (LEAP)
indicators: IgE-mediated reaction within 2 h of food / FPIES / EoE
recommendation: DETAILED history (food/timing/reaction/reproducibility) + SPT + specific IgE (ImmunoCAP) — sensitisation marker NOT diagnostic alone (30-50% false positive); COMPONENT-RESOLVED diagnostics (Ara h 2 peanut, Cor a 14 hazelnut, Gly m 8 soy) increase specificity + risk stratification; ORAL FOOD CHALLENGE gold standard + outgrowth + threshold (supervised allergist + emergency-ready); tryptase if anaphylaxis (within 4 h); eczema severity + atopy + asthma. AVOIDANCE strict for confirmed — read labels (top allergens; 'may contain' confusing); communicate eating out + cross-contamination + school/parties/travel. ADRENALINE AUTO-INJECTOR — TWO (EpiPen/Jext/Emerade) for anaphylaxis history + severe + multiple + asthma+food + persistent peanut/tree nut + mast cell + exercise-induced; TRAIN family + school + carer + child age-appropriate + ANAPHYLAXIS ACTION PLAN pictorial + review annually + replace before expiry + ALWAYS CARRY (biphasic + injector failure). Medic-alert + dietitian + psychosocial + transition. Rescue mild non-anaph: oral antihistamine + observe; severe/progressive → adrenaline. ORAL IMMUNOTHERAPY emerging: PEANUT OIT Palforzia FDA 2020 ages 4-17 — desensitisation + threshold; risk reactions during build-up + EoE; access/cost. EARLY introduction of allergenic foods (LEAP NEJM 2015) — peanut from 4-6 mo in high-risk eczema/egg allergic infants REDUCES allergy 80% — PARADIGM SHIFT (replaced 'delay'); early egg/milk emerging; OMALIZUMAB adjunct OIT (OUtMATCH 2024 raises threshold + safer multi-food). OUTGROWING: milk + egg 50-80% by school age — re-challenge q12-24 mo allergist; peanut + tree nut + fish + shellfish usually lifelong; component results predict. FPIES (non-IgE): acute IV fluid + ondansetron + (refractory methylpred 1 mg/kg); chronic avoid trigger + supervised reintro 12-18 mo (yearly); common triggers cow milk/soy/rice/oats/egg. EoE: PPI + topical steroid (swallowed fluticasone/budesonide) + elimination diet (6-food/4-food/milk-only) + dilatation strictures + dupilumab FDA. Proctocolitis: maternal exclusion if breastfed; eHF formula if formula-fed; resolves by 1 yr usually. Pollen-food (OAS): cook trigger (denature); avoid raw if sx; usually mild; rare anaph. Pregnancy/lactation: NORMAL diet (no restriction benefit; promotes tolerance). SSA: emerging + auto-injector access + cost advocacy + school education + train primary care + integrate with anaphylaxis algorithm.
rationale: EAACI 2024 + BSACI + LEAP NEJM 2015 + OUtMATCH 2024.

title: Enuresis — exclude underlying + reassure + alarm first-line; desmopressin for short-term/refractory
indicators: wetting > 5 yr / daytime sx / family concern
recommendation: EXCLUDE underlying — UTI (urinalysis), DM (glycosuria), constipation (common contributor — treat), OSA (snoring + adenotonsillar — treat may resolve enuresis), neurological/structural (US KUB/MRI spine if daytime + sx + recurrent UTI). Secondary enuresis → workup more carefully. REASSURE — common + most outgrow + not naughty + no punishment. LIFESTYLE: adequate daytime fluid (6-8 drinks evenly); restrict evening fluid 2 h before bed; avoid caffeine + dark fizzy + chocolate; regular voiding day q2-3h + before bed + double void bedtime; treat constipation (Movicol/laxative + regular toileting); positive reward chart + no punishment; lifting/waking limited evidence — discontinue if not working. TREATMENT ages 5-7+ (or distress earlier): ENURESIS ALARM first-line — body-worn or pad-sound — child wakes to alarm → toilet → reset; 14-week trial; supportive parent + child engaged; cure ~ 65% (better long-term than meds; low relapse); continue until 14 consecutive dry or 14 wk. DESMOPRESSIN alternative/combination — short-term (sleepover/camp) or alarm not feasible/older — 120-240 μg sublingual (or 200-400 μg tab) at bedtime; RESTRICT FLUID EVENING (HYPONATRAEMIC SEIZURE risk if drink late — counsel + monitor); withdraw periodically — 1 wk break q3 mo; combination alarm + desmopressin for refractory. Imipramine 25-50 nocte historic — TOXIC overdose + cardiac risk — last resort + specialist only. Antimuscarinic (oxybutynin/tolterodine) if daytime overactive — specialist. REFER specialist if refractory / daytime + nocturnal / structural / underlying / safeguarding / mental health. PSYCHOSOCIAL: reassurance + sibling teasing + school + sleepovers + camp planning + self-esteem; address bullying + parental frustration; counselling if needed. Adult enuresis — neuro/structural/sleep/OUD/alcohol/psychiatric workup essential — never assume primary. SSA: constipation + UTI common contributors + train primary care + non-pharm for resource-limited.
rationale: NICE CG111 + ICCS 2020.

title: Asymmetric SNHL + tinnitus — MRI IAM for VS; CBT + hearing aid for tinnitus distress
indicators: tinnitus / unilateral SNHL / imbalance / NF2 family
recommendation: AUDIOLOGY: pure-tone audiogram + tympanometry + acoustic reflex + speech audiometry. IF ASYMMETRIC SNHL ≥ 15 dB any frequency or ≥ 10 dB 2 adjacent — MRI INTERNAL AUDITORY MEATUS + cerebellopontine angle WITH GADOLINIUM gold for VS. Tinnitus questionnaire TFI/THI. Identify treatable cause: cerumen + OME + otosclerosis + Meniere's + ototoxic review. Pulsatile tinnitus: MRA + MRV + duplex + autoimmune + ferritin (vascular — AVM/glomus/dural fistula/atherosclerosis/BIH). Bilateral VS/family — NF2 genetics. TINNITUS management: reassure benign primary + most habituate + address fears/catastrophising; treat treatable cause; HEARING AID for tinnitus + hearing loss — most effective intervention (masks + improves background); CBT strongest evidence for distress (NICE NG98 + AAO-HNS) + TRT; sound enrichment / masking (white noise + fan + music + masker); AVOID promising silence cures; AVOID gingko/B12/melatonin (AAO-HNS no evidence); sleep hygiene + relaxation + meditation + mindfulness + low-dose antidepressant if mood comorbid; avoid ototoxic + further noise + hearing protection; severe distress/suicide — MH urgent; cochlear implant for SNHL + tinnitus (severe-profound bilateral); BIMODAL stimulation (Lenire auditory + tongue) FDA 2023 emerging. VESTIBULAR SCHWANNOMA: SMALL < 1.5 cm intracanalicular — WATCH + WAIT (MRI q6-12 mo initially then yearly — most slow); growth/sx/larger > 1.5-2 cm — INTERVENE: STEREOTACTIC RADIOSURGERY (Gamma Knife/CyberKnife/linac) preferred small-medium + hearing preservation; MICROSURGERY (translab sacrifices hearing; middle fossa / retrosigmoid hearing preservation selected small); combined/staged large; facial nerve preservation paramount + skilled centre; hearing aid + CI + auditory brainstem implant (NF2 bilateral). NF2 — MDT (genetics + ENT + neurosurg + ophth + cardiac + tumour surveillance — meningiomas + ependymomas + schwannomas); bevacizumab anti-VEGF refractory NF2 schwannoma. Tinnitus UK + ANA peer support. SSA: MRI access tertiary + audiology + ENT scale-up + raise awareness asymmetric loss referral.
rationale: AAO-HNS 2014 Tinnitus + 2018 VS + NICE NG98.

title: Capacity — DECISION-SPECIFIC + 4-step functional test; presume capacity; support before declaring lack
indicators: treatment/finance/residence decision + concern about decision-making ability
recommendation: 5 PRINCIPLES (MCA 2005): presume capacity unless proven; all practicable steps to support decision; unwise decision ≠ lack capacity; best interests if lack; least restrictive. 2-STAGE TEST: diagnostic — impairment of mind/brain? functional — can the person UNDERSTAND + RETAIN + WEIGH + COMMUNICATE the decision (any means)? Inability in ANY ONE due to impairment = lacks capacity for THAT DECISION. Capacity is DECISION-SPECIFIC + TIME-SPECIFIC + fluctuates. BEFORE assessing — REASONABLE ADJUSTMENTS: quiet/private + best time-of-day; Easy Read + pictorial + plain language + interpreter + AAC + advocate + family if patient wishes; treat reversible (UTI/hypoxia/electrolyte/drug/infection — delirium reversible); multiple sessions + re-assess after improvement; respect cultural communication. CAPACITY EXISTS — RESPECT decision even if 'unwise'. LACK CAPACITY — best interests: decision-specific + minimum restriction + permissive; consider PAST + PRESENT wishes + values + beliefs + advance statement; consult those close (LPA + family + advocate) but final decision clinical/proxy; document 5 principles + reasoning. ADVANCE DIRECTIVE: valid (specific + signed + witnessed life-sustaining + had capacity + applicable). LPA Health+Welfare AND/OR Property+Finance. DEPRIVATION OF LIBERTY (DoLS/LPS): continuous supervision + control + not free to leave + lacks capacity → authorisation required + least restrictive. SUPPORTED DECISION-MAKING (UNCRPD Art 12) — global shift substitute → supported decision-making even with ID/dementia. PAED: Gillick competence < 16 sufficient understanding can consent; Fraser (contraception under 16); parental responsibility for younger; disagreement → court. EMERGENCY: doctrine of necessity preserve life when capacity not assessable; reassess + comply with directives if any. MHA (UK) — separate from MCA — compulsory psychiatric admission/treatment specific criteria. Research: additional safeguards for those lacking capacity. SAFEGUARDING — undue influence + abuse + financial — pathway. DOCUMENT thoroughly + explain to patient/family. TRAIN all clinicians + regular updates. SSA: Kenya MHA 2022 + draft Mental Capacity Bill + UNCRPD ratified 2008 — develop frameworks + train + community + supported decision-making + safeguarding.
rationale: MCA 2005 + UNCRPD Art 12 + Kenya MHA 2022 + BMA Toolkit.

title: Penicillin allergy — DELABEL low-risk via direct oral challenge; SCAR = lifelong avoidance + alternative class
indicators: reported drug allergy + need for antibiotic or alternative confirmation
recommendation: DETAILED history — drug + indication + timing (immediate < 1h vs delayed > 6h) + nature (urticaria vs rash vs anaph vs SJS vs serum sickness vs DRESS) + severity + hospitalised + how many years + intervening exposure + similar reactions related drugs. PENICILLIN DECISION (UK Penicillin Allergy Algorithm + ALLERGY-NICE): LOW-RISK (childhood rash > 10 yr ago / isolated GI / family-reported / vague) — DIRECT ORAL CHALLENGE single 250 mg amoxicillin observed 60-120 min — outpatient or inpatient trained team — if NEGATIVE DE-LABEL in records (EMR alert removed + patient counselled + alert card); MEDIUM-RISK (urticaria within hours not anaphylaxis) — skin testing + graded challenge (allergist); HIGH-RISK (anaphylaxis/SCAR/recent < 5 yr) — allergist + skin testing + caution; AVOID if SCAR. Should be SYSTEMATIC programme — hospital antibiotic stewardship + outpatient clinic + pharmacist-led + integrated. CROSS-REACTIVITY (modern evidence): penicillin → cephalosporin < 2% (esp different R1 side chain) — cefuroxime/ceftriaxone/cefepime/ceftaz usually safe; cefadroxil/cephalexin/cefaclor more cross-reactive (R1 similar to ampi/amox); penicillin → carbapenem < 1% — can use if not severe; cephalosporin → cephalosporin R1-dependent; penicillin → monobactam (aztreonam) minimal (unless ceftaz allergy — same R1). MODERN guidance side-chain + severity based — NOT blanket avoidance. ANAPHYLAXIS to drug: IM adrenaline + anaph algorithm + AVOID drug + class + auto-injector + medic-alert + allergist + alternative documented. MILD DELAYED rash (T-cell) — safe alternative β-lactam after evaluation. SCAR (SJS/TEN/DRESS/AGEP) — NEVER rechallenge + lifelong alternative + record clearly + alert + counsel. DESENSITISATION for true allergy + no alternative + essential treatment (penicillin for syphilis in pregnancy, sulfa for PCP in HIV, chemo allergy) — inpatient + allergist + ICU-ready + graded 3-12 h; temporary tolerance — must continue uninterrupted. Vaccine allergy: skin test + graded challenge (MMR + flu usually safe with egg allergy per UK + US updates). Contrast media: low-osmolar non-ionic + emergency-ready; pre-med controversial. PENICILLIN DE-LABELLING — highest-impact stewardship intervention (reduces vanco/broad-spectrum/HCAI/cost) — AHRQ + WHO advocate. SSA: AMR + stewardship priority + de-labelling cost-effective + train + integrate hospital stewardship.
rationale: EAACI 2024 + BSACI 2020 + NICE NG134 + AHRQ + PALACE JAMA 2022.

title: Pheo — α-block BEFORE β-block (NEVER β alone); 7-14 d pre-op + volume load
indicators: resistant HTN + paroxysmal sx / hereditary syndrome / adrenal incidentaloma + sx
recommendation: DIAGNOSIS: PLASMA FREE METANEPHRINES first-line or 24h URINE FRACTIONATED METANEPHRINES — avoid pre-test caffeine/paracetamol/TCA/SSRI/labetalol false-positives; supine 30 min before; CT/MRI adrenal/abdo/chest/pelvis + MIBG / 68-Ga DOTATATE PET; GENETICS all < 50 yr + bilateral + extra-adrenal + family + metastatic (10 genes); ECG + echo (catecholamine CM); HbA1c. PREOPERATIVE α-BLOCKADE 7-14 d BEFORE surgery MANDATORY: PHENOXYBENZAMINE 10 BD titrate 1-2 mg/kg/d (gold; supply limited) OR DOXAZOSIN 2 BD titrate 16-32 mg/d (selective α1); goals BP < 130/80 sitting + orthostatic 90 SBP acceptable + no paroxysms + nasal congestion + postural sx (effective blockade signs); LIBERAL SALT + FLUIDS last 3-5 d (catecholamines deplete volume — collapse on surgery). ADD β-BLOCKER ONLY AFTER α-blockade ≥ 3-4 d — NEVER β-FIRST (unopposed α → HTN crisis + cardiogenic shock + death). CCB (nicardipine/amlodipine) adjunct if labile. AVOID metoclopramide/glucagon/some opioids/cold pressor/IV contrast in unblocked. SURGERY: laparoscopic adrenalectomy (open > 6-8 cm/invasive); extra-adrenal location-dependent; anaesthetist expertise + arterial line + CVP + esmolol/phentolamine/nitroprusside/NTG/Mg ready; post-op hypotension common (catecholamine withdrawal) + fluid/pressor + hypoglycaemia. FOLLOW: metanephrines 2-6 wk post-op confirm cure + annual lifelong (recurrence 6-23% over 10 yr; higher SDHB/hereditary/paraganglioma) + imaging if biochemical. METASTATIC: 131I-MIBG + sunitinib + Lu-177 DOTATATE PRRT + CVD chemo + belzutifan (HIF-2α VHL/SDH); symptom α+β. PREG: plasma metanephrines + MRI (no CT); α first + β after; 2nd-trimester resection or post-delivery; MDT. SSA: phenoxybenzamine limited — doxazosin alt + surgical/anaesthetic expertise advocacy.
rationale: Endocrine Society 2014 + ESE 2024 + ENS@T.

title: Hyperprolactinaemia — exclude drug/hypothyroid/pregnancy first; cabergoline first-line; surgery selected
indicators: galactorrhoea / amenorrhoea / infertility / male hypogonadism / pituitary mass + raised PRL
recommendation: MORNING PRL (rest 30 min + no breast exam + fasting) — repeat borderline; > 100 ng/mL usually adenoma + > 200 macroadenoma. CHECK MACROPROLACTIN (PEG precipitation) — common asymptomatic false-high. RULE OUT 'HOOK EFFECT' macroadenoma + low PRL — dilute if imaging-level disconnect. WORKUP cause: drug history (review + switch culprit — antipsychotic to aripiprazole/quetiapine; metoclopramide/SSRI/methadone/verapamil/ranitidine); TSH (hypothyroid → TRH); creatinine (renal); hCG (pregnancy). Pituitary MRI + contrast if not drug/thyroid/pregnancy/renal + full pituitary function + visual fields if macro/compression. TREAT CAUSE: stop/switch drug; treat hypothyroidism; pregnancy normalises post-delivery. PROLACTINOMA → DOPAMINE AGONIST first-line: CABERGOLINE 0.25 mg twice/wk titrate by PRL (typical 0.5-1 mg twice/wk; max 3.5/wk) — most effective + tolerated + high MRI shrinkage; BROMOCRIPTINE 1.25 nocte titrate 2.5-15 mg/d alt (preferred pre-conception/pregnancy — more safety data); quinagolide alt; monitor PRL q1-3 mo until normal + q6-12 mo + MRI 1 yr + q1-2 yr + visual fields macro; withdrawal after ≥ 2 yr normal + tumour shrinkage MRI (30-40% sustained remission). SURGERY transsphenoidal: DA intolerance/resistance/visual not improving/CSF leak/apoplexy/pregnancy planning macro near chiasm — high-volume centre (cure micro 70-80%/macro 30-40%). RT selected refractory; TMZ aggressive. HYPOGONADISM (persistent): oestrogen+progesterone female / testosterone male AFTER tumour control + bone (DEXA + Ca+D + bisphosphonate if osteoporotic). PREG: most resume fertility on DA; STOP DA at confirmed preg IF micro (low growth); CONTINUE DA macro > 1 cm or near chiasm (bromocriptine more data); visual field each trimester + headache awareness; restart if growth + breastfeed usually OK; restart DA after weaning if needed. MEN1/AIP screen young + family. SSA: cabergoline/bromocriptine widely available; transsphenoidal limited (KNH) + MDT referral.
rationale: Endocrine Society 2011 + ESE 2024.

title: PMDD — DRSP × 2 cycles + luteal SSRI + drospirenone COC; GnRH refractory
recommendation: DSM-5-TR criteria PMDD + DAILY RECORD OF SEVERITY OF PROBLEMS (DRSP) × 2 prospective cycles confirms cyclical (resolves within 2-3 d menses onset + sx-free week after). EXCLUDE underlying MDD/bipolar/anxiety/OCD/PTSD/thyroid/anaemia/endometriosis/migraine (sx persist outside luteal → different management). Suicide risk assessment (12% lifetime). MILD-MOD: aerobic exercise + sleep + reduce caffeine/alcohol/Na luteal + mindfulness + CBT + Ca 1200/d + B6 50-100/d + Mg 200-360/d + evening primrose (modest evidence) + symptom diary. SEVERE/functional impairment FIRST-LINE: SSRI continuous OR LUTEAL-PHASE-ONLY (day 14 to menses; emerging symptom-onset dosing — Eriksson) — sertraline 50-150/fluoxetine 20/paroxetine/escitalopram/citalopram/venlafaxine — EFFECTIVE WITHIN 1-2 CYCLES (faster than MDD); side effects + sexual + weight monitor. COC with DROSPIRENONE 24/4 (Yaz/Yasmin) FDA-approved PMDD — superior other COCs; some women continuous (extended) COC eliminates withdrawal sx. REFRACTORY: GnRH ANALOGUE leuprolide/goserelin + add-back oestrogen+progesterone — ovulation suppression — significant relief; bone (DEXA + Ca+D + bisphosphonate if prolonged); surgical bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy ± hysterectomy + HRT — last resort + completed family; mindfulness/DBT/ACT; sepranolone (allopregnanolone modulator) trials. CO-OCCURRING — treat MDD/anxiety/OCD/ED in parallel. PSYCHOSOCIAL: education + family/partner + validate + peer support + impact relationships/work + reduce stigma. PERIMENOPAUSE: PMDD can worsen; HRT may help; may transition MDD/anxiety. PREG/POSTPARTUM: usually quiescent preg; postpartum depression/anxiety risk increased — anticipate + screen + treat. SSA: SSRI affordable (KEML); women's mental health integration + advocacy + reduce stigma.
rationale: ACOG 2023 + RCOG 2017 + ISPMD.

title: GTD — suction evacuation + serial β-hCG + chemo for GTN (MTX low-risk / EMA-CO high-risk)
indicators: very high β-hCG + 1st-trim bleed + uterus > dates + snowstorm US / persistent β-hCG post-pregnancy
recommendation: DIAGNOSIS: quantitative β-hCG (> 100,000 mole) + serial + pelvic US (snowstorm complete; partial mole + fetus + abnormal placenta) + HISTOPATH + ploidy (complete 46XX paternal / partial 69-triploid). Pre-evac: FBC+UEC+LFT+TFT+coag+blood group+CXR (lung mets baseline). GTN suspected: WHO FIGO score (age+antecedent preg+interval+β-hCG+tumour size+sites+mets number+prior chemo); ≤ 6 low-risk / ≥ 7 high-risk + staging CT chest/abdo/pelvis + MRI brain (high-risk) + LP if neuro; cardiology/thyroid storm if very high β-hCG (cross-reacts TSH). MOLAR PREGNANCY: SUCTION EVACUATION experienced centre + cross-match + IV + uterotonic post (NOT misoprostol — trophoblast embolisation); anti-D if Rh- (partial — fetal tissue); histopath + ploidy; CONTRACEPTION mandatory while β-hCG monitored (COC preferred + IUD after normal); avoid preg 6 mo (complete) or 12 mo (partial/GTN); REGISTER national trophoblastic centre (UK Charing Cross/Sheffield/Dundee; Kenya KEMRI/KNH oncology). FOLLOW β-hCG: weekly until normal × 3 then monthly × 6-12 mo (complete) or 6 (partial); rising/plateau = GTN. GTN (persistent/metastatic/choriocarcinoma): WHO FIGO determines regimen — LOW-RISK ≤ 6: single agent METHOTREXATE (0.4 mg/kg/d × 5 d q2 wk OR 50 mg IM days 1,3,5,7 + folinic 2,4,6,8) or DACT alternative/salvage — cure > 90%; HIGH-RISK ≥ 7 / mets (lung > 3 cm/brain/liver): EMA-CO (etoposide+MTX+DACT+cyclo+vincristine); brain mets — high-dose MTX + IT MTX + WBRT/SRS; liver — TAE+chemo; cure 80-90%; refractory: EMA-EP; BEP; immunotherapy emerging; hysterectomy selected (perimenopausal/resistant local/life-threatening bleed). PSTT/ETT chemo-resistant — hysterectomy + EMA-EP. Subsequent pregs usually normal; 1-2% recurrence; early US + β-hCG post-delivery. PSYCHOSOCIAL: preg loss + cancer + chemo + fertility uncertainty — counselling. SSA: Kenya KEMRI/KNH/Aga Khan oncology referral; MTX/DACT widely available; EMA-CO tertiary; trophoblastic registry advocacy.
rationale: ESMO 2022 + RCOG GTG 38 + FIGO + Charing Cross.

title: SVT — vagal → adenosine; AF + WPW = DC cardiovert (AV-node blockers CONTRAINDICATED); ablation curative
indicators: narrow regular tach 150-250 + palpitations / irregular wide-complex + delta wave / pre-excited AF
recommendation: 12-LEAD ECG during + sinus (short PR + delta wave WPW); telemetry/Holter/loop; echo to exclude structural; EPS + accessory pathway refractory period stratify WPW (< 250 ms high risk); electrolytes + TSH + drug/caffeine. ACUTE SVT (stable narrow regular): VAGAL FIRST — Valsalva modified (supine + leg-raise — REVERT Lancet 2015 — more effective than standard) or carotid sinus massage (auscultate first + avoid elderly/bruit/TIA); ADENOSINE 6 mg IV rapid bolus + 20 mL flush antecubital → 12 mg → 12 mg q1-2 min (warn brief chest discomfort + flushing + 'impending doom'; caution asthma theoretical + transplant start 3 mg); verapamil 5-10 IV (avoid WPW/HF/LV dys); diltiazem 0.25 mg/kg IV; β-blocker (metoprolol 5 IV); SYNCHRONISED DC CARDIOVERSION 50-100 J if unstable/refractory. AF + WPW (PRE-EXCITED AF — IRREGULAR WIDE COMPLEX) EMERGENCY: SYNCHRONISED DC CARDIOVERSION 100-200 J first-line; procainamide 10-15 mg/kg IV over 30 min if stable + no IHD/HF; ibutilide alt. AVOID ALL AV-NODE BLOCKERS (adenosine/β-blocker/CCB/digoxin/IV amiodarone) — facilitate accessory → VF. Anticoag per AF (CHADS-VASc) + plan EPS + ABLATION. PROPHYLAXIS recurrent: CATHETER ABLATION first-line symptomatic + WPW + recurrent — > 95% success + curative + minimal complication; drug therapy alt — β-blocker/CCB(verapamil)/flecainide/propafenone (no IHD) AVRT/AVNRT. ASYMPTOMATIC WPW: risk stratify EPS — short refractory < 250 ms + multiple pathways + high-risk occupation → ablation; most asymptomatic + long refractory observe. PREG: vagal+adenosine safe; β-blocker (metoprolol; avoid atenolol 1st-trimester); flecainide alt; delay ablation until post-delivery if possible (radiation). EDUCATION: identify + train vagal self-administer + medic-alert + recognise + ED if SVT/AF. SSA: vagal+adenosine+DC cardioversion widely; catheter ablation tertiary (KNH/Aga Khan/few); EPS scale-up advocacy.
rationale: ESC 2019 SVT + ACC/AHA/HRS 2015 + 2024 AF + REVERT Lancet 2015.

title: Acute prostatitis/epididymo-orchitis — Rule out testicular torsion; STI vs uropathogen pathway
indicators: fever + perineal/pelvic pain + dysuria / scrotal pain + swelling
recommendation: EXCLUDE TESTICULAR TORSION (young man + sudden + nausea + high-riding + absent cremasteric + < 6h = SURGICAL EMERGENCY — Doppler if available + immediate exploration). Diagnosis: urinalysis + culture (MSU); STI screen if epididymitis < 35/risk — urethral/urine NAAT chlamydia+gonorrhoea+HIV+syphilis (Kenya NASCOP syndromic + lab); acute prostatitis blood culture if septic + FBC+CRP+creatinine + PSA NOT acute (recheck 6-8 wk); imaging US Doppler torsion + TRUS abscess; Mears-Stamey chronic. ACUTE BACTERIAL PROSTATITIS: outpatient mild — ciprofloxacin 500 BD or cotrim 960 BD × 2-4 wk; inpatient severe — gentamicin + ampicillin OR ceftriaxone 2 g IV OD then PO step-down cipro; duration 2-4 wk; analgesia + α-blocker (tamsulosin) LUTS + suprapubic catheter if retention (avoid urethral); drain abscess if found. CHRONIC BACTERIAL PROSTATITIS: cipro/levo × 4-6 wk (prostate penetration); cotrim alt; refractory tetracycline/azithro. CHRONIC PROSTATITIS/CPPS: UPOINT — Urinary (α-blocker) + Psychosocial (CBT) + Organ-specific (5α-RI/NSAID/pelvic-floor PT) + Infection (trial Abx if Mears-Stamey) + Neuro (gabapentin/amitriptyline) + Tenderness (pelvic-floor PT); MDT. EPIDIDYMO-ORCHITIS: < 35 yr or STI risk — CEFTRIAXONE 500 mg IM single + DOXYCYCLINE 100 BD × 10-14 d (covers chlamydia + gonorrhoea); test of cure GC 1 wk + chlamydia 4 wk; contact tracing partners; HIV+syphilis screen; Kenya MoH algorithm. ≥ 35 yr/no STI risk OR enteric organism: cipro 500 BD × 10-14 d or ofloxacin. Severe/sepsis: IV ceftriaxone + admit + urology. Bed rest + scrotal elevation + ice + analgesia + NSAID + ABSTAIN sex until partners treated; surgical exploration if torsion uncertain. Mumps orchitis supportive; TB epididymo-orchitis chronic indurated — biopsy + workup + ATT. PREVENT: safe sex + condoms + STI screen + partner notification + treat + PrEP MSM + vaccines (HPV/HBV/menACWY); treat BPH/structural. FOLLOW: PSA 6-8 wk if elevated + sexual function counsel + recurrence. SSA: STI Abx widely + Kenya NASCOP syndromic + tertiary urology + TB awareness.
rationale: EAU 2024 + NICE NG109 + CDC STI 2021 + Kenya NASCOP.

title: PSC — MRCP + annual colonoscopy + cancer surveillance; transplant when MELD high; AVOID high-dose URSO
indicators: cholestatic LFT + IBD / MRCP beaded ducts / pruritus + raised ALP
recommendation: MRCP gold (multifocal strictures/dilatations/beaded intra+extrahepatic); ERCP only if intervention (dominant stricture/brush cytology/stenting — cholangitis risk); LFT cholestatic + AMA neg (exclude PBC) + IgG4 + ANA/ANCA p-positive 70%; biopsy small-duct only; COLONOSCOPY at dx + ANNUAL (50-75% IBD subclinical + UC-PSC HIGHEST CRC risk — chromoendoscopy); CA 19-9 baseline + annual (cholangiocarcinoma surveillance); US 6-12 monthly (HCC/cholangio/GB); Fibroscan staging. NO disease-modifying with survival benefit; URSO 13-15 mg/kg/d low-mid (some clinicians for sx/LFT — DOES NOT improve survival) — AVOID HIGH-DOSE > 28 mg/kg (Lindor NEJM 2009 adverse); vedolizumab + investigational FXR/norUDCA/anti-LOXL2 trials. DOMINANT STRICTURE: ERCP + balloon dilatation ± temporary stent + BRUSH + FISH — cholangiocarcinoma workup. CHOLANGITIS: ceftriaxone + metronidazole + URGENT biliary drainage (ERCP/PTC/surgery). PRURITUS: cholestyramine 4 BD-QDS + rifampicin 150-600 + naltrexone/nalmefene + sertraline + odevixibat (IBAT) emerging + phototherapy refractory. MAINTENANCE: fat-soluble vits (ADEK) + bone (DEXA + Ca+D + bisphosphonate if osteo) + vaccines (no live cirrhotic/pre-tx — pneumo+flu+COVID+zoster recomb+HepA+HepB) + CV RF + statin (NOT CI) + treat IBD. SURVEILLANCE: cholangio annual CA 19-9 + MRI/MRCP; CRC annual colon (UC-PSC chromo); GB annual US + cholecystectomy ANY polyp; HCC 6-monthly US ± AFP; osteo DEXA q2-3 yr; variceal endoscopy at cirrhosis + q1-2 yr. TRANSPLANT: MELD ≥ 15 or refractory pruritus/cholangitis/dominant strictures unresponsive/QoL; PSC-specific MELD exception many programmes; recurrence post-tx 20-30%; CCA + tx — Mayo protocol selected early hilar < 3 cm + chemo-RT + tx. SSA: MRCP tertiary; ERCP for dominant; URSO + supportive widely; transplant emerging (Kenya KNH planning); cholangitis prompt treatment awareness.
rationale: EASL 2022 + AASLD 2021 + BSG + Lindor NEJM 2009.

title: PBC — UDCA first-line; OCA/fibrate/seladelpar/elafibranor for inadequate response (POISE/BEZURSO/ELATIVE)
indicators: female + raised ALP + AMA-positive / pruritus + cholestasis
recommendation: DIAGNOSIS: ALP > 1.5× ULN + AMA-M2 + (≥ 1:40) — diagnostic without biopsy in most; AMA-negative 5-10% — anti-sp100/gp210/PML (PBC ANA) + biopsy/clinical; LFT cholestatic + bili + albumin + INR + IgG/IgM + ANA/SMA (exclude AIH overlap) + lipids + TSH (autoimmune thyroid 20-25%) + DEXA + bone + vit D + US baseline (HCC surveillance) + Fibroscan; biopsy reserved AMA-neg/AIH overlap/atypical. FIRST-LINE: URSODEOXYCHOLIC ACID (URSO/UDCA) 13-15 mg/kg/d divided — improves LFT + SURVIVAL + reduces transplant (POISE + cohort); response 12 mo POISE-criteria/Paris-II/Toronto/GLOBE/UK-PBC; GOOD: ALP < 1.67× ULN + bili normal — continue UDCA only; INADEQUATE 25-40% — ADD second-line. SECOND-LINE: OBETICHOLIC ACID (Ocaliva FXR — POISE NEJM 2016 FDA 2016) 5 OD titrate 10 mg — SE pruritus dose-limiting + caution decompensated cirrhosis (label restrictions); FIBRATES bezafibrate 400 OD (BEZURSO NEJM 2018) or fenofibrate — LFT + survival; off-label many countries; renal+muscle monitor; triple (UDCA+OCA+fibrate) emerging. THIRD-LINE: SELADELPAR (PPARδ — RESPONSE Hepatology 2023 FDA 2024); ELAFIBRANOR (PPARα/δ — ELATIVE NEJM 2023 FDA 2024); transplant end-stage/refractory pruritus. PRURITUS: cholestyramine 4 BD-QDS + rifampicin 150-600 + naltrexone/nalmefene + sertraline + IBAT odevixibat/linerixibat (GLIMMER). FATIGUE: r/o anaemia+hypothyroid+OSA+depression + modafinil selected. OSTEO: Ca + vit D + bisphosphonate/denosumab if FRAX-high. DYSLIPIDAEMIA: statin (not CI). AIH-PBC OVERLAP: + pred + AZA on UDCA. PREG: UDCA safe; cholestasis worsens 3rd trim — pruritus + LFT + fetal wellbeing + MDT. VACCINES pneumo+flu+COVID+HepA+HepB+zoster recomb (no live cirrhotic/IS). HCC 6-monthly US ± AFP cirrhotic. TRANSPLANT MELD ≥ 15 + refractory + severe pruritus + variceal bleed; recurrence 20-30%. SSA: UDCA KEML widely; OCA/fibrate/newer agents access advocacy; transplant emerging.
rationale: EASL 2017 + AASLD 2018/2023 + POISE/BEZURSO/ELATIVE/Seladelpar RESPONSE.

title: PNH — flow cytometry; complement inhibitor + meningococcal vaccine; LMWH thrombosis; allo-HSCT curative
indicators: intravascular haemolysis + thrombosis + AA overlap + low CD55/CD59 flow
recommendation: DIAGNOSIS: FLOW CYTOMETRY GPI-anchor (CD55+CD59) deficient on RBC + granulocytes + monocytes; FLAER most sensitive; FBC + retic + LDH (very high) + haptoglobin low + indirect bili + urine haemosiderin; DAT NEGATIVE distinguishes from AIHA; iron studies (chronic haemoglobinuria → IDA); UEC+LFT+coag+D-dimer; BM if cytopenias/AA overlap/MDS workup; imaging for thrombosis (Doppler/CT/MRI venous/MRCP Budd-Chiari). COMPLEMENT INHIBITION first-line for symptomatic (haemolysis/thrombosis/transfusion-dep): ECULIZUMAB (Soliris) C5i IV q14 d — TRIUMPH/SHEPHERD NEJM 2004/06 landmark — reduces haemolysis+thrombosis+improves survival; RAVULIZUMAB (Ultomiris) long-acting C5i IV q8 wk — FDA 2018 non-inferior + convenient; PEGCETACOPLAN (Empaveli) C3i SC twice wk — FDA 2021 PEGASUS NEJM 2021 superior to anti-C5 in suboptimal Hb; IPTACOPAN (Fabhalta) ORAL factor B BD — FDA 2023 APPLY/APPOINT — FIRST ORAL; danicopan add-on; crovalimab emerging. MENINGOCOCCAL VACCINE MenACWY + MenB ≥ 2 wk BEFORE complement inhibitor + revaccinate per schedule (MENINGOCOCCAL SEPSIS risk 1000× on anti-C5); PEN V 250 BD additional layer ≥ first 2 wk + ongoing some programmes; medic-alert + emergency Abx supply + fever education; pneumo+Hib+flu+COVID also. FOLATE+IRON. ANTICOAG: acute thrombosis therapeutic LMWH → DOAC (apix/rivarox) or warfarin INR 2-3; prophylaxis if clone > 50% + thrombosis hx (not all asymptomatic on anti-C5); Budd-Chiari anticoag + TIPS/liver tx. ALLO-HSCT CURATIVE: AA/severe pancytopenia/MDS evolution/refractory PNH/preg planning/cost-prohibitive; matched sibling best; MDT. TRANSFUSION + IRON CHELATION as needed. AA overlap: IS (ATG + ciclosporin) + eltrombopag + tx. MDS evolution surveillance (cytogenetics) + tx. PREG: high maternal+fetal risk+thrombosis; CONTINUE eculizumab/ravulizumab throughout (Kelly NEJM 2015); PROPHYLACTIC LMWH throughout + 6 wk postpartum; MDT close monitor. MONITOR: FBC+LDH+retic+flow clone size periodic + thrombosis surveillance. SSA: ultra-rare + complement inhibitor access EXTREMELY LIMITED + cost ($400-700k/yr US) — advocacy + tx access + trial referral.
rationale: International PNH WG 2024 + TRIUMPH/SHEPHERD + PEGASUS + APPLY-PNH.

title: HTN urgency vs emergency — END-ORGAN distinguishes; gradual oral vs IV titration
recommendation: First — distinguish URGENCY vs EMERGENCY (end-organ damage). Repeat BP after 15-30 min rest + appropriate cuff + both arms (asymmetry > 20 mmHg → consider dissection). Examine end-organ: neuro (mental+focal+fundoscopy), cardiac (chest pain+ECG+troponin+CXR+echo), renal (urinalysis+UEC), aortic (asym pulse+CT), preg (urinalysis+PCR+FBC+LFT+reflexes); med history + adherence + new drugs (cocaine/sympathomimetic/MAOI+tyramine/sudden BP-med stop). URGENCY (BP ≥ 180/120 + NO acute organ): NO IV — slow oral reduction over h-d; goal 20-25% reduction over 24-48 h to ≤ 160/100 then gradual to 140/90 over d-wk; AVOID short-acting nifedipine sublingual (sudden drops + ischaemic events — historic + abandoned); restart/adjust regimen (ACE-i/ARB/CCB/thiazide/β-blocker); identify trigger (non-adherence+new med+pain+anxiety+alcohol+drugs); outpatient 24-48 h follow-up; ensure no end-organ before discharge. EMERGENCY (severe + acute end-organ): ICU/HDU + arterial line + IV titration; goal 25% MAP reduction within 1 h (some scenarios faster) → ~ 160/100 over 2-6 h → gradual 140/90 over 24-48 h; AVOID rapid normalisation (cerebral/coronary/renal hypoperfusion). AGENT BY CAUSE: HYPERTENSIVE ENCEPHALOPATHY / acute ischaemic stroke + tPA (BP > 185/110) — labetalol/nicardipine; AVOID nitroprusside (ICP rise). ACUTE ICH (SBP > 180): nicardipine/labetalol target SBP ~ 140 (INTERACT-3/ATACH-II). ACS: nitroglycerin + β-blocker (labetalol/metoprolol). ACUTE LVF/pulm oedema: NTG + furosemide + nitroprusside/clevidipine. AORTIC DISSECTION: target SBP < 120 + HR < 60 within 5-10 min — ESMOLOL/LABETALOL FIRST then nicardipine/nitroprusside (β before vasodilator — shear stress). AKI: nicardipine/fenoldopam. PHEO CRISIS: PHENTOLAMINE (α-blocker)/nitroprusside; NEVER β alone (unopposed α). ECLAMPSIA/SEVERE PE: LABETALOL/NIFEDIPINE IR safe preg + MAGNESIUM for seizure prevention. COCAINE/sympathomimetic: BENZODIAZEPINE first (calms sympathetic) + phentolamine/NTG; AVOID β alone (unopposed α). IV AGENTS: labetalol 10-20 IV bolus + infusion / nicardipine 5 mg/h titrate / clevidipine / NTG infusion / nitroprusside (last resort + ICU + cyanide + short-term) / esmolol (dissection+tachyarrhythmia) / hydralazine IV (preg). POST-EMERGENCY: transition oral + outpatient follow-up + workup secondary HTN if young/refractory (renal Doppler+art+plasma metanephrines+ARR+TSH+cortisol+OSA). PRIMARY CARE: home BP + adherence + lifestyle (DASH+reduce Na+weight+exercise+alcohol+smoking) + medication reconciliation + barriers. SSA: oral antihypertensives (amlodipine+lisinopril+losartan+HCTZ) KEML; IV tertiary; Mg for preg emergency universal + Kenya MoH protocol.
rationale: ESC 2024 + ACC/AHA 2017/2023 + NICE NG136 + INTERACT-3 + ATACH-II.

title: Neonatal hypoglycaemia — recognition and operational thresholds
description: For at-risk neonates (preterm <37 weeks, SGA, LGA, infant of diabetic mother, perinatal stress) screen blood glucose by 2 h of life and every 3-6 h before feeds for the first 24 h. Operational thresholds: <2.6 mmol/L (47 mg/dL) in first 48 h — feed and recheck; <2.0 mmol/L (36 mg/dL) or any symptomatic — IV 10% dextrose 2 mL/kg bolus then infusion 60-80 mL/kg/day (GIR 4-6 mg/kg/min) and admit. Persistent hypoglycaemia >48 h — investigate hyperinsulinism, metabolic, endocrine.

outcomes.summary: Neonatal glucose <2.0 mmol/L or symptomatic — IV dextrose now
outcomes.detail: Give 10% dextrose 2 mL/kg IV bolus, start maintenance infusion, admit to neonatal unit.
outcomes.suggestion: Avoid bolus of >10% dextrose peripherally; use 12.5% or central line for higher concentrations.

outcomes.summary: At-risk neonate — screen glucose by 2 h of life
outcomes.detail: Risk factors: preterm, SGA, LGA, IDM, sepsis, perinatal stress, cold stress.

references.label: BAPM Identification and Management of Neonatal Hypoglycaemia in the Full Term Infant 2017
WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children 2013

title: Neonatal hyperbilirubinaemia — Bhutani-based phototherapy and exchange thresholds
description: Plot total serum bilirubin against postnatal age in hours on AAP 2022 nomograms, adjusted by gestational age and neurotoxicity risk factors (isoimmune haemolysis, G6PD deficiency, asphyxia, sepsis, hypoalbuminaemia <30 g/L, lethargy, temperature instability, acidosis). Start phototherapy when TSB at or above the gestation-and-risk-specific phototherapy threshold; arrange urgent exchange transfusion if TSB exceeds the exchange threshold or any bilirubin-induced neurologic dysfunction sign is present.

outcomes.summary: TSB above exchange threshold or BIND signs — escalate now
outcomes.detail: Prepare exchange transfusion, continue intensive phototherapy, IV hydration, treat sepsis/haemolysis.

outcomes.summary: TSB at phototherapy threshold — start intensive phototherapy
outcomes.detail: Use blue light 425-475 nm, ≥30 µW/cm²/nm, maximum exposed skin, continue breastfeeding.

references.label: AAP Clinical Practice Guideline Revision: Management of Hyperbilirubinemia in the Newborn Infant ≥35 Weeks of Gestation 2022
NICE CG98 Jaundice in newborn babies under 28 days

title: Late preterm infant (34+0 to 36+6 weeks) — discharge pathway
description: Late preterm infants are at higher risk of feeding difficulty, hypoglycaemia, jaundice, respiratory distress, and readmission. Before discharge: 24 h documented thermoregulation in open cot, 24 h successful feeding, weight loss <7%, bilirubin trend on nomogram, hearing screen, car seat tolerance if eligible, follow-up within 48-72 h.

outcomes.summary: Late preterm — apply discharge bundle and 48-72 h review
outcomes.detail: Defer discharge until criteria met; arrange community midwife/health visitor review.

references.label: AAP Clinical Report: Late-Preterm Infants 2007 (reaffirmed)
NICE NG194 Postnatal care

title: Acute paediatric asthma — BTS/SIGN severity bands
description: Grade severity by SpO2, work of breathing, ability to speak/feed, HR and RR. Moderate (SpO2 ≥92%, no severe features) — salbutamol 4-10 puffs MDI+spacer every 20 min for 1 h, oral prednisolone 1-2 mg/kg (max 40 mg) once daily for 3 days. Severe (SpO2 <92%, unable to talk in sentences, accessory muscles) — add ipratropium 250 mcg neb back-to-back, IV magnesium 40 mg/kg (max 2 g) over 20 min if no response. Life-threatening (silent chest, cyanosis, exhaustion, SpO2 <90%) — IV salbutamol load 15 mcg/kg over 10 min then infusion, paediatric intensivist, anaesthetic standby.

outcomes.summary: Life-threatening features — escalate to PICU
outcomes.detail: Silent chest, cyanosis, hypotension, exhaustion or SpO2 <90% on oxygen.

outcomes.summary: Severe exacerbation — back-to-back nebs + IV magnesium
outcomes.detail: Reassess every 15 min; oral steroid stat.

references.label: BTS/SIGN/NICE Asthma joint guideline 2024
GINA 2024 — Paediatric supplement

title: Croup — Westley score guides oral dexamethasone and nebulised adrenaline
description: Mild (Westley 0-2; barking cough, no stridor at rest) — single oral dexamethasone 0.15-0.6 mg/kg (max 12 mg). Moderate (3-7; stridor at rest, mild retraction) — dexamethasone plus observation 2-4 h. Severe (8-11) — nebulised adrenaline 0.5 mL/kg of 1:1000 (max 5 mL), dexamethasone, oxygen, admit. Impending respiratory failure (≥12) — anaesthetic and ENT, paediatric ICU.

outcomes.summary: Severe croup — neb adrenaline + dexamethasone now
outcomes.detail: Reassess after 30 min; rebound stridor possible at 2 h — observe ≥4 h after adrenaline.

outcomes.summary: Mild/moderate croup — oral dexamethasone single dose
outcomes.detail: Dexamethasone reduces re-attendance and admission across severity bands.

references.label: Westley CR et al. Nebulized racemic epinephrine by IPPB for the treatment of croup. Am J Dis Child 1978
NICE CKS Croup 2023

title: Bronchiolitis under 2 years — admission criteria and management
description: Admit if any of: apnoea (observed or reported), persistent SpO2 <90% (or <92% per local policy) on room air, inadequate oral intake (50-75% of usual), severe respiratory distress (grunting, marked chest recession, RR >70/min), clinical dehydration, or significant comorbidity (preterm, congenital heart disease, immunodeficiency, neuromuscular). Supportive care only — humidified oxygen, NG/IV fluids; do NOT routinely give salbutamol, ipratropium, adrenaline (nebulised), hypertonic saline, montelukast, antibiotics, or systemic steroids.

outcomes.summary: Bronchiolitis — admit if any red flag present
outcomes.detail: Apnoea, SpO2 <90%, poor feeding, marked work of breathing, dehydration, comorbidity.

outcomes.summary: Avoid routine bronchodilators and antibiotics in bronchiolitis
outcomes.detail: Evidence does not support their use; supportive care is the standard.

references.label: NICE NG9 Bronchiolitis in children: diagnosis and management 2021 update
AAP Clinical Practice Guideline: Diagnosis, Management, and Prevention of Bronchiolitis 2014

title: Paediatric DKA — ISPAD 2022 fluid and insulin protocol
description: Diagnose DKA when glucose >11 mmol/L, venous pH <7.3 or HCO3 <18 mmol/L, ketonaemia (β-hydroxybutyrate ≥3 mmol/L) or moderate-large ketonuria. Start IV fluids first; delay insulin by 1 h after fluids begin (cerebral oedema risk). Use 0.9% saline 10 mL/kg over 30-60 min for shock only, then deficit replacement over 24-48 h with maintenance fluids; assume 5-7% deficit moderate, 7-10% severe. Insulin infusion 0.05-0.1 U/kg/h after the 1 h fluid lead-in; do NOT bolus insulin. Add KCl 40 mmol/L once K<5.5 and urine confirmed. Monitor for cerebral oedema (headache, bradycardia, hypertension, GCS change) — mannitol 0.5-1 g/kg or hypertonic 3% saline 2.5-5 mL/kg.

outcomes.summary: Paediatric DKA — start fluids first, insulin after 1 h, watch cerebral oedema
outcomes.detail: Avoid insulin bolus; avoid bicarbonate; do not exceed 1.5-2× maintenance fluid rate.

references.label: ISPAD Clinical Practice Consensus Guidelines 2022: Diabetic ketoacidosis and hyperglycemic hyperosmolar state

codings.display: Type 1 DM with ketoacidosis without coma

title: Paediatric sepsis — Phoenix Sepsis Score and PEWS recognition
description: Use Phoenix Sepsis Score (respiratory, cardiovascular, coagulation, neurological domains) for sepsis recognition in children with suspected infection; Phoenix Score ≥2 defines sepsis, septic shock when ≥1 cardiovascular point. Use locally adopted PEWS for ward-level deterioration. Sepsis bundle within 1 h: oxygen, IV/IO access, blood cultures, broad-spectrum antibiotics, isotonic crystalloid 10-20 mL/kg bolus (reassess after each), lactate, glucose check. Escalate to vasopressors (peripheral noradrenaline) if persistent hypotension after 40-60 mL/kg.

outcomes.summary: Suspected paediatric sepsis — 1-hour bundle now
outcomes.detail: Cultures + IV antibiotics + balanced crystalloid bolus + lactate within 1 h of recognition.

references.label: Schlapbach LJ et al. International Consensus Criteria for Pediatric Sepsis and Septic Shock (Phoenix). JAMA 2024
Surviving Sepsis Campaign International Guidelines for the Management of Septic Shock and Sepsis-Associated Organ Dysfunction in Children 2020

title: Paediatric UTI — NICE NG224 refer/treat criteria
description: All infants <3 months with suspected UTI — refer to paediatrics for parenteral antibiotics and full septic screen. 3 months to 3 years with unexplained fever ≥38°C — urine sample within 24 h; positive dipstick or microscopy/culture → oral antibiotics 3 days (lower UTI) or 7-10 days and ultrasound within 6 weeks (upper UTI/atypical). Investigate atypical UTI (poor flow, abdominal mass, sepsis, raised creatinine, non-E.coli, no response by 48 h) with US during the infection plus DMSA at 4-6 months.

outcomes.summary: Infant <3 months with suspected UTI — refer for IV antibiotics
outcomes.detail: Do not treat in the community; full septic screen including lumbar puncture per local protocol.

outcomes.summary: Atypical UTI features — arrange imaging
outcomes.detail: US during illness, plus DMSA at 4-6 months; MCUG if recurrent or anomaly on US.

references.label: NICE NG224 Urinary tract infection in under 16s: diagnosis and management 2022

codings.display: Urinary tract infection, site not specified

title: Kawasaki disease — diagnostic criteria and IVIG within 10 days
description: Fever ≥5 days plus ≥4 of: bilateral non-purulent conjunctivitis, oral mucosal changes (red fissured lips, strawberry tongue), polymorphous rash, peripheral changes (erythema/oedema of hands and feet, periungual desquamation), cervical lymphadenopathy ≥1.5 cm. Consider incomplete KD when fever ≥5 days with 2-3 criteria plus raised CRP/ESR or supportive labs. Treat with IVIG 2 g/kg single infusion plus high-dose aspirin 30-50 mg/kg/day, started within 10 days of fever onset. Echocardiogram at baseline, 2 weeks, 6-8 weeks.

outcomes.summary: Suspected Kawasaki disease — IVIG within 10 days
outcomes.detail: Delay risks coronary artery aneurysm; refer paediatric cardiology.

references.label: AHA Scientific Statement: Diagnosis, Treatment, and Long-Term Management of Kawasaki Disease 2017

title: Acute rheumatic fever — 2015 revised Jones criteria
description: In moderate/high-risk populations diagnose ARF when initial episode meets: evidence of recent group A strep infection plus 2 major OR 1 major + 2 minor manifestations. Majors: carditis (clinical or subclinical on echo), arthritis (polyarthritis OR monoarthritis OR polyarthralgia in high-risk), chorea, erythema marginatum, subcutaneous nodules. Minors: monoarthralgia, fever ≥38°C, ESR ≥30 or CRP ≥3 mg/dL, prolonged PR interval. Treat carditis with bed rest and salicylates/NSAIDs; benzathine penicillin G secondary prophylaxis IM every 3-4 weeks for minimum 5 years, longer with carditis or residual valve disease.

outcomes.summary: Possible ARF — apply 2015 Jones criteria with population risk
outcomes.detail: Echocardiogram for all suspected ARF; start secondary prophylaxis on confirmation.

references.label: AHA Revision of the Jones Criteria for the Diagnosis of Acute Rheumatic Fever in the Era of Doppler Echocardiography 2015

title: Childhood TB — WHO 2022 diagnostic and treatment pathway
description: In children with suspected pulmonary TB use Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra on respiratory specimen (induced sputum, gastric aspirate, nasopharyngeal aspirate, or stool) as first test. Treatment-decision algorithm allowed where bacteriological confirmation not feasible. First-line regimen for non-severe drug-susceptible TB: 4 months 2HRZ(E)/2HR (shortened regimen, WHO 2022). Severe disease or HIV co-infection: full 6 months 2HRZE/4HR. Decentralised, child-friendly dispersible FDC at WHO weight bands.

outcomes.summary: Suspected paediatric TB — Xpert Ultra + treatment-decision algorithm
outcomes.detail: Do not delay treatment if bacteriological confirmation is unavailable in high-burden settings.

references.label: WHO Operational Handbook on Tuberculosis. Module 5: Management of TB in children and adolescents 2022

title: HIV-exposed infant — early infant diagnosis schedule
description: Provide ART/nevirapine prophylaxis from birth per maternal risk category. HIV DNA PCR at birth (high-risk), 4-6 weeks, 9 months, and 18 months (final antibody test). Confirm any positive PCR with a second sample before declaring infection. Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis from 6 weeks until HIV-negative status confirmed after cessation of breastfeeding. Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months with maternal ART, continue with complementary foods to ≥12 months.

outcomes.summary: HIV-exposed infant — first PCR by 4-6 weeks + cotrimoxazole
outcomes.detail: Confirm positive with second specimen; same-day ART start if confirmed.

references.label: WHO Consolidated guidelines on HIV prevention, testing, treatment, service delivery and monitoring 2021

codings.display: Contact with and (suspected) exposure to HIV

title: Early-onset neonatal sepsis — empirical antibiotics
description: For suspected early-onset (<72 h) neonatal sepsis start IV benzylpenicillin 25 mg/kg every 12 h (every 8 h after 7 days of age) plus gentamicin 5 mg/kg every 36 h initially, with levels by 24 h. For suspected late-onset sepsis cover Gram-negatives and coagulase-negative staphylococci; choice driven by local antibiogram (cefotaxime or flucloxacillin + gentamicin, or vancomycin + amikacin in NICU). Review at 36-48 h and stop if cultures negative and CRP <10 mg/L and well.

outcomes.summary: Neonatal sepsis — benzylpenicillin + gentamicin within 1 h
outcomes.detail: Do not delay for LP if unstable; ensure blood cultures before antibiotics where possible.

references.label: NICE NG195 Neonatal infection: antibiotics for prevention and treatment 2021

title: Paediatric intussusception — red flags and ultrasound pathway
description: Suspect in infants/toddlers (3 months to 3 years) with episodic inconsolable crying, drawing up of legs, vomiting (often bilious), redcurrant-jelly stool (late), or a sausage-shaped abdominal mass. First-line investigation is abdominal ultrasound showing target sign or pseudokidney. Definitive treatment: air or contrast enema reduction in stable child; surgical reduction for failed enema, peritonitis, perforation, or pathological lead point.

outcomes.summary: Suspected intussusception — urgent ultrasound and surgical referral
outcomes.detail: Do not delay imaging while awaiting redcurrant stool; resuscitate and give broad antibiotics if peritonitic.

references.label: Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline: Intussusception 2023

title: Paediatric appendicitis — Pediatric Appendicitis Score guidance
description: PAS components (1 point each, cough/hop pain and RLQ tenderness 2 points each): nausea, anorexia, fever, RLQ tenderness ×2, cough/percussion/hopping pain ×2, migration of pain, leucocytosis, neutrophilia. Score ≤3 — low risk, observation/discharge with safety-net. 4-6 — equivocal, US or surgical observation. ≥7 — high risk, surgical referral for appendicectomy. Ultrasound first-line in children to avoid CT radiation.

outcomes.summary: PAS ≥7 — surgical referral
outcomes.detail: Use US first-line; CT only if US inconclusive and high suspicion.

references.label: Samuel M. Pediatric appendicitis score. J Pediatr Surg 2002

title: Bilious vomiting in a neonate — exclude malrotation with volvulus
description: Any neonate with bilious vomiting requires urgent exclusion of malrotation with midgut volvulus — a surgical emergency. Resuscitate with isotonic crystalloid, IV broad-spectrum antibiotics, NG decompression, urgent upper GI contrast study (corkscrew duodenum, abnormal duodenojejunal flexure) and immediate paediatric surgical referral. Delay risks midgut necrosis within hours.

outcomes.summary: Bilious vomiting in neonate — surgical emergency until proven otherwise
outcomes.detail: Urgent upper GI contrast and paediatric surgical referral within 1 hour.

references.label: BAPS/BAPM Joint Statement: Bilious vomiting in the newborn 2020

title: Non-accidental injury — red flags in children
description: Consider safeguarding referral for: any unexplained bruising in a non-mobile infant; injury inconsistent with developmental stage or history; delayed presentation; multiple injuries of different ages; torn frenulum; bruising in unusual sites (ears, neck, buttocks, thighs); spiral or metaphyseal long-bone fractures in <2y; subdural haemorrhage with retinal haemorrhages; bite marks; cigarette burns or symmetrical scald patterns. Document precisely, do not photograph without consent, and refer to children's social care within agreed local timescales.

outcomes.summary: Non-accidental injury suspected — safeguard referral
outcomes.detail: Admit to safe place, do not discharge home until safeguarding assessment complete.

references.label: NICE NG76 Child abuse and neglect 2017
RCPCH Child Protection Companion 2023

title: Newborn vitamin K prophylaxis
description: Offer IM vitamin K 1 mg (0.4 mg/kg if <1.5 kg) as a single dose within 1 hour of birth to prevent vitamin K deficiency bleeding. If parents decline IM offer oral regimen: 2 mg at birth, 2 mg at 4-7 days, and 2 mg at 1 month (formula-fed infants may stop after second dose). IM has greater efficacy against late VKDB.

outcomes.summary: Newborn — offer IM vitamin K within 1 h
outcomes.detail: Document consent and route; IM is preferred to prevent late VKDB.

references.label: NICE NG194 Postnatal care 2021 — Vitamin K
AAP Policy Statement: Controversies Concerning Vitamin K and the Newborn 2003 (reaffirmed)

title: WHO iron supplementation for children in endemic settings
description: In settings where anaemia prevalence in children 6-23 months is ≥40%, provide universal iron supplementation 10-12.5 mg elemental iron daily for 3 consecutive months per year. Children 2-12 years: 30 mg daily for 3 months/year where anaemia prevalence ≥40%. Combine with malaria prevention and deworming. Co-administer with vitamin C-containing meals where feasible; avoid with milk or tea.

outcomes.summary: Endemic anaemia — universal iron supplementation 3 months/year
outcomes.detail: Combine with deworming, malaria prevention, and dietary counselling.

references.label: WHO Guideline: Daily iron supplementation in infants and children 2016

title: WHO vitamin A supplementation for children 6-59 months
description: In settings with vitamin A deficiency a public-health problem (under-5 mortality >50/1000 or clinical VAD), provide vitamin A: 100 000 IU at 6-11 months, then 200 000 IU every 4-6 months from 12-59 months. Document each dose; avoid stacking within 1 month. Also give vitamin A 200 000 IU on days 1 and 2 to children with measles, severe acute malnutrition, or persistent diarrhoea.

outcomes.summary: Endemic VAD — schedule vitamin A every 4-6 months
outcomes.detail: Treat measles, SAM, and persistent diarrhoea with therapeutic vitamin A regardless of routine schedule.

references.label: WHO Guideline: Vitamin A supplementation in infants and children 6-59 months of age 2011

title: Routine immunisation — catch-up at every visit
description: At every encounter check the child's immunisation status against the national schedule. There is no minimum interval requirement to catch up missed doses. Use any visit (acute, well-child, opportunistic) to give due vaccines unless contraindicated (anaphylaxis to a prior dose). Mild illness without fever is not a contraindication.

outcomes.summary: Check immunisation status at every visit
outcomes.detail: Use opportunistic and acute visits to catch up missed doses.

references.label: WHO Recommendations for Routine Immunization 2024
UK Green Book Immunisation against infectious disease

title: Faltering growth in infants — assessment pathway
description: Define faltering growth as a sustained fall across centile spaces (1 centile space ≥91st, 2 if 9th-91st, 3 if <9th) or weight below 2nd centile for age. Take dietary, social and developmental history; observe a feed; examine including stool/urine; first-line investigations only if indicated (FBC, ferritin, UEC, LFT, coeliac serology, urinalysis, CRP). Refer to paediatrician if persistent decline despite 4-8 weeks of community input, severe faltering at presentation, or red-flag features (dysmorphism, recurrent infections, organomegaly, neurological signs).

outcomes.summary: Faltering growth — structured feed observation and dietetic input
outcomes.detail: Do not initiate routine investigations without clinical indication.

references.label: NICE NG75 Faltering growth: recognition and management of faltering growth in children 2017

title: Paediatric anaphylaxis — IM adrenaline dose by weight band
description: IM adrenaline 1:1000 anterolateral mid-thigh: <6 months 100-150 mcg (0.1-0.15 mL); 6 months-6 years 150 mcg; 6-12 years 300 mcg; >12 years 500 mcg. Repeat every 5 minutes if needed. Lay flat with legs elevated (or left-lateral in pregnancy); high-flow oxygen; IV fluid bolus 10 mL/kg if hypotensive; refractory anaphylaxis requires adrenaline infusion 0.1-1 mcg/kg/min in HDU.

outcomes.summary: Paediatric anaphylaxis — IM adrenaline by weight band
outcomes.detail: Do not delay for IV; IM into mid-thigh; repeat every 5 minutes if no improvement.

references.label: Resuscitation Council UK Emergency Treatment of Anaphylaxis 2021

title: Paediatric severe asthma — IV magnesium sulphate
description: If severe acute asthma not responding to first-line nebulised therapy (back-to-back salbutamol + ipratropium) consider IV magnesium sulphate 40 mg/kg (maximum 2 g) over 20 minutes. Monitor BP — magnesium can cause hypotension. Escalate to IV salbutamol load 15 mcg/kg over 10 min then infusion 1-5 mcg/kg/min, or IV aminophylline load 5 mg/kg over 20 min (omit if on oral theophylline) then 1 mg/kg/h, in HDU/PICU.

outcomes.summary: Refractory severe asthma — IV magnesium 40 mg/kg over 20 min
outcomes.detail: Monitor BP, electrolytes; escalate to PICU if no improvement.

references.label: BTS/SIGN/NICE Asthma joint guideline 2024

title: Paediatric pneumonia — WHO classification and amoxicillin first-line
description: Classify per WHO Pocket Book: fast breathing pneumonia (RR ≥50/min 2-12 mo, ≥40/min 12-59 mo, ≥30/min ≥5 y) → oral amoxicillin 40-50 mg/kg/dose BD for 5 days. Chest indrawing pneumonia in under-5 also treated as outpatient amoxicillin in revised 2014 WHO guidance if no danger signs. Severe pneumonia with general danger sign (unable to drink, vomits everything, convulsions, lethargy, central cyanosis, severe respiratory distress) → admit + IV ampicillin/penicillin + gentamicin, plus oxygen for SpO2 <90%.

outcomes.summary: Paediatric pneumonia — amoxicillin 5 days oral if no danger sign
outcomes.detail: Admit only if danger sign or SpO2 <90%; oxygen for hypoxaemia.

references.label: WHO Revised classification and treatment of childhood pneumonia at health facilities 2014

title: Paediatric acute gastroenteritis — low-osmolarity ORS plus zinc
description: Manage acute diarrhoea in children with low-osmolarity ORS (75 mmol/L sodium, 75 mmol/L glucose, 245 mOsm/L). Give zinc 10 mg/day (<6 months) or 20 mg/day (≥6 months) for 10-14 days — reduces duration and severity. Continue breastfeeding; reintroduce age-appropriate diet within 4-6 hours. IV rehydration only when severe dehydration or oral route fails. Avoid antimotility agents; antibiotics only for cholera, dysentery, or proven invasive bacterial disease.

outcomes.summary: Paediatric diarrhoea — ORS + zinc 10-14 days
outcomes.detail: Avoid antimotility agents; continue feeding; reassess hydration after 4 h.

references.label: WHO/UNICEF Joint Statement: Clinical management of acute diarrhoea 2004 (reaffirmed)

title: Simple febrile seizure — discharge criteria and parental advice
description: Simple febrile seizure: generalised tonic-clonic, <15 minutes, no recurrence in 24 h, full neurological recovery, age 6 months-5 years. No routine investigations (no EEG, no neuroimaging, no LP unless meningitis suspected). Discharge with safety-net advice and antipyretic guidance (paracetamol/ibuprofen for symptomatic comfort only — they do not prevent recurrence). Complex (focal, >15 min, recurrence within 24 h, post-ictal focal deficit) — admit, paediatric review, consider LP/imaging/EEG.

outcomes.summary: Simple febrile seizure — no routine investigation, discharge with advice
outcomes.detail: Antipyretics do not prevent recurrence; safety-net for prolonged or focal events.

outcomes.summary: Complex febrile seizure — admit for paediatric review
outcomes.detail: Investigate per local protocol; lumbar puncture if meningitis suspected.

references.label: NICE CKS Febrile seizure 2023
AAP Clinical Practice Guideline: Febrile Seizures 2008

title: Paediatric meningococcal disease — recognition and IM/IV benzylpenicillin
description: Suspect meningococcal disease in any child with fever plus non-blanching rash (petechiae or purpura), neck stiffness, photophobia, altered mental status, leg pain, cold peripheries, or abnormal skin colour. Give IM/IV benzylpenicillin BEFORE transfer if delay to hospital expected: <1 y 300 mg, 1-9 y 600 mg, ≥10 y 1.2 g. In hospital give ceftriaxone 80-100 mg/kg/day (max 4 g). Notify public health; chemoprophylaxis (ciprofloxacin) to close contacts.

outcomes.summary: Suspected meningococcal disease — benzylpenicillin before transfer
outcomes.detail: Do not delay for confirmatory tests; notify public health.

references.label: NICE NG240 Meningitis (bacterial) and meningococcal disease: recognition, diagnosis and management 2024

title: Paediatric head injury — NICE CT head criteria
description: CT head within 1 hour for under-16s with any of: GCS <14 in ED (or <15 in infants <1 y), GCS <15 at 2 h post-injury, suspected open/depressed skull fracture, tense fontanelle, signs of basal skull fracture, focal neurology, post-traumatic seizure with no prior epilepsy, ≥1 episode vomiting, age <1 y with bruise/swelling/laceration >5 cm. Loss of consciousness >5 min, abnormal drowsiness, ≥3 vomits, dangerous mechanism, amnesia >5 min — observe 4 h and CT if any develop.

outcomes.summary: High-risk paediatric head injury — CT within 1 hour
outcomes.detail: Apply NICE criteria; admit if any indication.

references.label: NICE NG232 Head injury: assessment and early management 2023

title: Paediatric maintenance fluids — isotonic
description: Use isotonic crystalloid (0.9% saline or balanced solution) with or without 5% glucose for routine paediatric maintenance fluids — do NOT use hypotonic fluids (risk of hyponatraemia). Calculate maintenance by Holliday-Segar: 100 mL/kg/day for first 10 kg, 50 mL/kg/day for next 10 kg, 20 mL/kg/day thereafter. Add glucose for fasted/neonates. Monitor sodium every 24 h; review prescription daily.

outcomes.summary: Paediatric maintenance — isotonic only, check sodium daily
outcomes.detail: Avoid 0.18% or 0.45% saline for maintenance; review prescription each shift.

references.label: NICE NG29 IV fluids in children 2015

title: Paediatric shock fluid bolus — 10-20 mL/kg with reassessment
description: For paediatric septic shock without features of fluid overload give isotonic crystalloid bolus 10-20 mL/kg over 30-60 minutes (faster in shock with profound hypotension). Reassess after each bolus for response and signs of overload (hepatomegaly, rales, gallop). In resource-limited settings without ventilatory support apply the FEAST-aware approach — slower, smaller boluses (10 mL/kg) and early vasopressors. Do NOT routinely give >40 mL/kg before starting vasopressors.

outcomes.summary: Paediatric shock — 10-20 mL/kg with reassessment
outcomes.detail: Stop and start vasopressor if signs of overload appear; in resource-limited setting use smaller boluses.

references.label: Maitland K et al. Mortality after fluid bolus in African children with severe infection (FEAST). NEJM 2011
Surviving Sepsis Campaign Children 2020

title: Paediatric burns — modified Parkland resuscitation
description: Calculate burn TBSA using Lund-Browder chart (age-corrected). For burns ≥10% TBSA in children give Parkland formula: 3-4 mL Ringer's lactate × kg × % TBSA over 24 h, half in first 8 h from time of burn. Add maintenance fluid (Holliday-Segar) for children. Titrate to urine output 1 mL/kg/h. Refer >10% TBSA, full-thickness, face/hands/perineum, electrical, chemical, or inhalational to burn centre.

outcomes.summary: Paediatric burn ≥10% TBSA — Parkland + burn centre referral
outcomes.detail: Add maintenance fluid in children; titrate to UO 1 mL/kg/h.

references.label: ABA Advanced Burn Life Support 2018
British Burn Association referral criteria

codings.display: Burns classified according to extent of body surface

title: Paediatric anaemia — staged investigation
description: Confirm anaemia using age- and altitude-adjusted Hb cut-offs (WHO: 6 mo-5 y <11 g/dL, 5-11 y <11.5 g/dL, 12-14 y <12 g/dL). Step 1 — FBC + film + reticulocytes + ferritin. Microcytic with low ferritin → iron deficiency, trial oral iron 3-6 mg/kg/day elemental, recheck at 4 weeks. Microcytic with normal/high ferritin → consider thalassaemia, haemoglobin electrophoresis. Macrocytic → B12, folate. Normocytic with reticulocytosis → haemolysis (DAT, G6PD, haemoglobinopathy). Refer when no response to iron, suspected haemoglobinopathy, marrow disease, or severe (Hb <7 g/dL).

outcomes.summary: Paediatric anaemia — staged workup, treat empirically only IDA
outcomes.detail: Do not transfuse asymptomatic Hb >6 g/dL without workup outside malaria/sickle context.

references.label: WHO Haemoglobin concentrations for the diagnosis of anaemia and assessment of severity 2011

title: Sickle cell — acute chest syndrome bundle
description: Suspect acute chest syndrome (ACS) in any sickle patient with new pulmonary infiltrate on CXR plus respiratory symptoms, fever, hypoxia, or chest pain. Bundle: oxygen for SpO2 <94%, IV fluids at maintenance (avoid overhydration), broad-spectrum antibiotics covering atypicals (ceftriaxone + macrolide), incentive spirometry, adequate analgesia (avoid sedation that suppresses respiration), bronchodilators if wheeze, urgent simple or exchange transfusion if hypoxia worsens (target HbS <30%), HDU/PICU referral.

outcomes.summary: Sickle cell ACS — antibiotics, oxygen, exchange if hypoxic
outcomes.detail: Top-up or exchange transfusion early if SpO2 falls; PICU referral.

references.label: BSH Guideline on the Management of Acute Chest Syndrome in Sickle Cell Disease 2015

codings.display: Hb-SS disease with acute chest syndrome

title: Severe paediatric malaria — IV artesunate first-line
description: For severe P. falciparum malaria in children give IV artesunate 3 mg/kg if <20 kg, 2.4 mg/kg if ≥20 kg, at 0, 12 and 24 h then daily for minimum 24 h IV, then switch to full course of oral artemisinin combination therapy (artemether-lumefantrine, dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine). Monitor for post-artesunate delayed haemolysis at 7-14 days (FBC and haemolysis screen). Quinine only if artesunate unavailable.

outcomes.summary: Severe paediatric malaria — IV artesunate, weight-banded
outcomes.detail: Switch to oral ACT after minimum 24 h IV; screen for post-artesunate delayed haemolysis at 7-14 d.

references.label: WHO Guidelines for the treatment of malaria 2023

codings.display: Plasmodium falciparum malaria with cerebral complications

title: Paediatric snake envenoming — anti-snake venom by syndrome
description: Diagnose envenoming clinically by syndrome (neurotoxic, haemotoxic with 20-min whole-blood clotting test, cytotoxic). Children receive the SAME total dose of polyvalent anti-snake venom as adults — dose is based on the amount of venom injected, not body weight. Initial dose typically 10 vials reconstituted in 100-200 mL isotonic fluid IV over 1 hour. Pre-treat with adrenaline subcutaneously per WHO/SE Asia regional approach if available. Repeat after 1-2 h if syndrome unresolved.

outcomes.summary: Paediatric envenoming — ASV at adult dose, by syndrome
outcomes.detail: Children receive the same total ASV dose as adults; manage anaphylaxis with IM adrenaline.

references.label: WHO Guidelines for the management of snakebites SE Asia 2016

title: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia — preterm follow-up
description: Diagnose BPD when an infant born <32 weeks requires supplemental oxygen at 36 weeks postmenstrual age. Discharge bundle: home oxygen if SpO2 <90% in air, palivizumab for RSV prophylaxis in eligible cohort, immunisations on chronological schedule (no correction for prematurity), pulse oximetry monitoring, sleep position counselling, growth and neurodevelopmental follow-up to 2 years corrected age minimum.

outcomes.summary: BPD — structured follow-up bundle
outcomes.detail: Palivizumab if eligible; immunise on chronological age; neurodevelopmental follow-up to 2 y corrected.

references.label: AAP Policy Statement: Updated Guidance for Palivizumab Prophylaxis 2023
NICE NG124 Specialist neonatal respiratory care

codings.display: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia originating in the perinatal period

title: Paediatric obstructive sleep apnoea — adenotonsillectomy referral
description: Refer for adenotonsillectomy when habitual snoring plus any of: witnessed apnoea, restless sleep, daytime behavioural problems, failure to thrive, hypertension, polycythaemia, or polysomnography AHI >5/h. Polysomnography preferred when high-risk (obesity, craniofacial anomaly, Down syndrome, neuromuscular). Post-operative monitoring for severe OSA (AHI >10), young age (<3 y), or comorbidity.

outcomes.summary: Paediatric OSA — refer ENT for adenotonsillectomy
outcomes.detail: PSG for high-risk groups; admit post-op for severe OSA or comorbidity.

references.label: AAP Clinical Practice Guideline: Diagnosis and Management of Childhood Obstructive Sleep Apnea Syndrome 2012

title: Paediatric acute otitis media — selective antibiotic strategy
description: Most cases resolve without antibiotics. Use observation 48-72 h with safety-net for >2 years with unilateral non-severe AOM. Treat immediately with amoxicillin 80-90 mg/kg/day divided BD for: <6 months, bilateral AOM in <2 years, otorrhoea, severe symptoms (severe pain, fever ≥39°C), or immunocompromise. Duration: <2 y or severe — 10 days; ≥2 y non-severe — 5-7 days. Use amoxicillin-clavulanate if failure at 48-72 h or recent amoxicillin.

outcomes.summary: AOM — observe vs immediate amoxicillin based on age/severity
outcomes.detail: Most cases resolve spontaneously; antibiotics indicated for under-2, severe symptoms, or otorrhoea.

references.label: AAP Clinical Practice Guideline: Diagnosis and Management of Acute Otitis Media 2013

title: Paediatric pharyngitis — McIsaac score and selective testing
description: McIsaac score (age 3-14 +1, 15-44 0, ≥45 -1; fever, no cough, tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical nodes) guides streptococcal pharyngitis management in 3-14 y. Score ≤1 — no testing, no antibiotic. 2-3 — RADT/culture, treat if positive. ≥4 — RADT/culture, treat positive. Treatment: penicillin V 250 mg BD (<27 kg) or 500 mg BD (≥27 kg) for 10 days, or amoxicillin 50 mg/kg/day for 10 days. Withhold antibiotics if test negative.

outcomes.summary: Paediatric sore throat — McIsaac-guided testing
outcomes.detail: Avoid empirical antibiotics; confirm streptococcal infection first.

references.label: IDSA Clinical Practice Guideline for Group A Streptococcal Pharyngitis 2012

title: Adolescent consent — Gillick competence and confidentiality
description: For under-16s assess Gillick competence: ability to understand the nature, purpose, benefits and risks of the proposed intervention and to retain that information to make an informed decision. Where Gillick competent the adolescent may consent without parental knowledge for contraception, sexual health, mental health, and substance misuse care. Breach confidentiality only with consent or where there is risk of serious harm to the adolescent or others — document the reasoning. Apply Fraser guidelines specifically for contraception.

outcomes.summary: Under-16 — assess Gillick competence and document
outcomes.detail: Encourage parental involvement; breach confidentiality only with serious-harm justification.

references.label: GMC 0-18 years: guidance for all doctors 2018
Gillick v West Norfolk and Wisbech AHA [1986] AC 112

title: Paediatric developmental red flags by age
description: Refer for specialist developmental assessment when any milestone red flag is present: no smile by 8 weeks; no fixing/following by 3 months; not sitting unsupported by 12 months; not walking by 18 months; no clear words by 18 months; no 2-word phrases by 2 years; loss of any skill at any age; persistent toe-walking >3 years; squint at any age. Ensure hearing test, vision check, growth plot, family history, and rule out neglect.

outcomes.summary: Developmental red flag — refer for specialist assessment
outcomes.detail: Loss of skill at any age requires urgent neurodevelopmental review.

references.label: RCPCH Developmental Surveillance Workstream

title: Paediatric functional constipation — disimpaction and maintenance
description: Diagnose by Rome IV criteria. Step 1 disimpaction with macrogol (polyethylene glycol) — escalating dose for 7 days. Step 2 maintenance with macrogol at half the disimpaction dose, titrating to a soft daily stool, continued for at least several months and weaned slowly. Add stimulant (senna or sodium picosulfate) if response inadequate. Behavioural advice: regular toilet sitting after meals, foot support, reward chart, fluid and dietary advice (do not restrict diet).

outcomes.summary: Paediatric constipation — disimpact then maintain with macrogol
outcomes.detail: Maintenance for months not weeks; do not stop at first regular stool.

references.label: NICE CG99 Constipation in children and young people 2010 (updated 2017)

title: Newborn bloodspot screening — timing and conditions
description: Offer newborn bloodspot screening between day 5 and day 8 of life (ideally day 5). UK panel screens for sickle cell disease, cystic fibrosis, congenital hypothyroidism, and inherited metabolic diseases (PKU, MCADD, MSUD, IVA, GA1, HCU). Pre-term infants <32 weeks need a second sample at 28 days or discharge. Document parental consent in record. Provide written information ahead of sampling.

outcomes.summary: Bloodspot screening at day 5-8 — document consent
outcomes.detail: Second sample for preterm <32 weeks at 28 days or discharge.

references.label: UK NHS Newborn Blood Spot Screening Programme Handbook 2024

codings.display: Encounter for screening for nutritional disorder

title: Henoch-Schönlein purpura (IgA vasculitis) — monitoring for renal involvement
description: IgA vasculitis presents with palpable purpura (lower limbs/buttocks), arthralgia, abdominal pain, and renal involvement. Confirm clinical features; investigate for nephritis with urinalysis (haematuria, proteinuria) and BP weekly for first month, fortnightly to 3 months, monthly to 6 months, then 6 monthly to 12 months. Refer to paediatric nephrology if hypertension, persistent proteinuria, raised creatinine, or nephrotic-range proteinuria. Most cases self-limit; analgesia and supportive care; consider steroids for severe abdominal pain or scrotal involvement.

outcomes.summary: HSP — 12 months of urinalysis and BP follow-up
outcomes.detail: Renal involvement may appear weeks to months after presentation.

references.label: RCPCH HSP nephritis follow-up guideline 2019

title: Vaccine administration — anaphylaxis history check
description: Before each vaccine confirm there is no history of confirmed anaphylaxis to a previous dose of the same vaccine, or to a vaccine constituent. Egg allergy is NOT a contraindication to MMR or to most influenza vaccines (use LAIV or egg-free if severe). Latex allergy may contraindicate vaccines in latex-stoppered vials. Always have adrenaline IM available; observe 15 minutes after vaccination.

outcomes.summary: Check vaccine constituent allergy before each dose
outcomes.detail: Egg allergy not a contraindication to MMR; have adrenaline available.

references.label: UK Green Book Immunisation against infectious disease — Contraindications and special considerations

codings.display: Allergy status to serum and vaccine

title: Paediatric acute scrotum — exclude testicular torsion
description: Sudden-onset severe testicular pain in a boy is testicular torsion until proven otherwise. Do NOT delay surgical exploration for imaging if clinical suspicion high. The testicular salvage rate falls below 50% after 6 hours. If Doppler ultrasound available without delay it may support diagnosis (absent intratesticular flow) but a negative scan does not rule out torsion. Manual detorsion (open-the-book) buys time while preparing theatre.

outcomes.summary: Suspected testicular torsion — theatre without delay
outcomes.detail: Salvage falls below 50% after 6 h; do not delay surgical exploration for imaging.

references.label: EAU Paediatric Urology Guidelines 2024

title: Paediatric familial hypercholesterolaemia — universal/cascade screening
description: Consider universal lipid screen once between ages 9 and 11, with cascade testing of first-degree relatives if a parent has known FH. Refer if LDL ≥4.0 mmol/L (or ≥3.5 with FH in family) for specialist lipid clinic. Treatment with statin from age 8-10 in confirmed heterozygous FH, with healthy lifestyle and family-wide counselling. Refer all suspected homozygous FH urgently to specialist centre.

outcomes.summary: Suspected paediatric FH — refer to specialist lipid clinic
outcomes.detail: Statin from age 8-10 in heterozygous FH; urgent referral for homozygous FH.

references.label: NICE CG71 Familial hypercholesterolaemia 2008 (updated 2019)

title: Paediatric acute limp — Kocher criteria and septic arthritis exclusion
description: For a child with hip pain and limp apply Kocher criteria: fever >38.5°C, non-weight-bearing, ESR >40 mm/h, WBC >12 × 10⁹/L. 0 criteria <0.2% septic arthritis; 1 criterion 3%; 2 — 40%; 3 — 93%; 4 — 99%. Hip ultrasound for effusion; aspirate joint if any suspicion of septic arthritis. Other diagnoses by age: transient synovitis (4-10 y), Perthes (4-8 y), SUFE (10-15 y), DDH (infant), trauma, malignancy, JIA.

outcomes.summary: ≥2 Kocher criteria — joint aspiration
outcomes.detail: Septic arthritis is a surgical emergency; aspirate before antibiotics where possible.
